And if I was right, there was a way to grow stronger even without choosing a sponsor now.
A way to perhaps become even stronger than incarnations with the most powerful sponsors.
[Haha, well now······ Someone has made an interesting choice, haven't they? Well, all right. There will be other opportunities.]
The dokkaebi's eyes, curved like crescent moons, rested on me for a moment.
[Now, now, you should all have finished choosing, so take a little rest here. I need to go prepare the next scenario. See you in 10 minutes!]
After <Sponsor Selection> ended, the dokkaebi left us with that crap and disappeared.
It had told us to rest, but these 10 minutes were crucial.
Within 10 minutes, we had to sort all of this out and prepare for the next scenario.
I mentally went over the abilities I possessed.
[Character List], and [Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint].
I still didn't know exactly how to use them, but I had a rough idea of what kind of skills they were. With these, I could manage somehow.
“Everyone, please gather here.”
At my words, the survivors, who had been standing around watching one another uncertainly, gathered hesitantly. Lee Hyunsung was the first to extend a hand.
“Hello. I'm Lee Hyunsung.”
“I'm Kim Dokja.”
“I'm not sure ‘nice to meet you’··· is appropriate in this situation, but it's nice to meet you. As I mentioned, I'm a soldier······ though I suppose I should now say I was a soldier.”
“You can't get in touch with your unit?”
His grip was remarkably strong as we shook hands. Just what you'd expect from the tank in the early stages of ‘Ways of Survival,’ I supposed.
I had to take Lee Hyunsung with me.
He might not seem like much now, but Lee Hyunsung became increasingly important in the later parts of Ways of Survival.
“Oh, and Dokja-ssi.”
“Yes?”
“Thank you for earlier. If it hadn't been for you, we would all have died.”
“No, that's—”
“Or even if we'd survived, we couldn't have lived as human beings. Thank you so much. And······ I'm ashamed.”
Lee Hyunsung, bowing deeply at the waist.
I felt a little conflicted.
The truth was, Lee Hyunsung would have survived even if I hadn't done anything.
Someone grabbed my shoulder.
“Haha, our contract worker's done something big. Dokja-ssi, you know my name, don't you?”
I knew who it was without turning around. I removed the hand from my shoulder and said,
“I do, Han Myungoh-ssi.”
“Now, now, Han Myungoh-ssi? You should call me Department Head-nim, shouldn't you?”
Insisting on his rank even in this situation. Typical Han Myungoh.
Mino Soft's biggest old blowhard, and the final boss of authoritarianism.
“This isn't the office.”
“Ha, would you look at this. Planning to stop coming to work? Where did you learn such bad manners?”
Strangely, the sight of Han Myungoh snarling brought home once again that the world I had known was over.
Before the scenario began, the man before me had been a ‘predator’ in this world.
And I had been nothing more than prey before that predator. That was certainly how it had been.
“And no matter how I look at it, you went too far earlier. Huh? If you had bugs or something, you should at least have tipped me off. How could you throw them around so carelessly?”
“Kim Dokja-ssi, you'd better treat me well. Your contract's almost up, isn't it?”
Suddenly, it was funny.
So the world I'd lived in had been this fragile.
“Han Myungoh-ssi.”
“Huh?”
“Please shut up.”
“Wh-what?”

“Do you still not understand what's happening? Did that little shit need to beat you up earlier for you to come to your senses? Mino Soft? After all this, do you think a company like that still exists?”
Han Myungoh went pale, his mouth opening and closing.
I turned my gaze to the others. Now that I'd brought it up, I needed to make things clear.
“Han Myungoh-ssi isn't the only problem. Everyone, get a grip. As the dokkaebi said, this isn't a joke.”

“Even if you haven't said anything, I trust you've all worked out roughly what's happening. An Attributes Window, exclusive skills. An interface like a game's. Is there anyone who still doesn't get it?”
As expected, nobody raised a hand. This was what made Korea convenient. With smartphones so widespread, there was nobody who had never played an RPG.
Even if they hadn't played a phone game, they would at least have read a fantasy novel.
Lee Hyunsung sighed.
“This sort of thing only happened in the novels I read secretly while on duty. It still doesn't feel real. This really isn't a dream, is it?”
“Of course it's real.”
The look in Lee Hyunsung's eyes changed slightly at my composed reply.
[The character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ feels a faint sense of trust in you.]
[Your understanding of the character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ has increased.]
Lee Hyunsung nodded.
“I'm glad you're certain. Then what should we do now? Do you have any ideas, Dokja-ssi?”
“We need to get out of here.”
I spoke without the slightest hesitation.
“G-get out? Are you out of your mind?”
“Dokja-ssi, I also think that's a bit······.”
This time, even Yoo Sangah joined in.
They still hadn't come to their senses.
“Then how long do you plan to stay here?”
In fact, from a rational perspective, there was something unreasonable about what I was proposing. Outside was a paradise for monsters.
But I knew. We had to go outside now.
“Aren't you thinking about your parents? With all this happening, do you think they're safe?”
“Oh, actually, the phone hasn't been working for a while now. KakaoTalk isn't working either······.”
Yoo Sangah looked close to tears.
Just what you'd expect from Korea, where Confucianism still held strong. Everyone's face darkened at the single word ‘parents,’ even Lee Hyunsung's and Han Myungoh's.
I firmly squeezed the shoulder of Lee Gilyoung, who had his head bowed. Yoo Sangah was the first to rise.
“Let's go. We need to get out.”
“N-no! Didn't you hear what that bastard said? It told us to rest here! Our heads will burst if we go wandering around!”
“Let's take a majority vote.”
Yoo Sangah raised her hand first, followed by me and Lee Gilyoung. And that was all.
“······I do need to get back to my unit, but I think moving around carelessly in this situation would be dangerous. We were warned earlier, too.”
“Fuck, go out by yourselves! I'm not going! I said I'm not going!”
Han Myungoh was useless anyway, so he didn't matter. The problem was Lee Hyunsung. I had to bring him along somehow······.
Booom!
The thick steel plate buckled with a deafening crash. The steel door leading to carriage 3707 was slowly crumpling.
“Wh-what is that?”
Regardless of Han Myungoh's shouting, the steel door rang out with another crash.
Booom!
Someone on the other side was trying to break down the steel door. This was unexpected, and my thoughts raced.
Could this be the next scenario?
No. The dokkaebi wasn't back yet.
My mind worked quickly.
The fine hairs on my skin stood up, and a brief shudder ran through my entire body.
It was him.
“Wh-what are you doing? Everyone, block the door!”
Han Myungoh shouted as he backed away from the door. I stopped Lee Hyunsung from approaching it.
“You won't be able to stop him.”
“Pardon?”
“We need to get out of here right now.”
I spoke as I stared grimly at the steel door.
“What? But—”
“If we don't leave now―”
The sole survivor of carriage 3707. The identity of the person beyond that door was all too obvious.
“We'll all die before the next scenario even arrives.”
Yes. He was finally coming.
The ‘real’ protagonist of this story.
I looked straight into the eyes of the hesitant Lee Hyunsung and Han Myungoh and said,
“Die here at the hands of the guy beyond that steel door, or get out of the train and try your luck. Which will you choose?”
“Dokja-ssi, there's no guarantee that whoever's beyond that steel door is an enemy, is there?”
The Steel Sword Emperor faltered at crucial moments. There was a reason Lee Hyunsung couldn't be the party leader.
“If they're coming from another carriage, they're likely a survivor. We could at least meet them······.”
Instead of answering, I surveyed the blood-soaked carriage. Lee Hyunsung followed my gaze and quietly closed his mouth.
“······I spoke thoughtlessly. Let's find a way out.”
“L-let's go! Let's get out, quickly!”
In that instant, the two of them had realized it, too.
That the survivors in the other carriages must have been through the same thing we had.
And that they wouldn't have been lucky enough to have ‘insects.’
“This one's broken!”
“Damn it, this one won't turn, either!”
Listening to Lee Hyunsung's and Han Myungoh's shouts, I checked a door mechanism myself. I could now touch the mechanism that had been sealed behind a barrier earlier.
Excluding the doors connecting the carriages, a subway carriage had 8 entry doors in total. And 3 exits remained unchecked.
Boom!
The steel door looked unlikely to last even another minute.
Protagonist or not, his Strength level couldn't be high enough at this early stage. Frankly, it was astonishing that he would even think of breaking down that thick steel door.
“Dokja-ssi! Here―”
We had found a working manual door mechanism.
“I'm opening it!”
But although the mechanism turned smoothly, the door didn't open all the way. About a fifth of the way open, it stopped as though caught on something.
“······This one seems to be broken, too.”
“What about the others?”
“This is the only one we have any chance of getting through.”
A child might manage it, but the gap was too narrow for an adult man or woman. Han Myungoh and Lee Hyunsung each grabbed one side of the door and strained with all their might, but it didn't budge.
[Coins held: 4700 C]
One use for coins was raising overall stats.
I'd already spent 2700 coins bringing my Constitution level to 10.
If I used the remaining coins to raise my Strength level, I could somehow solve this, but with no way of knowing what might happen or when, I couldn't spend coins recklessly at this early stage.
In the end, there was only one approach I could count on.
“Lee Hyunsung-ssi. Use your skill.”
“Pardon? By skill, you mean······.”
I quietly activated [Character List].

Hissss!

Gyaaaaaah!

Graaaaaah······.
Humans weren't the only ones struggling in this new world.

The sign for Exit 3, visible in the distance.
······Closed.

Soon, a faint thread connected Gong Pildu and me, and system messages began to sound.
[The contract has been concluded.]
[Under the contract, you have become the ‘joint backer’ of incarnation ‘Gong Pildu’.]
[Under the contract, you have acquired command rights over incarnation ‘Gong Pildu.’]
[The term of this contract is 5 years. It will be extended automatically if it is not renewed.]

To acquire the Armed Fortress Master, Gong Pildu, this easily—Yoo Joonghyuk would faint if he knew. If I hadn't read into the later part of the original novel, I wouldn't have known that a <Behind the Scenes Contract> could be used this way either.
I handed the recovery potions to Yoo Sangah.
“Please give these to Gong Pildu. One about every 40 minutes should do.”
“···Will it be all right to give them to him?”
We had to. Without them, he wouldn't be able to clear the main scenario. After receiving a potion from Yoo Sangah, Gong Pildu looked our way.
“What's this?”
“Drink it and fight.”
After a moment of suspicion, Gong Pildu uncapped the potion. Blue smoke rose from his body, and the deteriorating turrets regained their original form.
[The magic power of character ‘Gong Pildu’ has been fully restored.]
Gong Pildu wiped the potion from his lips and looked up at me.
“Idiot. Do you think doing this will make me forgive you? The day I get out of here will be the day you die······.”
“Shut your mouth, Gong Pildu.”
[‘Command rights’ activate under the terms of the contract!]
“Mmph, mmph mmph? Mmph mmph mmph mmph?”
Poor bastard. He didn't even know what position he was in.
“Now fight hard. And leave my companions alone.”
“Mmph! Mmmph mmph······!”
Ratatatatat!
Yoo Sangah's eyes widened as she watched Gong Pildu obediently follow my instructions.
“D-Dokja-ssi? Why is he suddenly acting like that······?”
“I simply turned ‘Party A’ into ‘Party B.’”
“···Did you pull some kind of trick?”
“You don't need to worry about Gong Pildu anymore.”
That was when a barrage of constellation messages poured in.
[The constellation, ‘Secretive Plotter,’ finds your idea amusing.]
[The constellation, ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband,’ drops the Ruyi Jingu Bang in response to your strategy.]
[The constellation, ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon,’ thinks you are insolent.]
I'd negotiated the contract fairly discreetly, but some of them had already caught on. Defense Master was only intermediate in rank, but was still a constellation.

A mere human like me had become a ‘joint backer’ with an actual ‘constellation,’ so the shock to the constellations would be tremendous. Some would probably object, like the ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon.’ But.
[A considerable number of constellations are paying attention to you.]
[A considerable number of constellations wish to become your constellation sponsor.]
Far more constellations had realized my value. That was only natural: if they could become my sponsor, they would be able to use the combat power of ‘Defense Master’ too.
That was when the dokkaebi Biryu, owner of the channel Gong Pildu was in, appeared in midair.
[Constellations-nim! Wh-why······ Why are you all leaving so suddenly! D-don't go! If you just wait a little longer······!]
With his channel suddenly on the verge of collapse, Biryu was pleading into the air. The damned dokkaebi bastard who'd imposed the ‘survival fee’ and ‘food penalty’ at Geumho Station.
[E-eeeeeek! N-noooo······.]
The dokkaebi Biryu's form slowly grew indistinct.
[Channel # BIR-3642 has been forcibly shut down due to a decrease in subscribing constellations.]
Watching a channel collapse so helplessly, Bihyung spoke in a trembling voice.
[Um······ Dokja-nim?]
‘What?’
[You······ Don't tell me you were after Gong Pildu from the beginning?]
I merely shrugged.
[Holy shit······ How could a human······ What the hell did I make a contract with?]
Bihyung couldn't close his gaping mouth.
Whatever.
Well, things here were settled. Time to move on to the next place.
I spoke to my companions, who were still bewildered and hadn't grasped what had happened.
“Everyone. I'm sorry, but I think I'll have to step away for a while.”
“What? Now?”

“There's somewhere I urgently need to go. Hyunsung-ssi and Yoo Sangah-ssi, please stay here. There's nothing much you need to do. Just rest and toss that Pildu guy a potion now and then until the scenario ends.”
Jung Heewon asked,
“What about Gilyoung and me?”
“Come with me.”
“Where?”
“Hmm······ It's hard to explain properly, but there's a bad guy.”
“A bad guy?”
“Yes. A bad guy who disappeared to hog all the damn items for himself, whether people died or not. We're going to smack him in the back of the head.”
Very hard, at that. After thinking for a moment, Jung Heewon asked,
“···Is he worse than Gong Pildu?”
I thought for a moment, then said,
“Much worse.”
“Let's go, then.”
“I'll explain the details on the way.”
I set off with a delighted Jung Heewon and Lee Gilyoung. But someone grabbed my shoulder. It was Lee Jihye.
“Wait, ajusshi. Where are you going?”
She really did have good instincts.
“Good timing. You come too.”
“Where?”
“Yoo Joonghyuk is in danger.”
Lee Jihye gave a little laugh, apparently thinking I was joking.
“What kind of bullshit is that? Master's in danger?”
When my expression remained serious, the amusement soon faded from Lee Jihye's face too.
“···Seriously? Wait, how do you know that, ajusshi?”
How did I know? I was probably the world's number one—no, number two (第二)—authority on your master.
I checked the time and said,
“That bastard entered the hidden dungeon at Exit 1, right?”
“H-huh?”
“And it's now been 11 hours since he went in?”
Lee Jihye sounded dumbfounded.

As I remembered it, Yoo Joonghyuk had attempted Chungmuro's ‘hidden dungeon’ a total of eight times. Of those, he'd failed twice and succeeded six times. The problem was that both failures had occurred in his early rounds. The 8th and 11th rounds.
And the Yoo Joonghyuk of the 8th round had died in Chungmuro's ‘hidden dungeon.’
“If we leave him like this, Yoo Joonghyuk will die today.”
If my prediction was right, our damned regressor would be well on his way down the ‘sunfish route’ by now.
Omniscient Sunfish

A little later, we were heading toward the entrance to the ‘hidden dungeon’ on basement level 1. With Lee Jihye and Jung Heewon in front, I walked at the rear of the group with Lee Gilyoung, looking at my smartphone.
「······Amid pain that felt as though his head would split open, Yoo Joonghyuk’s mind gave way.
‘I give up on this life.’
That was Yoo Joonghyuk’s eighth life.」
Surely not.
It couldn’t have come to that yet.

······Damn it, why was a bastard only on his third round getting so carried away? If he’d acted cautiously like he had in his second round, he could have muddled through to the middle and later scenarios just fine.
When I looked up, Jung Heewon was watching me.
“Dokja-ssi, what are you looking at so intently?”
“···Oh, just the calendar······. With everything like this, I’ve lost track of the date.”
Looking at an actual calendar would probably be more entertaining. Sometimes I wondered how I’d managed to read this entire novel. Jung Heewon eyed me suspiciously, then turned toward Lee Jihye.
“By the way······ Jihye, was it? Are you any good with a sword, too?”
“Yes. I like swords.”
“Right? Swords really are the best. There’s something satisfying about cutting things, you know?”
“···So you know that feeling too, unnie?”
Jung Heewon smiled, then quietly studied Lee Jihye’s longsword. Its rich sheen made it obvious at a glance that it was a fine blade. Yoo Joonghyuk had probably given it to her.
“Your sword looks nice.”
“Oh, my master gave it to me. What about yours, unnie······?”
“Mine······ M-my sword’s nice, too.”
Looking down at her horn blade, which seemed shabby by comparison, Jung Heewon quietly concealed it at the other side of her waist.
I hadn’t done anything wrong, but somehow I felt guilty.
I picked on Lee Jihye for no particular reason.
“Hey, why do you speak politely to Heewon-ssi but casually to me?”
“Uh······ Well, I’ve got a bit of a weakness for cool unnies.”

When Lee Jihye answered awkwardly, Jung Heewon put her in a headlock as though she found her adorable. Apparently, those [Demon Slaying] types were on the same wavelength. After barely escaping the headlock, Lee Jihye asked,
“But why are you trying to save my master, ajusshi?”
“He’s my companion.”
“Cut the bullshit.”
“Because he’s useful.”
“······Somehow, that sounds like something my master would say.”
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ is curious about your intentions.]

Thinking about it, my actions could well have puzzled the constellations as well as Lee Jihye. Even now, the bastard was thinking about killing me whenever he got the chance, so rushing off to save him would certainly look strange.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is pleased by your desire to reform a fallen friend.]
[You have received a donation of 100 coins.]
And there was someone drawing their own mistaken conclusions.
But contrary to the expectations of the Demon-like Judge of Fire··· in other words, the archangel Uriel, my reason for going to save Yoo Joonghyuk was entirely personal.
Namely, to prevent his ‘regression upon death.’
Regression upon death. It sounded great. The stigma ‘Regression,’ which returned him to the past every time he died. Befitting a protagonist, it was an undeniably overpowered ability.
The problem, however, was that this ability stirred up some rather complicated thoughts in the supporting characters around him.
「But what happens to the world after you regress?」
At some point after Yoo Joonghyuk’s life count reached double digits, a supporting character had asked him that question. I’d forgotten the name, but Yoo Joonghyuk’s answer remained vivid.
「···I don’t know, either. I simply always choose a world where more people can live.」

It sounded convincing, but what he really meant was that an abandoned world was none of his business. In fact, nowhere in ‘Ways of Survival’ was there any definite theoretical explanation of what happened to a world after he regressed.
Scientific, magical, or otherwise.
That was precisely why I was uneasy.
What happened to a world after its regressor disappeared?
Did it reset along with the regressor?
Or did it split off into another branch of a parallel universe?
The latter would be a relief, but if it was the former, then my existence······.
“Hyung?”
“Oh, huh?”
Lee Gilyoung, who was holding on to my clothes beside me, was looking up at me with worried eyes.
“I think we’re here?”
[You are approaching an area outside the permitted zone. Take care not to leave the scenario area.]
A warning message popping up. It didn’t matter. Chungmuro’s ‘hidden dungeon’ was treated as an area ‘within the permitted zone’ anyway.
Exit 1, coming into view as we rounded the corner. Beside it, the dungeon entrance greeted us, shimmering with ominous shadows.
[You have discovered a ‘hidden dungeon’!]
[This dungeon has already been discovered by someone else. You cannot obtain the first discovery achievement.]
[A new hidden scenario has arrived!]
<Hidden Scenario ― Theatre Dungeon>
Category : Hidden
Difficulty : A-
Clear Conditions : Defeat the master of the Theatre Dungeon.
Time Limit : None
Reward : 4000 coins
Upon Failure : ―
Startled, Lee Jihye hesitantly stepped back.
“······What’s this? Theatre Dungeon?”
Lee Gilyoung looked startled, too. Well, this was probably the first time any of them had received a ‘hidden scenario.’ Jung Heewon also chimed in.
“A movie theatre turned into a dungeon······ There’s something romantic about that.”
Romantic, huh. She could only say that because she didn’t know how frightening a movie theatre could be. We proceeded inside the theatre. The familiar basement lobby of a multiplex greeted us.
[You have entered the ‘Theatre Dungeon’!]
Despite the tension with which we’d entered, the dungeon’s interior was desolate. A multiplex with nine floors in total, from basement level 1 to floor 8.
“Hyung, all the posters are torn. Who did that?”
“Who knows?”
That was what I said, but I actually knew the reason.

The key to this ‘Theatre Dungeon’ lay in the ‘posters’ on the walls. Yoo Joonghyuk had probably advanced upstairs while clearing all the trials contained in each poster. No doubt he’d intended to sweep up every trial reward.
Apart from the torn posters, there was nothing particularly strange about basement level 1. No items, no monsters. The only unusual thing was an elevator in one corner, smashed, its doors warped.
Lee Jihye asked,
“Is this really a dungeon? Why isn’t there anything here?”
“Something will turn up once we go upstairs.”
“···Do you know something, ajusshi?”
“A little.”
“How? There’s something suspicious about you, ajusshi. Are you on your second life or something?”
That would be your master.
No, that bastard was on his third.
Then Jung Heewon said,
“It’s because Dokja-ssi’s sponsor is Gung Ye.”
“···Really?”

Ignoring the two women’s banter, I was about to head to the ground floor when Lee Gilyoung suddenly grabbed me. The cockroach on his head was waving its antennae violently. Lee Jihye drew her sword almost at the same instant that I raised a hand to my mouth.
“Shh. There’s someone here besides us.”
Once we quieted our breathing, faint sounds of movement began to reach us. Directly upstairs. So······ near the lobby? At first I thought it might be Yoo Joonghyuk, but it wasn’t his voice.
“···So you’re sure, right? That there’s······ loads of that stuff here.”
“I told you, yes. I paid them a whole 1000 coins for this information.”
“You mean the <Prophets>?”
“Yeah. They’re a little creepy, but their information’s solid.”
Their murmured conversation drifted toward us. We climbed the escalator one step at a time, approaching them. Four men were gathered in the ground-floor lobby.
Lee Jihye whispered in my ear.
“Who the hell are those guys? I’ve never seen any of them in Chungmuro.”
“They probably came through the entrance aboveground.”
“Aboveground? Isn’t that covered in deadly poisonous fog? And the scenario, too―”

“Each station has different scenarios, and they progress at different speeds. They probably finished theirs faster than our station did. Eating subterranean species’ meat takes care of mild poisoning.”
Despite what I said, I was just as bewildered.
The <Prophets>?

There had been no information about people like that in any of Yoo Joonghyuk’s lives so far. At this point, Yoo Joonghyuk and I were the only ones who knew about the hidden dungeon in the first place.
What new variable had appeared?
It seemed I needed to find out.
“Then let’s go in.”
As the men spoke, a blue spotlight switched on in midair. The bright light seemed to envelop them, and then they vanished from sight.
“···What just happened?”

Jung Heewon asked, but I didn’t answer. Instead, I examined the posters on the wall. This one was torn, and that one, too······ Only when I reached the end of the wall did I find the sole intact poster. I read the words printed on it.
Steven Spielberg, Samuel L. Jackson, Jeff Goldblum······.
That bastard Yoo Joonghyuk··· Of all things, he’d left only this one? Just what I’d expect of his third round.
At that moment, the light returned.
With a whirrrrr― the spotlight aimed at us. Alarmed, Lee Jihye and Lee Gilyoung recoiled, but there was no way to avoid it. This beam was designed to hit us.
At the last moment, I asked Jung Heewon,
“Heewon-ssi, do you like movies?”
“Of course. Doesn’t pretty much everyone?”
“Then you might start hating them now.”
“What’s this all of a sudden―”
[You have been struck by a projection beam.]
[The screening on this floor will begin.]

The scenery around us slowly began to change. Perhaps because this wasn’t a mere illusion, [Fourth Wall] didn’t work as it had before. The worn linoleum floor turned into green undergrowth, while the information desk and the concession stand where popcorn had been popped became dense rainforest. The ceiling had transformed into an endless blue sky without a single cloud. Flustered, Lee Jihye muttered,
“Where the hell are we?”
Shouting, Lee Jihye slashed wildly at the surrounding trees and bushes, but nothing changed. With a calm expression, Lee Gilyoung began searching for insects.

I touched a nearby tree to test it. A hard, damp texture. It was a real tropical rainforest recreating the Mesozoic Era. The realism was on an entirely different level from the Specter’s [Phantom Prison]. As expected, this was probably the power of the theatre master on the dungeon’s eighth floor.
“We’re inside a movie.”
“······It really is one impossible thing after another.”
A novel had become reality, so there was no rule saying a movie couldn’t become reality, too.
Quick to adapt, Jung Heewon seemed to accept it right away.
“Ajusshi, what movie is this?”
“You’ll find out soon.”
“···Can’t you just tell me? Wait, kid, what are you···”

At that moment, the bushes stirred, and something sprang out in front of Lee Gilyoung. It was an insect resembling a giant praying mantis. About 40 cm long, perhaps. Horrified, Lee Jihye adjusted her grip on her longsword and shouted,
“Hey, kid! Get back, quick!”
But Lee Gilyoung’s expression seemed to ask what all the fuss was about.
“It’s not a praying mantis. It’s an insect from the Triassic called Titanoptera.”
“What?”
Lee Gilyoung reached straight toward the insect called Titano-whatever. It didn’t reject his touch, and a little later, both Lee Gilyoung and the insect were enveloped in blue light.
Lee Jihye looked at me blankly.
“What······ is he?”
“Fabre.”
Bringing Lee Gilyoung had definitely been a good decision. With his ability, we might be able to get through the trials more easily than I’d expected.
The giant mantis twitched its large mouth, and Lee Gilyoung nodded repeatedly. I wasn’t sure, but presumably some sort of conversation was taking place.
A little later, however, Lee Gilyoung’s face began to pale as he talked to the mantis.
······What was wrong?
Lee Gilyoung hurriedly turned toward me.
“Hyung!”
No sooner had he spoken than an earthshaking rumble sounded. Something was charging toward us at tremendous speed, smashing huge palm trees to pieces.
GROOOOOAR!

The muzzle of the enormous reptile emerging through the rainforest was stained with bright red blood. In front of it, several bloodied men were running toward us. They were the men who’d entered before us.
“Aaaaaaagh!”
“H-help me!”
Backing away hesitantly, Lee Jihye spoke to Jung Heewon.
“I know what movie this is.”
“······Yeah, me too.”
A height well over ten metres, and a tough hide. Brutal muscle covering its entire body. The Mesozoic Era’s strongest predator stood before our eyes.
A beast comparable to a grade-7 monster species, even at a glance.
Considering that this was still only the dungeon’s first floor, the difficulty was atrocious, but instead my heart began to race.
Because the harder a ‘hidden dungeon’ was, the better its rewards.
I drew my sword and said,
“Get ready to fight.”

Yoo Joonghyuk had probably skipped this movie after looking only at its subject matter. The Theatre Dungeon’s main rewards were related to the subject of each movie. He must have thought there was no way a movie full of dinosaurs would offer any useful rewards. But he wouldn’t know.
That this movie, too, held a truly important reward.
“···Seriously? You’re going to fight that thing?”
“We have to kill it to make an exit.”
“An exit?”
“We’re inside a movie. Did you forget?”
The T-Rex’s massive body, approaching in great strides. Behind it, I could see the island’s central research laboratory. And the escape helicopter stationed on the laboratory roof.
We were inside a movie. A movie made tangible by the master of the ‘Theatre Dungeon.’
So there was only one way to escape.
“Let’s give it a great ending.”
The moment its vivid yellow eyes turned toward us, an ear-splitting roar rang out.
GROOOOOAR!
[The grade-7 earth dragon species ‘Tyrannosaurus Rex’ has noticed you.]
[‘Tyrannosaurus Rex’ has activated the skill ‘Predation Fear’!]
[The exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ blocks the effects of ‘Predation Fear.’]
Thanks to [Fourth Wall], my mind was calm, but it couldn’t keep the hairs on my body from standing on end. This must have been the fear felt by prey.
“Everyone, dodge!”
Jung Heewon and Lee Jihye, who’d briefly frozen, snapped out of it. I picked up Lee Gilyoung, who was right beside me, and ran toward the rear.
CRASH, CRASH, CRASH, CRASH!
An enormous tail came sweeping in, destroying every tree in front of it.
“Guuurgh!”
The fleeing men were struck in the back and sent flying, vomiting blood. Fortunately, Jung Heewon and Lee Jihye seemed to have barely escaped the danger zone.
I put Lee Gilyoung down and shouted,
“Gilyoung, fall back! Heewon-ssi and Jihye, spread out to the left and right!”
That was when a message appeared beside me.
[The character ‘Lee Gilyoung’ activates the skill ‘Dinosaur Book’!]
···Huh?
“Tyrannosaurus is agile for its size, but its narrow field of vision makes it vulnerable to attacks from its blind spots.”
“···What?”
“I read it in a dinosaur book when I was little.”
“When you were little?”
“···When I was younger than I am now.”
I stared blankly at Lee Gilyoung, then shut my mouth.
Right, this wasn’t the time for pointless quibbling.
GROOOOAR!
[You activate the exclusive skill ‘White Pure Star Energy’!]

Waving my brilliant blade from side to side, I began drawing the T-Rex’s attention. Neither Lee Jihye nor Jung Heewon was a tank. Lee Gilyoung wasn’t either, of course. That left me as the only one who could take the risk here.
“While I keep its attention, get behind it―”
Before I’d even finished speaking, Lee Jihye and Jung Heewon were already sprinting behind the T-Rex. It was nice that they caught on quickly.
KROOOOAR!

I barely dodged the teeth of the charging beast before its hind foot came flying at me. Before I could swing [Unbreakable Faith], its tail followed, grazing just above my hair. A chilling shudder swept through my body. My Constitution level had passed 20, so getting hit by that wouldn’t kill me, but it was still terrifying.
Perhaps I was the one who’d been lucky all this time.
Perhaps the ‘sunfish’ who’d die at the slightest brush was actually me, rather than Yoo Joonghyuk.
Slash! Swish!

Meanwhile, Jung Heewon and Lee Jihye were steadily dealing damage from behind it. A combination of [Sword Training] and [Kendo]. Brilliant sword strikes were adding more and more wounds to the T-Rex’s thick legs.
If they activated [Demon Slaying] as well, killing the T-Rex would take a little time, but shouldn’t be too difficult.
“Hyung! I’ll draw its attention!”
This little brat. I’d told him to stay back, but he wouldn’t listen.
“No, Gilyoung, you―”
“I can do it!”

Suddenly, Lee Gilyoung stepped forward and began making incomprehensible hand signals. I was wondering what that was about when the giant mantis flew in from somewhere, jabbed the T-Rex’s eye, and fled. It was that Titano-whatever insect from earlier.
GROOOAR!

The T-Rex’s eyes darted in confusion as the mantis disrupted its vision. Judging by the elaborate hand movements, Lee Gilyoung seemed to be controlling the mantis. I looked down at him with renewed interest.
Between this and that Dinosaur Book skill earlier, wasn’t this kid actually an incredibly overpowered character?
No wonder Yoo Joonghyuk wanted him.
Krrr, GROOOOAR!

Thanks to Lee Gilyoung’s outstanding performance, the battle turned in our favour in an instant. The T-Rex’s movements had grown much slower, and before I knew it, a red murderous gleam shone in Jung Heewon’s and Lee Jihye’s eyes.
[Demon Slaying].

It had the drawback of leaving its user vulnerable to mental attacks, but it was a good skill that increased combat power with heightened excitement. The sight of the two women darting through the rainforest with blazing eyes was truly spectacular.
It stung quite a bit to see this after losing Lee Jihye to Yoo Joonghyuk.
Still, Jung Heewon was overwhelmingly superior in potential for growth. ‘Judge of Evil’ was that good an attribute, and Jung Heewon hadn’t even made a <Sponsorship Contract> yet.
The T-Rex seemed to have lost quite a bit of health by now. Time to land the final blow?
[You activate ‘Blade of Faith’!]

I began concentrating my remaining magic power into the blade. I had no constellation sponsor, and I wasn’t as nimble as Jung Heewon or Lee Jihye. But that didn’t mean my combat power was weak. I had an overpowered item that made up for all of it.
WOOOOOSH!
Ether Blade.
[The special option of ‘Unbreakable Faith’ activates.]
[The ether’s element changes to ‘Flame.’]
An enormous amount of magic power drained out all at once, leaving my body severely fatigued. But I had a way to replenish it later, so I didn’t worry.
In an instant, the blade lengthened by over 1 metre, and flames coiled around it.
I ran behind the tyrannosaurus.
“Everyone, get out of the way!”

The moment the sluggish tyrannosaurus faltered, I climbed up its tail. Without the [Sense of Balance] skill, I nearly fell several times, but by repeatedly driving my blade into its skin, I somehow managed to avoid falling off.
KROOOOAR!
Bleeding all over, the T-Rex rolled on the ground. I drove my blade in wherever I could. Flames rose from each wound when I pulled the sword out.
Gasping in agony, the T-Rex glared at me one final time with its yellow eyes before they rolled back.
[You have become the first to successfully hunt the grade-7 earth dragon species ‘Tyrannosaurus Rex’!]
[You have obtained 1000 coins as a reward.]
“Ah······ We really killed it.”
“I told you I could do it.”
At my words, the panting Jung Heewon looked proud. A T-Rex ranked among the strongest grade-7 monster species, so she had every right to be. Lee Jihye ran over a little later and grumbled at me.
“I’d practically killed it already!”
“As if. It would’ve taken a lot more hits to die.”
For no particular reason, I made a show of taking the credit as I wiped my sword. Jung Heewon asked,
“But did they kill the tyrannosaurus in this movie?”
“No, but isn’t this more entertaining?”
“···Pardon?”
“If it’s a fantasy action adventure, we ought to do at least this much.”
At that moment, a system message appeared in my mind.
[The theatre master is satisfied with the movie’s altered ending.]
Jung Heewon cried out in disbelief.
“Huh?”
That was right. The way to clear the ‘Theatre Dungeon’ wasn’t to see the ‘real ending.’

If it were, even Yoo Joonghyuk wouldn’t have cleared this dungeon. The key was to create the ending the ‘theatre master’ wanted. And for the record, this theatre master was an extreme catharsis junkie.
“You get it now, right? We just have to smash everything.”
In other words, if we removed every obstacle to the ending, the movie would naturally come to a conclusion.
[You can now move to the next floor.]
[Proceed to the helipad at the top of the laboratory.]
“Let’s move in a little while. We need to collect some rewards, too.”
With that, I began looking around the T-Rex. Before long, I found one of the men who’d entered before us. The others seemed to have been eaten by the T-Rex or torn to death.
“Hey, stay with me.”
“U-uuurgh······.”
Blood was still pouring from the man’s back. A wound from the T-Rex’s claws. Judging by the fully exposed bones, he was already beyond saving.
“Breathe out slowly.”
I gave the man some of the drinking water I’d brought. He gulped it down, then vomited blood again. With no other choice, I decided to ask the urgent questions first.
“How did you find out about this place?”
“Who exactly are the <Prophets>?”
The man’s breathing was growing even harsher.
“Those······ who received······ r-revelations······.”
······Revelations?
“I want······ to live······.”
With a wet splutter, a stream of blood burst from the man’s mouth. His breathing stopped, and he went limp. Jung Heewon and the rest of the group approached from behind.
“That man······?”
I shook my head, looking down at the fallen man.
‘Revelations,’ huh. Interesting nonsense.
Because the only similar ability in the ‘Ways of Survival’ I knew was ‘Future Sight,’ and the only person with that ability was the Prophet ‘Anna Croft.’
Then there was only one answer.
······So there were others besides me.
But they didn’t know as much as I did.
The proof was that they’d leaked information about this place to test it rather than coming themselves.
“Dokja-ssi?”
“Let’s rest a little before we go.”

We covered the man’s body with large leaves and gathered near the dead T-Rex. We needed to hurry to catch up with Yoo Joonghyuk, but if we chased him without enough rest, the entire group might be wiped out before we even met him.
I searched the T-Rex’s carcass.

The older a relic was, the better.

We stopped at the ‘Seoul Museum of History’, beside Gyeonghuigung Palace.
Yoo Sangah's eyes lit up.

Fwoooosh― Crack!

A shiver ran down my spine.
[Strong Magic Arrow (强魔矢)].
Someone had properly learned the Archery skill.
Who on earth was it?
The unexpected attack sent my thoughts into a tangle.
Had someone actually anticipated our route?
“Everyone, get inside! Hurry!”
Several more arrows flew toward us.
[Activating ‘Blade of Faith’!]
I swung my sword to cover a wide area, knocking away the incoming arrows. Fortunately, they weren't imbued with much magic, so blocking them wasn't difficult.
The problem was their number.
Fwit!
An arrow flew in from my blind spot and grazed the outside of my thigh. I quickly retreated and hid behind cover.
“Hahaha! Where do you think you're roaming, fledgling king!”
A booming voice like a tiger's roar rang out.

Which meant a separate detachment had been sent out.
Apparently, some of these kings were cleverer than I'd thought.
Were they planning to grab the items while also taking the flags of kings from smaller territories?
[The exclusive skill ‘Character List’ activates.]
I used the skill on the hulking man charging toward us from the front.
<Character Information>

Age: 33

Damn it. They say a tiger comes when you speak of it.

People with acting attributes were prone to attracting constellations like these.
“If you know what a king's honor means, surrender your flag willingly. Then I shall spare the lives of your group members.”

[Coins Owned: 68,150C]
Damn it······ Should I just spend my coins here?
But if I spent coins here to recklessly raise my overall stats, the difficulty of the fourth scenario's final phase would rise sharply.
Then the entire plan would fall apart.
If I just bit the bullet and spent about 20,000 coins...
“Are you not ashamed to bear the name of the Three Kingdoms while persecuting the king of a mere minor nation?”
At the sudden voice, I turned to the side—and there, of all people, was a familiar figure approaching. Gyebaek's incarnation, Chu Wangin, scowled.

Min Jiwon, the King of Beauty.

······Seriously?

Yoo Sangah was running toward me from behind, holding a relic that resembled a small disc.
She'd found it already?
[Ganpyeongui (簡平儀)]
The relic, which resembled a wall clock, was emitting light in Yoo Sangah's hand.
A flurry of thoughts raced through my mind.
I looked at the Ganpyeongui, then at Min Jiwon, then at Gwanchang's terrified incarnation.

Maybe I could win this without spending any coins?
“Attack!”

Gyebaek's greatsword split a Hwarang in two as he charged.

“Never retreat in battle! In battle, there shall be no retreat!”
Before I could continue, the Hwarang captain stepped forward and shouted.
At the same time, the Hwarang drew their weapons in unison and echoed him.
“No retreat!”

“Serve the king!”
That bastard?

“Hahaha, you hasten your own deaths!”
Gyebaek's incarnation, Chu Wangin, shouted gleefully.
The Hwarang captain, charging forward and swinging his spear.
They said an incarnation took after their sponsor. That guy was a perfect example.
[The character ‘Chu Wangin’ activates the stigma ‘Baekje Kendo Lv.4’!]
“Guaaagh!”
Struck by the greatsword, the Hwarang captain's body flew through the air.
I shouted to Min Jiwon.
“Tell them to pull back their formation!”
“Pull back your formation! Now!”
[The character ‘Min Jiwon’ has activated ‘Army Command Lv.2’!]
[The soldiers have lost their reason.]
[Skill activation is canceled.]
“I said pull back your formation!”

A flustered Min Jiwon shouted once more, but the Hwarang, already fired up by ‘Five Secular Precepts,’ did not heed her commands. Their loyalty was to beauty (美), rather than Queen Jinseong's charisma, in the first place······ Perhaps it couldn't be helped.
With a crash, Lee Gilyoung broke through a second-floor window of the museum and landed beside me.
“Hyung, should I call Titano?”
Lee Gilyoung's eyes gleamed, as though he was ready to use [Diverse Communication] at any moment.
“No, we're all right for now.”

Summoning a grade-6 insect king species like last time would help, but Lee Gilyoung had slept for two whole days afterward. High-grade monster species were difficult to control, and one wrong move could get our allies swept up in the attack too.
Above all, Lee Gilyoung was my secret weapon.
I had to keep him in reserve until the melee between the kings began.
“Aaaaagh!”
Four or five Hwarang at the front were sent flying.
By contrast, I couldn't see a single dead soldier in the Baekje army.
I reached toward Yoo Sangah as she ran up.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi, the relic······!”
I took the [Ganpyeongui] from Yoo Sangah.
The Ganpyeongui. Everyone was distracted by the Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword, but this was the item you truly had to acquire in the fourth scenario.

The Hwarang captain, struck by Chu Wangin yet again, was already battered all over.

[The constellation ‘The Last Hero of Hwangsanbeol’ is enjoying himself.]
[The constellation ‘Supreme Maegum’ grows anxious.]
The Baekje army's momentum kept rising, while the Silla army's morale crumbled.
Gyebaek's resentful spirit seemed to shimmer within Chu Wangin's body.
“Wipe out those damned Silla bastards!”

The more closely a constellation's situation resembled the history they had lived through, the higher their synchronization rate with their incarnation became, and the greater the power of their stigmas.
And now, ‘constellations’ with ties to one another had encountered each other······.
It was about time for a ‘stage’ to take shape.
Bzzzzzt―
“Waaah? What's going on!”
The startled people screamed.
Sparks flew through the space around us, and the scenery began to change. Seoul's sprawling Gwanghwamun was turning into a plain amid rugged mountains.
「Stage Transformation (舞臺化).」
A phenomenon that occurred when constellations with ties to one another fought while highly synchronized with their incarnations.
「Stage Transformation」 summoned the very time and space in which those constellations had fought to this location.
Of course, the space didn't actually change; it was closer to augmented reality······.
The problem was that, for those who had summoned this stage, that wasn't the case.
“Hahahaha······ How I have missed you, Hwangsanbeol!”
Chu Wangin shouted, his synchronization rate having risen considerably.
Now he seemed to believe he truly was General Gyebaek.

KABOOOOM!
Rampaging like a crazed monster, Chu Wangin was the very image of a yaksha.
Once 「Stage Transformation」 occurred and their synchronization with their sponsors increased, incarnations could wield several times their own power.

The Ganpyeongui, an astronomical observation instrument made in seventeenth-century Joseon.

In an instant, part of the sky turned pitch-black, casting a shadow over the ground.

Sensing something amiss, Chu Wangin charged toward me.

Lee Sungkook stepped forward, drawing his sword. I didn't know how long a Hypnotist like him could last, but he should buy me a little time.
A moment later, a constellation shone brilliantly in the sky.
You've finally appeared.
[The constellation ‘King Heungmu the Great’ looks at you.]
“O General.”
[The constellation ‘King Heungmu the Great’ listens to your words.]
“There are people here who need your help. Your people are dying, calling for you.”

King Heungmu the Great. The one and only person posthumously honored as a king of Silla despite not being royalty.
He probably wouldn't be able to refuse my plea.
Because Hwangsanbeol was his battlefield.
But something unexpected happened.
[The constellation ‘King Heungmu the Great’ does not wish to intervene in the history of the present world.]
[The constellation ‘King Heungmu the Great’ will refuse your proposal.]
Just as the constellation was about to fade, Yoo Sangah interjected.

Quick-witted Yoo Sangah seemed to have realized who King Heungmu the Great was.
[The constellation ‘King Heungmu the Great’ looks back.]

Drawing a short breath, Yoo Sangah began to speak.
“I understand your wish to respect what has already happened, the history that has passed. But General-nim! Some histories still don't end even after they've been recorded.”
Clear and steady—the voice of the Yoo Sangah I knew.
“Do you have no regrets? That field where you sacrificed a young Hwarang, stained by the deaths of countless people—your battlefield······! Have you already forgotten it?”

“Of course, the history that has passed will not change. The soldiers on that field will still find no solace, and the young Hwarang will not regain their lives. But General-nim! I'd forgotten. Just how good Yoo Sangah was with words.
When she was a new employee, she'd been the queen of presentations at Mino Soft.
“General-nim! Your Hwangsanbeol has ended······ but we are still in Hwangsanbeol.”
[The constellation ‘King Heungmu the Great’ quietly closes his eyes.]
There were moments like that in life.
Moments when, without anyone telling you, you knew what was about to happen.

This was a constellation's True Voice (眞言).
Words that endangered one's very existence simply by being heard.

Gyebaek's incarnation, Chu Wangin, was aghast.

Such was the magnitude of the beings called constellations (星座).

An unfamiliar depth resonated in my voice.
In the distance, Gwanchang's incarnation staggered to his feet.

King Heungmu the Great was seeing the world through me.

To the point that even I, a reader of Ways of Survival, found it puzzling.

Looking at Gyebaek's incarnation with sorrowful eyes, King Heungmu the Great spoke through me.
“I am Kim Yushin, the 15th leader of the Hwarang.”
King Heungmu the Great, the National Immortal Kim Yushin (金庾信).
“I shall comfort the soul of this unfortunate constellation and set right the history of the present world.”

The renowned general who had led Silla to victory at the Battle of Hwangsanbeol conveyed his will to me. I moved my right hand. A brilliant blue light began to shimmer around the sword hilt I held upright.

Rrrrrumble―
It seemed as though all of Hwangsan was screaming.

「All Yonghwa Hyangdo (龍華香徒), come here at once.」

Something was rising from within the fissure.
Forgotten ghosts, buried in the defiled earth (穢土) of history.

Groooooar!
The Yonghwa Hyangdo, Kim Yushin's most elite unit, emerged from the pages of forgotten history.
The Owner of the Throne
Kim Yushin's stigma, ‘Great Hwarang Assembly,’ was a technique that summoned the ‘Yonghwa Hyangdo,’ the elite hwarang who had died throughout history.
GRAAAAAAH!
Put simply, this was a land-based version of the ‘Ghost Fleet’ Lee Jihye had used.

The soldiers who had fought to prevent their country's ruin.

CRUNCH! CR-CR-CRUNCH!
“Kim Yushin―!”
As that fearsome cry thundered through the air, even the emotionless ranks of the Yonghwa Hyangdo faltered.
That was Gyebaek.
Baekje's last great general, Gyebaek.
In terms of physical buffing abilities alone, Gyebaek surpassed Kim Yushin. In fact, Gyebaek had never fought Kim Yushin one-on-one in the ‘Battle of Hwangsanbeol.’
More precisely, it would be fair to say that Kim Yushin had avoided the duel.

In history, Gyebaek's detachment had resisted Kim Yushin's army, which outnumbered them ten to one, winning again and again on an impossible battlefield.
Although Kim Yushin had ultimately been the victor, Gyebaek had not lost a single battle until the final act at Hwangsanbeol began.
A battle fanatic driven by patriotism bordering on madness and a grim resolve.
Though I now had Kim Yushin's blessing behind me, under different circumstances I might have summoned Gyebaek instead of Kim Yushin.
Unable to watch any longer, Gwanchang's incarnation shouted.
“General-nim!”
“Do not move.”
Kim Yushin spoke through my mouth. Watching the ranks of the Yonghwa Hyangdo die, without the slightest change in his expression.
Kim Yushin's boundlessly tranquil state of mind came through to me exactly as it was.
Gyebaek shouted.

He feared death, and he was afraid of defeat.
That was why he was strong.
He did not act rashly or let emotions sweep him away.
He disposed of enemies he could defeat, using methods that guaranteed victory.

“KRAAAAAAGH!”

Gyebaek's desperate struggle against hundreds of Yonghwa Hyangdo was harrowing. His incarnation's wounds were now too severe for him to survive. His whole body was drenched in blood, with fatal wounds in his thigh, both arms, and his side.

[Activating the stigma ‘Request Reinforcements’!]
