Startled by my words, my companions looked at me.
[······Did you just call us?]
Of course they would be surprised.
They couldn’t have expected a mere incarnation to stop the Enforcement Division’s dokkaebis.
After studying me quietly, the dokkaebi executor spoke.
[I see. You’re that incarnation called ‘Kim Dokja’, aren’t you?]
The other dokkaebi asked.
[You know him?]
[An incarnation who has recently become famous around here. One of the strongest on the peninsula, yet apparently he still hasn’t signed a constellation sponsorship contract.]
Watching them chatter as they pleased, I immediately spoke to Bihyung through [Dokkaebi Communication].
‘Bihyung. I’ll give you 100,000 coins.’
Bihyung, who had been following the dokkaebi executors, opened his eyes wide.
‘Upgrade me to a Platinum Member of the [Dokkaebi Bag].’
―Wait, why all of a sudden?
‘Just do it.’
―Damn it······.
Watching the executors approach, I hurried Bihyung along. With a sigh, he began manipulating something in midair.
[100000 coins have been spent.]
[Congratulations! You have become a Platinum Member of the ‘Dokkaebi Bag’!]
Normally, the upgrade came with spectacular celebratory fireworks and visual effects, but I asked Bihyung to skip them.
Unlike [Gold Member] status, which cost only 5000 coins to attain, [Platinum Member] status brought an entirely different level of treatment.
[Well, incarnation Kim Dokja. Why did you call us?]
The executors asked, still unaware of my upgrade. Unlike other dokkaebis, they were mountainous in size, and merely facing them made me tense.
That was hardly surprising. Though they had lost their Status and fallen far, some of them had originally been Historical-grade constellations.
I let out a light breath and spoke.
“I request a ‘Private Dokkaebi Audience (獨對)’.”
[What?]
Taken aback by my words, the dokkaebi executors looked at each other. Then came a snort of laughter, followed by a voice.
[Only Platinum Members or higher may request a ‘private audience’······. Could it be?]
“You guessed right. Check for yourselves.”
At that, the two dokkaebis looked at each other again. They checked several details through the system, then exclaimed in astonishment.
[It’s true.]
[How on earth did an incarnation become a Platinum Member······?]
“Now, I qualify, don’t I?”
After a moment’s hesitation, the dokkaebi executor nodded.
[Indeed. Which dokkaebi do you wish to have a ‘private audience’ with? Platinum status permits audiences with dokkaebis up to quasi-upper-grade, and as for scheduling an appointment······.]
“There’s no need to schedule one. You already have the one I want with you.”
I pointed at the dokkaebi I wanted.
“I want a private audience with intermediate dokkaebi ‘Paul’.”
At those words, the Enforcement Division’s dokkaebis turned to each other again.
How long did they remain like that? The two dokkaebis burst out laughing at the same time.
[Pfft. Bwahahahaha!]
[Interesting. Don’t tell me······.]
The quick-witted executors seemed to have caught on to something.
Some distance away, Paul was looking toward us with a bewildered expression.
[A private audience with prisoner dokkaebi ‘Paul’ is granted.]
[You have 20 minutes for your private audience.]
As though they had found an entertaining spectacle, the Enforcement Division readily granted my request.
I had known they would.
The ‘Enforcement Division’ didn’t like other streamers to begin with.
By their very origins, they were closer to ‘subscribing constellations’ than to ‘streamers’.
No sooner had they finished speaking than a small, transparent dome appeared around Paul and me.
A ‘private audience’ was originally a space for constellations and dokkaebis to meet in secret.
[Your private audience with intermediate dokkaebi ‘Paul’ begins.]
But a thing’s purpose could always change depending on who used it.
Outside the dome, I could see Bihyung saying something to the executors.
Suddenly trapped alone with me, Paul ground his teeth and bared his hostility.
“Why did you ask to see me? I suppose you want to gloat?”
The [Restraint Code] the dokkaebi executors had placed on him still shimmered over his body. As long as that code remained, Paul could use neither his dokkaebi authority nor any of his innate power.
In other words, the bastard standing before me was completely powerless.
“Stop bluffing. I know exactly what situation you’re in.”
Paul faltered and backed toward the edge of the dome. But a condescending smile still lingered on his lips.
“Haha, I see. I think I understand what vulgar thoughts you’re having. You want to avenge that slave, don’t you?”

“How laughable. Did you think I wouldn’t understand a lowly human’s desires? Very well, go ahead and try. I don’t know how you learned about ‘private audiences’, but this is a place where neither party can take the other’s life. No matter how much you struggle······!”
I charged straight at him and drove my fist into his face with all my strength.
A jet of blue blood burst from his nose. Still failing to grasp what was happening, he let out a belated scream and crumpled to the ground. I spoke.
“I can’t kill you, but I can hit you.”
“Gaaaaagh! How dare you······!”
“There, your true colors are finally showing. I was sick of hearing that disgusting politeness anyway.”
“Guh, guh-huurgh······.”
“First time you’ve felt pain like this, isn’t it? You’ve never been beaten like this in all your life as a dokkaebi, have you?”
“Heh, heh-heh. Heheheh······.”
Even as he spilled blood, Paul was still laughing.
“Y-you’ve just made a mistake. Th-this space has special rules in place for those who abuse ‘private audiences’, as you are doing.”
As though it had been waiting, a message sounded.
[You have injured a dokkaebi inside the ‘private audience space’.]
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
Dokkaebis really were an insufferable bunch.
To think they had even set up this sort of penalty in case a constellation lost its temper and attacked them. Their greed for coins had reached ridiculous heights.
But I had known about the penalty, so I merely shrugged.
Wiping away his blood, Paul laughed.
“Foolish human. You bring ruin upon yourself through anger. Go on, hit me as much as you please. With the coins a mere incarnation like you possesses······.”
“How much do you think I have?”
At that moment, Paul fell silent.
“Doesn’t it seem strange? How a mere incarnation like me became a ‘Platinum Member’?”
Watching his wavering gaze, I grinned at him.
“I have plenty of coins. I made a fortune thanks to you.”
As Paul turned white, I quietly cracked my knuckles.
All the goddamn scenarios I had endured flashed through my mind.
[Coins possessed: 205,902C]
I recalled my last glimpse of the dying Shin Yoosung.
Incidentally, among the things I had told her was this.
―I’ll make sure to beat that dokkaebi bastard within an inch of his life.
So this was the first promise I would keep.
Thwaaack!
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
My next punch shattered his nose.
I didn’t say things like, ‘This one is for so-and-so.’
Thwaaack!
After all, none of these blows could count as revenge for anyone.
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
“Aaaaagh! A-a lowly human dares······!”
Thwaaack!
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
“Y-you think you can do this to me and get away······!”
Thwaaack!
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
“I’ll kill you! I swear, I swear I’ll······!”
Thwaaack!
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
“W-wait! Just a moment! Sto······.”
As he curled up in terror, I stopped punching for the first time. For an instant, hope entered his eyes.
“Y-yes. A wise decision. There is nothing to be gained by doing this here······.”
Watching him hastily return to polite speech, I asked.
“Did you stop?”
“When Yoosung told you to stop, did you?”
I looked down at him quietly. He said nothing.
Instead, he looked once at me and once at the ground. Finally, he looked at the sky. As though the one he blamed for his predicament were up there.
“Th-this is meaningless! Doing this won’t bring your dead companion back to life!”
It wouldn’t bring my dead companion back to life. That was true.
But.
“It does mean something.”
I raised my fist at him again as his horns trembled.
“If I’d died. Shin Yoosung would have done this too.”
Thwaaack!
Flesh flew in a violent spray, and one of his fangs flew out and rolled across the ground.
“Lee Hyunsung would have too. So would Yoo Sangah and Lee Gilyoung.”
My fist slammed into his abdomen and ruptured his internal organs.
“And probably······ even that bastard Yoo Joonghyuk······.”
My companions outside the dome were watching.

Shin Yoosung, her eyes red and her fists clenched. Lee Jihye and Lee Gilyoung were shouting something. Lee Hyunsung’s eyes were reddening, his face solemn, and Yoo Sangah watched me, biting her lip hard.
I looked at Yoo Joonghyuk last, then turned my gaze back to Paul.
“I-I exist outside the scenarios! You can’t earn coins by doing this! There’s nothing in it for you!”
Coins······.
Right. In the end, that was all you dokkaebis could think about.
Some stories became coins.
Some stories didn’t become coins.
“Maybe you’re right.”
No constellation had issued a bounty scenario, and no sub-scenario had told me to take him down.
But that was precisely why this act had meaning.
Because no one had told me to do it.
“I’m doing it because there’s nothing in it for me.”
“Wh-what?”
Ever since the world’s destruction began, coins had become the guiding principle behind all humans’ behavior.
People acted because the constellations gave them coins, and didn’t act because the constellations didn’t give them coins.
But sometimes humans acted without regard for any of that.
“You probably don’t understand, but humans are animals who find meaning in life through things like this.”
“Wh-what are you······ Aaaaagh!”
I raised my fist again and began beating him.
Thwaaack!
The punches that followed crushed his face, his ribs, his joints, one by one, with meticulous care.
There was no danger of killing him, so I didn’t hold back.
Every blow the best I could deliver.
Each time his skin split and his bones crumbled, something deep inside me burst apart too.
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
The truth was, I knew.
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
I knew perfectly well. No matter how much I beat him, this could not offer even the slightest consolation for Shin Yoosung’s death.
The dead Shin Yoosung would not witness this scene.
But even so, I kept my fists moving.
I beat him, and beat him again.
Thwaaack!
Just as Yoo Joonghyuk had.
Just as he had continued regressing until the very last moment, even when no one understood his cause.
[500 coins have been deducted as a penalty.]
Eventually, the constellations’ messages sounded from the air.
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ is excited by a development unlike anything previously seen.]
[You have received 500 coins in sponsorship.]
I stopped punching for a moment and looked up at the sky.
Even a story like this became a scenario for the constellations.
“This time, I’m not acting.”
[The 500 coins received in sponsorship have been returned.]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ is greatly flustered.]
They could think of it as a free service.
Right now, I didn’t care.
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ expresses interest in your actions.]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is deeply moved by your actions.]
I began punching again.
Only the sound of the dokkaebi’s skin bursting and his intermittent groans rang out.
The constellations silently watched what I did.
No one gave me coins, but I could feel that they were watching me.
And sometimes, that alone was enough.
“U-uuurgh······ I was wrong. P-please spare me! P-please! Please!”
Unable to endure any more, Paul dragged his body, beaten to a pulp, to the edge of the dome and pounded on it.
The dome’s wall rang hollowly, but the Enforcement Division didn’t respond.
If anything, they seemed to welcome my bizarre behavior.
I couldn’t know for certain, but they were probably saying things like this.
「So they can make coins that way too.」
「Those goddamn streamer bastards.」
The Enforcement Division’s dokkaebis didn’t like streamers. Having evolved into dokkaebis from beings of alien form (異形), the executors were good at fighting, but had no talent for leading scenarios.
Before long, Paul’s body was utterly mangled. I grabbed the bloodied wreck of him by the collar.
By now, I could probably start asking what I wanted to know.
“Where is Shin Yoosung’s soul now?”
A soul that died as a component of a scenario could not escape the shackles of its contract, even in death.
But it was different when the contract itself had ceased to exist.
Intermediate dokkaebi Paul spoke only after taking dozens more blows.
[Th······ that. I-I don’t know either. B-because you borrowed the archangels’ power······ o-our contract with that bitch was destroyed······.]
Just as I’d thought.
The dokkaebis had received ‘Beast Lord Shin Yoosung’ from a demon, and during the transfer, the bonds of the contract had been joined through demonic power.
And those bonds had all been burned away by Uriel’s [Hell Flames Ignition].
In other words, Shin Yoosung’s soul had lost its anchor and was now drifting through the world.
[Y-you. Will never, get, your companion, back······ That bitch’s soul, will soon, enter, the labyrinth, of worldlines······.]
With those final words, Paul collapsed.
[The ‘Private Dokkaebi Audience’ has ended.]
The transparent dome vanished, and the Enforcement Division swaggered over, whistling.
[Well, he’s suffered something terrible before even being referred for disciplinary action.]
They glanced at me, then departed with cheerful smiles. Watching Bihyung hurry after them, I asked.
‘Did you pay the bribe?’
―Of course. But didn’t you spend too many coins?
‘I still have plenty left.’
Paul had taken exactly 124 blows before losing consciousness.
[Coins possessed: 143,902C]
Bihyung sighed and glanced at me.
―Once I enter the Bureau, we won’t be able to communicate for a while. I’ll leave the channel open, so stay out of trouble while I’m gone. Please.
As Bihyung earnestly urged me to behave, I privately thought this was a good thing. With him gone, no one would object to what I was about to do.
[Settlement of additional rewards is delayed due to a scenario error.]
With the main scenario’s administrator entirely absent, scenario developments would stall for a while. It would only be a day or two, but that was enough time for me.
Looking up at the dokkaebis disappearing through the portal, I recalled my last conversation with Shin Yoosung.
―Don’t worry. You won’t die.
―What do you mean?
―I’ll help you come back to life. I’ve done it twice myself, and it’s more manageable than you’d think.
In truth, I had intended to avoid using this method right through to the end.
After all, this plan required her to die ‘once’.
And there was no firm guarantee she could return to life.
―I don’t know how long it’ll take. But if you’ll wait for me, if you don’t give up, I’ll make sure to bring you back to life.
If Shin Yoosung’s soul fell into the ‘labyrinth of worldlines’, bringing her back to life would become almost impossible.
But that hadn’t happened yet.
If I could only retrieve her soul, she could surely live again.
The problem was ‘how’ to find that soul.
I turned to Yoo Sangah.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
“Yes.”
Even if Shin Yoosung’s soul came from another worldline, all souls ultimately passed through the ‘afterlife’ to leave this world.
I thought of several constellations associated with the afterlife.
But all of them were either somewhere I dared not approach, or possessed a Status so high that my present self could never establish a connection with them.
There was, however, one I might be able to work something out with.
“Could you perhaps call the ‘Lover of the Abandoned Labyrinth’?”
At my words, Yoo Sangah hesitated briefly, then nodded.
A little later, faint sparks flickered around her.
Because of the probability spent last time, this wasn’t a direct descent, but I could clearly tell that Ariadne was faintly present within Yoo Sangah.
I spoke.
“Olympus. I want to make a deal with you.”
The sparks around her grew violent.
Well, that was understandable, considering how badly our last meeting had gone.
But this time, I had to yield.
I took a short breath, then went straight to the point.
“Let me meet your King of the Underworld (冥王).”
Now it was time to keep my second promise.
I could tell immediately from Yoo Sangah’s expression what Olympus’s answer was. Only after watching her face turn red, then pale, then finally blue did I think I had brought it up too hastily.
“Um······ Dokja-ssi.”
What sort of vicious curses had she heard? Yoo Sangah looked at me and hesitated for a long time. I found myself feeling sorry.
“Could you tell me what your constellation sponsors said?”

Electricity crackled from Yoo Sangah’s body. Ariadne seemed to be throwing quite a fit. I waited a little for things to calm down. I hadn’t known our previous exchange of three questions and answers would have such far-reaching consequences.
At last, the sparks subsided, and Yoo Sangah spoke with a sigh in her voice.
“She says the ‘Father of the Rich Night’ isn’t someone she can just bring here······.”
Father of the Rich Night.
That was the modifier of ‘Hades, King of the Underworld’, one of Olympus’s three chief gods.
A constellation who was one of Olympus’s three chief gods, but whose permanent residence in the Underworld excluded him from the ‘Twelve Olympians’, the nebula’s great constellations.
Well, Hades’s Status might be too high for Ariadne, a mere Historical-grade constellation, to make contact with him.
For the moment, I expressed my thanks.
“Thank you, Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
“But Dokja-ssi, are you perhaps······.”
Clever as she was, Yoo Sangah would already have known that the ‘Father of the Rich Night’ was Hades.
She probably had some inkling of why I was seeking him too.
After all, the story of Orpheus, who went to the Underworld to bring his wife Eurydice back to life, was a famous myth even in Korea.
“······Is it possible?”
In principle, bringing the dead back to life was impossible.

I received a probability correction through the effect of ‘King of No Killing’, but in most cases there was no such correction. Shin Yoosung was no exception. If indiscriminate resurrection had been possible in the first place, Yoo Joonghyuk wouldn’t have needed to regress.
But if I could somehow get my hands on her soul······.
“I can’t explain the details right now. I’m sorry.”
I didn’t want to spell out all my future plans while every constellation was watching. This incident had increased the number of constellations who disliked me, too.
I had made my move. The other side would take the bait.
What mattered now was patience.
I turned to the companions around me and spoke.
“Shall we get things in order first?”

As though they had been waiting, my companions approached one by one. Lee Gilyoung, glancing at Shin Yoosung; Jung Heewon, supporting Lee Hyunsung; Lee Jihye, who had been standing apart with a slightly sulky expression.
A lower-grade dokkaebi’s voice sounded from the air.
[I am dokkaebi ‘Youngki’, temporarily assigned to handle reward settlement.]
Apparently a newcomer, the dokkaebi continued in a somewhat stiff voice.
[I will now settle the additional rewards for the fifth scenario.]
With all the higher-ranking dokkaebis gone, it seemed the unwanted work had been dumped on this one.
[You have received ‘Ellain Forest’s Vital Force’.]
Everyone caught one of the little fruits falling from the air.

[What you have just received is the most widely used recovery medicine in the ‘Star Stream’. Even if you have suffered serious injuries, eating it and going to sleep will allow you to recover quickly, so please eat it and get plenty of rest.]
I had never encountered such a polite dokkaebi before, and it almost made me uncomfortable. Looking at me and several others, the dokkaebi continued.
[Additional rewards for the main contributors will be distributed this evening. Thank you all for your efforts, and I wish you the best in the next scenario.]
The voice vanished, and I looked at my companions holding their fruits.

More characters I didn’t know would have died, and someone was probably dying even now. But we had survived. My companions looked as though they didn’t know whether to be grateful for that or to grieve.
At times like this, someone had to take the lead.
Looking at each of them in turn, I slowly spoke.
“You all worked hard.”
A moment in which nothing was decided would ultimately remain just that: a moment in which nothing was decided.
What was sad was sad, and what was happy was happy.
If you at least decided something, that moment would remain meaningful.
“You really worked hard.”
Relief slowly spread across my companions’ faces, as though my insignificant words were a reward in themselves.
They deserved it.
Only then did the corners of Lee Jihye’s mouth begin to twitch, and she was the first to speak.
“······You were seriously awesome back there, ajusshi. A tiny bit cooler than my master, even. I’ll give you that.”
Her words prompted Lee Hyunsung and Jung Heewon to speak up too.
“······That was truly incredible.”
“Even I found that satisfying to watch.”
······Had these people been holding back until they could talk about that?
I smiled wryly as my companions began talking excitedly.
We had overcome the greatest crisis of the early scenarios, and Seoul had been protected.
At least for a while, until a few more scenarios had passed, Seoul would face no threat.
“You worked hard too, Dokja-ssi.”
Yoo Sangah, who had been quietly watching me from beside me, smiled brightly.
Perhaps this was the reward I had been given.

Something bumped into me with a soft thud, and I found Shin Yoosung resting her forehead against my waist. Lee Gilyoung looked vaguely displeased, but said nothing in particular. I gently rested a hand on Shin Yoosung’s head.
······Yes, this too.
Evening came, and the additional rewards for the major contributors began to be distributed.
There were three major contributors eligible for the additional rewards.
Me, Jung Heewon, and Yoo Joonghyuk.
[The additional reward for the fifth scenario is a ‘B-grade skill.’]
After everything we'd been through, getting just one B-grade skill as a reward might sound unbalanced to someone, but the balance was fine.
A low letter grade didn't mean all the skills were crap.
Above all, this scenario's reward came in the form of a ‘free choice.’
In other words, I could choose any one B-grade skill I wanted.
Even among B-grade skills, some were difficult to acquire, and I had to use this opportunity to get one.
[Would you like to view the list of B-grade skills?]
A list of tens of thousands of skills.
I didn't get stuck trying to choose because I'd had a skill in mind from the start.
[Would you like to receive the B-grade skill ‘Lie Detection’ as your reward?]
When I nodded, a faint glow spread, and another message appeared.
[The exclusive skill ‘Lie Detection’ has been added to your skill list.]
Ha. I'd finally gotten it.
Thinking of how frustrating it had been all this time without [Lie Detection], honestly······.
When I looked over, Jung Heewon was also busily choosing something.
I asked Lee Jihye, who was beside me.
“Hey, do you know where Yoo Joonghyuk went?”
“Oh, he was taking Seolhwa-unnie somewhere earlier.”
······With Lee Seolhwa?
As though she could tell what I was thinking, Lee Jihye gave me a look that said I was pathetic.
“······Ugh, it's not what you're thinking, ajusshi.”
“Seriously. I've been watching them the whole time. There's absolutely nothing between those two. I'm sure of it.”

I tilted my head. Come to think of it, I was sure about the second round, but I couldn't quite remember whether they'd become lovers in the third round. Yoo Joonghyuk had taken the eunuch route more often than one might think.
Then where on earth had he gone? To pick up his little sister?
[The sixth scenario will begin in three days.]
Then I heard a system message.
Somehow, I thought I knew what Yoo Joonghyuk had gone off to do.
In the sixth scenario, we would finally encounter incarnations from other domes.
Since he couldn't rest for even a moment, he'd probably gone to acquire some hidden skills and items he'd missed in his previous rounds.
There were still quite a few hidden scenarios left in the Seoul Dome.
It stung a little to have Yoo Joonghyuk snatch them away, but that was still better than some random bastard getting the skills.
Besides, he needed to become even stronger than he was now if we were going to clear the remaining scenarios easily.
“Oh, right. Master told me to pass a message on to you earlier, ajusshi.”
“To me?”
Lee Jihye nodded, then her expression suddenly hardened. She gripped the hilt of her sword and spoke in a solemn tone.
“Kim Dokja, the oath's term has ended.”
I felt my heart plummet.
The existence oath.
With everything going on, I'd completely forgotten.
―Swear you won't hurt me until the fifth scenario ends. If you can't even do that, I really can't help you.
―I swear.
Come to think of it, he'd sworn that oath.
That bastard······ Was that oath why he hadn't killed me all this time?
Come to think of it, he'd said something strange back then, too.
―I won't kill you. But I will hit you once.
I swallowed without realizing it.
Surely his current absence had nothing to do with that?
Had he gone to learn some monstrous skill that could finish me off in a single blow?
“But······ what kind of oath did you two make?”
“Shut up.”
Right. There was no need to get scared already.
Above all, I now had the [Beast King’s Sensitivity] Shin Yoosung had used.
At level 3, no less.
······I also had [Way of the Wind], even if I used it through Bookmark, and strong companions besides.
When our eyes met, Lee Jihye smirked.
“You know I won't help you no matter what Master does, right?”
“I wasn't expecting anything from you.”
Instead, I looked toward the dependable Lee Hyunsung.
I hadn't said it at the time, but when he'd answered Shin Yoosung's question by saying he was my companion rather than Yoo Joonghyuk's, I'd been truly moved.
Lee Hyunsung gave me an uncomfortable look for a moment, then spoke.
“Um······ Dokja-ssi.”
“Yes?”
“To be honest, I'm a little afraid of Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi.”
“······Oh, it's all right. I understand.”
Come to think of it, Lee Hyunsung had become this strong because Yoo Joonghyuk had put him through hell.
Damn it.
But it was too early to despair.
I also had Jung Heewon.
A companion I'd nurtured with my own hands, who had never gotten her chance to shine in the original novel.
Then Jung Heewon scratched her cheek and said,
“I don't know why, but my sponsor says not to get involved if you two fight.”
“She says not to get in your way······ What on earth does that mean?”
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ smiles with satisfaction.]
A sudden chill ran down my spine.
What on earth was that damn angel thinking?
[The constellation ‘Scribe of Heaven’ keeps a stern watch on ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire.’]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ flinches and changes her expression.]
“Dokja-ssi.”
I turned with a start to find Yoo Sangah watching me with a calm smile.
“Don't worry. Joonghyuk-ssi didn't seem like such a bad person, either.”
“······I really hope you're right.”
“I'm sure you can become good friends.”
I quietly sighed at Yoo Sangah's naive words.
I didn't know why Han Sooyoung came to mind at times like this.
Apart from me, she was the only one who knew what kind of bastard Yoo Joonghyuk was.
Well, even if she'd been here, she wouldn't have protected me······.
The scenario was over now. I wondered what she was doing.
We finished tidying up the area and collected the items.
Even late into the night, Yoo Joonghyuk didn't return.
Instead, Jung Heewon returned from scouting the area with something I was glad to see.
Surprised, I asked,
“There was still some of that left?”
Jung Heewon had brought a six-pack of plastic beer bottles and some bottles of soju. She smiled and said,
“At a time like this, we should have a drink. To celebrate.”
We lit a bonfire and sat huddled around it. I slapped the back of Lee Jihye's hand as she quickly reached for the beer.
“You're a minor.”
“······There aren't even any laws anymore. Why are you going on about me being a minor?”
“Have soda with the kids.”

While we bickered, we quickly got through a round of drinks. Jung Heewon began rambling drunkenly, her cheeks oddly flushed, while Lee Hyunsung had a couple of glasses of beer and started snoring like a bear. Apparently, they couldn't hold their liquor as well as I'd have guessed from looking at them.
“Feeels so gooood······.”

Even Lee Jihye, her face bright red from however many drinks she'd sneaked, flopped backward. Yoo Sangah, who was surprisingly a heavy drinker, had already opened her fourth bottle of soju and was sipping it. Her face showed no sign of intoxication at all.
“I can hold my liquor.”
Come to think of it, I'd never seen Yoo Sangah drunk at a company dinner.
“······It would be a problem if I let myself get drunk.”

The sorrow in those words saddened me. The company had been crawling with nothing but bastards who wanted to get Yoo Sangah drunk and take advantage of her. Perhaps this was the first time she'd ever been able to drink without worrying.
“But today should be all right, shouldn't it?”
Perhaps because her face seemed paler than usual, I felt inexplicably awkward and avoided her eyes.
A lonely moon hung in the sky, and for once, no monsters could be heard howling. Other groups around us were also drinking, their noisy voices filling the area.
I wondered how they could drink in a situation like this, but then I also wondered if a situation like this left them no choice but to drink.
It was a world none of us could endure without a drink.
That was when a small spark leaped over my glass.
Crackle, crack-crackle.
Startled, Yoo Sangah looked at me.
I nodded.
As I'd thought, it was a good thing I hadn't had any alcohol.
The liquor spilled out and traced letters on the ground, as though playing a prank.
[The constellation ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’ wishes to speak with you.]
At last, Olympus had taken the bait.
God of Wine and Ecstasy.
The only one in Olympus who would use a modifier like that was Dionysus, one of the twelve Olympians.
[The constellation ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’ hums.]
I couldn't hear the tune, but I could see the spilled drops of liquor dancing to some melody. Moving as though they were alive, the drops wove countless musical notes across the ground.
The notes moved back and forth between Yoo Sangah and me.
After studying the notes, Yoo Sangah spoke.
“It's the Puppy Waltz.”
“You can read music, too?”
“A little.”
Yoo Sangah tilted her head and continued.
“Why Chopin all of a sudden? What could it mean?”

How would I know? It was strange that Dionysus even knew Chopin in the first place. No, wait. According to the original novel, he was a constellation with a keen interest in the musical culture of later eras, so perhaps it wasn't strange.
The notes traced cute little circles like a puppy's dance steps, then all formed arrows pointing toward the remaining soju bottles. Yoo Sangah said,
“······I think he's telling us to drink more?”
“Let's try drinking, then.”
No matter how I looked at it, there was no other way to interpret it.
“Just have a little, Yoo Sangah-ssi. At least one of us needs to keep a clear head.”
If I got wasted, someone would have to protect our companions.
In a pinch, I could wake Lee Gilyoung and Shin Yoosung, who had fallen asleep after drinking soda, but I wanted to let them sleep soundly, at least for tonight.
“Can't you hold your liquor, Dokja-ssi?”
“Not particularly well.”
I lightly clinked glasses with Yoo Sangah, then knocked back a glass of soju.
It had been a while since I'd had alcohol, and I felt its warm burn in my stomach.
But the notes still didn't stop.
“······I think he's telling you to drink more.”

I had several more glasses in quick succession. Heat rose from my stomach, and I soon felt my face flushing red. The notes moved even more energetically. Or did they just look that way because I was drunk? Yoo Sangah smiled.
“Still, it's nice to drink together. I was feeling a little lonely.”
How many more glasses had I drunk like that? A pleasant buzz came over me, and my mood improved a little, too. When I happened to look over, Yoo Sangah was much closer to me.
There had definitely been quite a gap between us earlier······.
Was I imagining it? I could hear heavy breathing.
I couldn't tell whether it was mine or Yoo Sangah's.
Yoo Sangah's shoulder lightly brushed mine.
“Dokja-ssi.”
“Yes?”
Skin with scarcely a blemish, though she surely wasn't wearing makeup.
Looking slightly dazed, Yoo Sangah was slowly leaning toward me.
Her face drawing closer and closer.
Quarter notes and eighth notes paired off, circling us in a frenzied dance. Perhaps it was the soft sensation against my shoulder, but my heart suddenly began to race.
······Something was strange here.
[The exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ reduces your intoxication.]
With the message, I suddenly came to my senses, my head clearing.
Right. There was no way something like this would happen in reality.
The ever-careful Yoo Sangah, in such an unguarded state.
This was only possible because it was ‘Ways of Survival.’
I firmly gripped Yoo Sangah's shoulders and said,
“Yoo Sangah-ssi, get a hold of yourself.”
“What? Ah······ Huh?”
Suddenly startled, Yoo Sangah blinked.
For the first time, her face flushed red, though even the alcohol hadn't changed its color.
“Wh-what was I······.”
As I'd thought, Yoo Sangah hadn't been acting of her own accord.
Feeling a little miserable, I addressed the notes circling on the ground.
“I'd appreciate it if you stopped playing games and got to the point.”
At that moment, all the notes stopped at once.
An ominous silence fell, as though a midnight festival had abruptly come to a halt.
The drinks we were having all tipped over, and the drops pooling on the ground crackled with sparks.
Soon, the drops formed a line of text.
―You're a killjoy.
I was a little startled by the words written on the ground.
You might ask what was so impressive about writing a few words with drops of liquor, but in the world of ‘Ways of Survival,’ a constellation conveying its ‘intent’ really was that impressive.
There was a reason so many constellations used dokkaebi channels to send ‘indirect messages.’

Only the very highest beings among the constellations could convey their intent to the world below without the help of a constellation sponsor or a dokkaebi, and even then, the probability cost was enormous. That was how sensitive this world's probability was to ‘language.’
A faint cry came from the ‘Great Hole’ in the sky.
It seemed an Outer God had noticed Dionysus's presence, too.

Since he'd chosen to communicate directly instead of through an incarnation, he probably felt confident he could handle the consequences······ So one of the twelve Olympians really was in a different league, was he?
I deliberately spoke as though to provoke him.
“If you're so confident, why don't you come here and speak in person?”
The line of text moved.
―I don't like those tentacled bastards.
He wouldn't admit he'd lose even if it killed him.
―Fighting is a bother, too. And if I came down myself, everyone would die.
To be honest, I hadn't expected him to. And if a constellation on the level of the twelve Olympians really descended, Seoul would be pulverized on the spot.
―That's how my father killed my mother, too.
After reading that sentence, Yoo Sangah whispered to me.
“······What does that mean?”
“He's probably talking about the myth of his birth.”
As far as I knew, Dionysus's parents were Zeus and Semele, the princess of Thebes.
Jealous of Zeus and Semele's relationship, Hera disguised herself as Semele's nurse one day and urged her on with these words.
‘Zeus-nim might be an impostor. Ask him to show you his true form, the one he takes on Olympus.’
Falling for the trick, Semele really did make that request of Zeus, and soon afterward, she was struck by the radiance of Zeus's true body (眞體) and burned to death.
Listening to my account, Yoo Sangah tilted her head.
“Um······ That's a little different from the tradition I know. As far as I know, his mother wasn't the princess of Thebes, but······.”
I was a little surprised by Yoo Sangah's knowledge.
Enough to suspect she held a level 1 certificate in mythological history as well as Korean history. Of course, no such certificate existed.
As though amused, the line of text changed its words.
―Hmm. You humans know quite a bit about me.

I asked Dionysus,
“Now I'm curious. Which of those two traditions is true?”
―Does that matter?

Dionysus, son of Persephone.
If that tradition was the right one, there was a good chance Dionysus could put me in contact with Persephone, Hades's wife.
―What an insolent human.
The drops of liquor forming the text trembled.
―But I like insolent humans.
In fact, I already knew which tradition was true.
Dionysus's story was briefly mentioned in ‘Ways of Survival,’ too.
―There was once another human as reckless as you. He played the lyre very beautifully. But he didn't come to a good end, either.
“I'll be different.”

Dionysus was a constellation whose thoughts were impossible to fathom.
―Remember. You have only 12 hours. If you fail to return within that time, you will never be able to return to the scenario you lived in.
My vision swam as the dizziness grew worse. A sudden drowsiness came over me. I realized what was about to happen.

―I hope ‘Father of the Rich Night’ takes a liking to you.
[The constellation ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’ guides your soul.]

Countless colors spread through my mind as though I'd taken drugs. A throbbing pain rose in my forehead, and faint voices came from all around.
[Who is that?]
[······Interesting.]

[You will regret this.]
Murmuring voices.

A little later, I felt I'd arrived somewhere.
It was hard to move, but I had a rough idea of the scene I'd see when I opened my eyes.
The clammy air of the Underworld.
Pitch-black sand clinging to my fingertips.
I was probably on a riverbank in the Underworld ruled by Hades.
There would be the River Acheron leading to Hades's palace, and Charon, the ferryman of the dead, would be waiting for me. And······.
“Hey! Get up! What are you doing here?”

Something blunt struck my head, and a pitch-black, oil-like substance poured over my body. Coughing and spluttering, I got to my feet. Someone patted me down, then grabbed my collar and hoisted me up.

I'd never seen his face before, either.
A sinister-looking man with bulging muscles all over his body. The people around us watched me dangling in the air and sneered.

“Hey, hey, don't mess with him. If he ended up here, he can't be ordinary. Did you forget that lunatic who arrived a little while ago?”
“Oh, that bastard was a special kind of crazy. You think guys like him are common?”
I let the men run their mouths and examined my surroundings.
A vast space filled with sweltering heat.
Judging by the swarming spirits, this did at least seem to be the Underworld.

Metal frameworks made from Underworld metal stood here and there, and I could see furnaces for smelting metal. The place felt like an enormous factory. Spirits who had done nothing but work themselves to the bone in the living world until they died were now slaves of the Underworld, making something even after death.
At a glance, it looked like a giant robot······.
What did they do here?
“Hey, are you ignoring me?”
I really did ignore him as I slowly bent his arm back.
“Wh-what the hell! How is this bastard so strong······!”
I had no time to waste on small fry like these.
I decided to first check the hidden scenario that had arrived.
<Hidden Scenario ― Underworld Walk>
Category : Hidden
Difficulty : A+
Clear Conditions : Evade the judges' watch and find a way to return safely to the world above.
Time Limit : 12 hours
Reward : 10000 coins
Failure : You will be forcibly made a resident of the Underworld.
······The right scenario had arrived.

Then why was I here?
I should definitely have landed on the banks of the Acheron.
“Y-you bastard! Who the hell do you think we······!”
Just as the man's huge fist was about to come at me, a sharp voice rang out from behind.
“Hey, what's going on over there? Something fun?”
“A-aaaargh!”
“Haha, let me join in. Huh? I'm bored to death from messing with nothing but Gundams here every day.”
“Run! Everyone, run!”
All the men who had surrounded me began to flee.
Swift movements, like herbivores encountering a predator.
I looked toward the voice.
A slender young man with long bangs covering his face.
Spotting me standing there alone, the young man approached.
He studied me closely, then muttered in surprise.
“······Why are you here?”
For a moment, I didn't understand what he meant.
······Who was this bastard, and why was he acting like he knew me?
“What, you don't recognize me? Did you really forget?”
Only when the young man lifted his bangs a little did I recognize him.
······Damn it.
Come to think of it, the Underworld was, after all, where dead people came.
I hadn't considered it.
The fact that, naturally, the bastard I'd killed would have come here, too.
“Ah, don't be so wary. We're both fucking dead already anyway, aren't we?”
His curious eyes suddenly came closer.
A vicious, cruel gaze.
I'd only seen him briefly, but it was an impression I could never forget.
With a sinister smile, he continued.
“So, who the hell killed you, ajusshi? Spit it out. Huh?”
The Delusion Demon Kim Namwoon, who had died in the first scenario, was in Hades's Underworld.
Only after thoroughly examining my surroundings for a while did I reach a conclusion about where I was.
And despaired.
Damn it. There was no mistaking it. This place was······.

Looking at the smirking Kim Namwoon, I let out a quiet sigh.

This was the prison of ‘Tartarus,’ the hell of the Underworld.

Kim Namwoon chattered away as though he were a tour guide to hell.

‘Ways of Survival’ said so, too.
The deeper the level of Tartarus, the stronger the prisoners held there, so the Cerberus guarding each level grew larger the farther down you went.
Kim Namwoon snickered and asked,
“So, how does it feel to be in hell?”
Wary of his swaggering attitude, I spoke.
There was no telling when this psychopath might turn on me, so I had to stay on guard.
“I have a question.”
“What?”
“Is there anyone else here besides you?”
“You're here, ajusshi.”
“Besides me.”
I closely examined the faces of the passing spirits.
But I saw no faces I knew.
For example, people like Myung Ilsang, the Disaster of Questions, or Song Minwoo, the non-human.
“Not that I know of. Of the people on that subway train, I'm the only one who came here.”
Hades's Underworld was only one of the countless afterlives in the world.

Myung Ilsang and Song Minwoo were probably no different.
Watching Kim Namwoon's reaction, I continued.
“Has a young woman come here recently, by any chance?”
“A young woman?”
“White hair, and, um······ a ponytail. She's quite pretty.”

“Aha, now I get it.”
I listened closely, wondering if he'd seen Shin Yoosung.

There was a chance she hadn't crossed the Acheron yet, though······.
Since her soul came from another worldline, she would only stay here briefly before being expelled beyond the worldline.
My job was to get hold of her soul before that happened.

A Giant Soldier (巨身兵).
Sure enough, it seemed Hades was already preparing for <Gigantomachia>.
He really was different from the twelve Olympians, who loafed around eating and fucking while using preparations for <Gigantomachia> as an excuse.
Come to think of it, Hades was a constellation of Greek mythology, but he didn't belong to the Olympus nebula.
That was when I heard a commotion outside the entrance.
Kim Namwoon's expression turned serious, and he grabbed my shoulder.
“Come here. Come with me.”
“Why?”
“Can't you see the overseers coming? I've set up a work area over there, so go and at least pretend to hammer something. Newcomers have to move fast. Got it?”
I knew that much myself. If this really was the ‘slave forge’ of Tartarus, I had a rough idea of how it worked.
So Tartarus wasn't what had surprised me.
Kim Namwoon stuck out his lower lip.
“Why are you looking at me like that?”

Kim Namwoon seemed to think for a moment, then an unsettling smile crossed his face.

To think someone could describe the hell of ‘Tartarus’ like that.
“And when I'm bored, I can build Gunpla. How great is that?”
Calling a Giant Soldier Gunpla.
“It's all thanks to you, ajusshi. I mean it. Seriously, thank you.”
This bastard really was insane.
[The character ‘Kim Namwoon’ feels favorably toward you.]
Damn it. With even a system message like that appearing, I had to believe him.
“Anyway, hurry over here. We don't have time!”
Kim Namwoon led me toward his work area.
The tools he'd been using were neatly arranged on the workbench, and I could also see ‘Gunpla’ he'd made from leftover metal.
Doing something like this with Underworld metal.
It brought home to me all over again that this bastard had been written as a chuunibyou.
“They're coming. Pick up a hammer.”
No sooner had he spoken than the Cerberus at the gates of hell began to bark.
Grrrrr······!

The moment I heard it, I felt my joints stiffen with a chill. Passing through the gate guarded by Cerberus, overseers entered Tartarus, each carrying a club in one hand and a whip in the other. Hades's servants, clad in pitch-black capes. They didn't look as strong as the judges, but it still wouldn't be good to be discovered.
Standing awkwardly, I pretended to hammer a few times.
Kim Namwoon snickered beside me.

―Attention, slaves of the first level. A surprise inspection will now take place.
Kim Namwoon frowned and grumbled.

―An illegal intruder has entered the Underworld. We are told someone crossed the Acheron as the soul of a living person.
The spirits holding hammers and saws murmured with confused expressions.

―If the Great Death learns of this, terrible things will happen to you as well. Therefore, this inspection is intended to root out that impure intruder. For now, it is merely a formality, so do not be nervous. Everyone remain where you are.
Damn it. Things were moving faster than I'd expected.
Of all times······.
I heard Kim Namwoon mutter through clenched teeth.
“What a load of stupid bullshit. Even if someone alive came here, why would they hide in ‘Tartarus’? Once you get in, you can never get out. Right?”
“Hey, ajusshi?”
“Uh, yeah.”
Lost in thought, I'd answered a beat too late.
Kim Namwoon stared at me for a moment, then spoke in a dumbfounded voice.
“I'm only asking just in case. They're not talking about you, are······.”
“They are.”
“Oh, fuck.”
Kim Namwoon threw down his hammer and laughed in disbelief.
“Wow, you really know how to blindside someone. Have I been whining about my lot to a living person this whole time?”
I couldn't tell whether he was angry or amused.
I sighed and asked,
“······Is there anywhere to hide here?”

“I'm only nice to dead people. What a shame, just when we're seeing each other again after so long. You'll be fucking dead soon, too, so I'll be nice to you again then.”
Kim Namwoon spoke as though my predicament served me right, drawing the edge of his hand across his throat.
While we exchanged this nonsense, the overseer had already drawn near.
If the Giant Soldier had been complete, I could have ridden it, beaten Cerberus down, and headed straight for Hades's palace, but even that wasn't possible now.
[Your attribute effect improves your recall of pages you have already read!]

What had he done then?
「“Tell the King of the Underworld that I'm taking Giant Soldier Pluto.”」
「“Tell them all to fuck off if they don't want to die.”」
······Damn it. That crazy bastard, so satisfying to read.
It had been great to read, but now that I was in this situation myself, it was no help at all.
Taking on Hades's judges head-on.
Only a regressor like Yoo Joonghyuk could do that. He had both the strength and the chances for it. But I······.
······No, wait a minute.
What was stopping me from doing what he'd done?
With that sudden change in approach, my thoughts took a different direction.
Of course, I couldn't actually act like him.

Because I'd fail the hidden scenario and become a ‘resident of the Underworld’?

I'd been a fool.

At last, the overseer reached our work area.
Instead, I stepped forward.
The overseer asked,

A sharp, metallic sound began to ring out from somewhere. I felt as though my body was gradually freezing, and soon a chill settled on the back of my neck.
If I looked back now, I'd probably find one of Hades's judges gripping my neck.
Resisting the cold that seemed to freeze my very bones, I spoke.
“It looks like you're going to annihilate me. You'd better think carefully.”
I didn't have Yoo Joonghyuk's strength.

“Because if you kill me now, you're certain to lose <Gigantomachia>.”
The overseer's gaze wavered for an instant, and the cold briefly eased. Seizing that opening, I looked toward the Giant Soldier and spoke.
“Tell ‘Father of the Rich Night’ that I know how to complete that Giant Soldier.”
Then a terrible silence fell. My body was slowly freezing outward from the back of my neck, but I deliberately didn't resist.
This was a test.
Before I knew it, the ice had spread past my neck and shoulders, down to my chest.
I didn't panic.
A little longer. Just a little longer.
And finally, just as the cold was about to seep in around my heart.
The chill stopped, as if by magic.

[The hidden scenario's details have been updated.]
A little later, guided by the judge, I began making my way up through Hades's palace.
Beyond the growling Cerberus, I could see Kim Namwoon receding into the distance.

Well, enjoy your stay in hell, Namwoon.

A whisper too quiet for the judge to hear.
‘I know you're listening.’
This was Hades's Underworld, not the world above.
I was curious.
Would a dokkaebi's ‘channel’ really function properly even here?

―······Yes. I'm watching.
The channel's Dokkaebi Communication.

―Yes. I'm the lower-grade dokkaebi ‘Youngki.’ Elder Bihyung has briefly left the channel on Bureau business, so I'm filling in.
The dokkaebi Youngki. Probably the rookie dokkaebi who'd had the scenario reward settlement dumped on them earlier that day. I got straight to the point.
‘Why aren't you doing your job properly?’
―Pardon?
‘The hidden scenario was updated. Why aren't you telling me about it?’
Having come to a place this terrifying, I should at least make sure I got my hidden scenario rewards.
―Ah, th-that's······!
Judging by that flustered response, this really did seem to be a rookie.

It dawned on me just how good Bihyung was at his job. I'd thought he was just a dim-witted, inept dokkaebi······. But after about ten seconds of silence, the dokkaebi Youngki suddenly began to stammer.
―Um, e-excuse me······.
‘What now?’
―How do you update a scenario?
For a moment, I was speechless.
‘What kind of dokkaebi asks an incarnation that?’

Where her gaze fell, the image of Kim Dokja could be seen, making his way through the darkness to leave the Underworld.
Kim Dokja, moving forward as he struggled to avoid looking back, even by accident.

The Abandoned World
Guided by the judge, I headed toward the Underworld's exit.
I was wearing a special blindfold, so I couldn't tell exactly where I was. It felt as though we were going up, but also as though we were going down.
In any case, only after we had walked for quite some time did the judge remove my blindfold.
[Follow this path.]
When I opened my eyes, I saw a narrow, dark side path.
This was probably the exit that led out of the Underworld without going through Charon, the ferryman.
[You would do well to find ‘ahead.’]
“What does that mean?”
When I looked back, the judge was already gone.

With no other choice, I walked along the side path. Soon, the light around me faded, and complete darkness settled in. At first, I could tell which way I was going by feeling along the wall, but before long, even that wall disappeared.
With nothing left to rely on, I felt like a ship adrift on a boundless sea without a buoy in sight.
The myth of Orpheus suddenly came to mind.
What would happen to me if I looked back here?
That was when faint, luminous writing appeared in the darkness.
[You're afraid of what's behind you. That poor child was, too.]
It was a message from Persephone.
[But remember this. To find ‘ahead,’ you must know where ‘behind’ is. After all, ‘ahead’ can only exist when there is a ‘behind.’]
Come to think of it, the judge had said something similar.
But hearing something that sounded profound wasn't enough to make me suddenly attain enlightenment and undergo some tremendous change.
[It seems you need a little motivation······.]
The strings of luminous letters hanging in the air stretched out, as though hesitating.
[Very well. She's already at the entrance to the labyrinth that crosses worldlines, so I cannot bring her here right away, but I can manage this much.]
Just as I wondered—could it be?
The strings of letters vanished all at once, and something small and faint, like a firefly, appeared before my eyes.
A distant light.
A very fragile, gentle light.
No one told me, but I knew what that light was.
It was Shin Yoosung from the 41st round.
I could tell from her voice alone.
How long she had been waiting.

If she was already at the threshold of crossing worldlines, time there would work differently from here. From my perspective, it hadn't been long since I sent Shin Yoosung off, but for her, years might already have passed.
The little light trembled again and again, then hesitated over something before cautiously speaking.
―Ajusshi.
She seemed to have been influenced by the young Shin Yoosung's memories.
―······I-I can call you that too, right? No··· may I?
A form of address was a bond. A desire to be tied to something. Perhaps that word, ‘ajusshi,’ was the last lingering attachment of Shin Yoosung from the 41st round. I smiled faintly and spoke.
“You're older than me now. Are you sure that's okay?”
The gentle light quivered once more.
As though playing, the light lightly touched my cheek, then drew away.
That simple warmth, that gesture······.
My heart hurt as though it were being torn apart.
She must have waited a long time.
And yet this child would have to wait longer.
“I'm sorry. I can't save you right away.”
The little light bobbed gently up and down, as though she understood.
―Don't push yourself. My story is already······.
“It isn't over.”
I spoke without giving her a chance to continue.
“After suffering for so many years, you can't let it end like this.”
“I'll never let that happen.”
The light looked at me and spoke.
With a plaintive tremor, as though confused.
―I came to know you through the memories of this world, ajusshi. But you······ why are you so good to me? You don't really know me, do you?
I didn't answer.
We had come to know each other through different mediums.
Just as Shin Yoosung from the 41st round had come to know me through her younger self's memories, I knew her through ‘Ways of Survival.’ And yet I couldn't properly explain that to her.
―It feels strange. I know I don't really know you, ajusshi, but when I'm with you, I feel completely understood. As though I'm standing before a ‘god’······.
If I really were a god, I'd be the most incompetent god in the world.
The feeling of being the world's most powerless god, knowing everything but unable to explain anything.
Shin Yoosung's light was rapidly fading.
Though I couldn't see her, I felt as though I knew what expression she was wearing.
―······Save me, ······please.
“I will.”
The tail of light wavering in the air grew smaller and smaller, and I reached out to touch it.
It felt as though my heart was being squeezed.
Shin Yoosung's despair. That long wait······.
An indescribable sorrow cut through my heart like a knife.
Little by little, I began to understand Persephone's words. That only with a ‘behind’ could I move ‘ahead.’
This was my ‘behind,’ and at the same time, the ‘ahead’ I had to move toward.
Perhaps Yoo Joonghyuk had felt this way, too. He kept returning to the past, yet could move forward only by returning.
The moment I became certain of my direction, my surroundings slowly began to distort.
Strings of luminous letters appeared over the dispersing darkness.
[I've held her back for a little while with my power, but if you want to save her, you have almost no time left.]
I remembered the faint warmth of Shin Yoosung that lingered in my hand.
Persephone spoke.
[Remember. A human being is a ‘story.’ So when you recover her, no one knows how much of her story will remain.]
With those final words, I was sucked away somewhere.
Aaaaah.
The wails of the spirits receded, and the vivid sensations of my body returned one by one.
Bright sunlight pierced my eyelids.
Feeling how damp my back had become, I opened my eyes with a start and saw a familiar face.
“······Ajusshi?”
The young Shin Yoosung was looking at me. The child's clear eyes. Those eyes gave me certainty. My pounding heart gradually settled.
I was back.
As I slowly caught my breath, the muscles throughout my body began working properly again.
[Hidden Scenario ― ‘Queen of the Underworld’ has ended.]

Fwoosh-fwoosh-fwoosh!

Boom-boom-boom-boom!

Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship (破天劍道).
Ultimate Technique (絶技).
Breaking the Sky Mad Emperor Technique (破天狂皇武).
The flash extending from the tip of Yoo Joonghyuk’s sword split into dozens of rays, slashing one of the snake’s heads to shreds.
Bzzzzzt!
Ghastly black blood spurted from the wounds inflicted by Totsuka-no-tsurugi, and one of the eight heads began to rot.
The only sword capable of killing Yamata no Orochi.
Since Yoo Joonghyuk wasn’t a constellation, 「Stage Transformation」 didn’t occur, but the effect imbued in the sword was unmistakable.
[The constellation, ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads,’ howls.]
One head had been severed, but Yamata no Orochi was still going strong.
To kill it, all eight heads had to be cut off.

Without hesitation, Yoo Joonghyuk leaped toward the second head. His fighting was so spectacular that there wasn’t even an opening for me to intervene. His prowess was astonishing as he zigzagged past the blood-red tails and heads, severing necks.
There was a reason the protagonist was the protagonist.
And Ways of Survival was a place where even someone like him died hundreds upon hundreds of times.
This world feels horrifying all over again.

Raaaaaar!

The moment the snake’s four remaining heads looked at me, I picked up Totsuka-no-tsurugi from the ground and ran toward Orochi.

[Activation Duration: 3 minutes]
[Your understanding of the character is considerable, but the character’s level is too high. Only some skills will be activated.]

[This skill can only be used by a ‘small person.’]

「The breadth of perception determines the Status of a being, for even in the smallest thing, one can behold the vastest universe.」

As the words Kyrgios had left in Ways of Survival flashed through my mind, the flow of magic power around me changed. Magic power became particles, and electrons resonating with one another began to vibrate violently.
「Within existence lies the Beginning (太初); thus, the smallest thing is the greatest.」

Bzzzzzt!

As I took my first step, a thunderous sound rang out. With my second step, the snake’s neck was right before my eyes. At my third step, space screamed beneath the White Pure lightning, and when I finally took my fourth step······.
I was already past Orochi, leaving a terrifying shock wave in my wake.
My feet trembled, lightning crackling around them, and blood poured from my nose and mouth.
I staggered as though my entire body had been electrocuted.

I frantically gulped down magic power recovery potions, steadying my trembling hand.
[The constellation, ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads,’ is appalled by your swordsmanship!]
Reduced to just one head in an instant, Orochi was writhing in pain.
[The constellation, ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads,’ questions the fairness of the scenario!]
Even as I staggered, I laughed.
“······Who’s talking to whom about fairness here?”
[Electrification] lasted three minutes, but with my body as it was, I wasn’t confident I could take more than three further steps.
In other words, I had to kill it within the next three steps.
Sparks flew in the air, and once again, that damned voice rang out.

The intermediate dokkaebi Ganul floated in the air, looking down at us.

Despite those words, Ganul didn’t seem particularly inclined to interfere.
[The constellation, ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads,’ howls in fury.]
[Hmm, throwing a tantrum won’t work this time. I understand how you feel, but you have used all the probability permitted in this scenario. ‘Those beings’ will no longer lend you their power.]
Yamata no Orochi’s aggrieved roar swept across all of [Peace Land].
For the Narrative-grade constellation Yamata no Orochi, this was probably a humiliation it had never experienced before.
Becoming a spectacle for someone else.
That this time, it was itself the victim of that spectacle.
Raaaaaaar!
Was it because of its anger? Though only one head remained, Orochi’s power was actually rising steadily.
“Protect the king!”
The flustered Japanese incarnations came running.
It had finally resorted to using even the power of the [Absolute Throne].
I heard a message from the dokkaebi ‘Youngki’ in my head.
―D-Dokja, sir. The channel is about to burst. I’ll block the indirect messages for a moment!
Now that I was even using Kyrgios’s power, constellations of every sort would have flocked here to watch me.
“Stop them!”
Having come to their senses, my companions rushed out to stop the disasters.
Covered in blood, Lee Hyunsung barely managed to get to his feet and took the lead, supported by the small people and Gong Pildu’s bombardment.
Meanwhile, Yamata no Orochi was preparing one last move to turn the tide.
[No, wait! Listen, constellation-nim! What are you······!]

Even though this wasn’t its true body, its stubborn refusal to lose to a mere incarnation like me was bringing about a real disaster. The dokkaebi belatedly exercised control over the system, but unfortunately, it was already too late.

Everyone gasped as they looked at the sky.

A sinister presence seething beyond the [Great Hole].
Chaos. Disorder. Emptiness. Something that was the origin of all those horrors.
That being was lending probability to Yamata no Orochi.
Bzzzzzt!

As probability that would not otherwise have been permitted was granted, the shadow of the one remaining snake’s head began to grow even larger. Larger, and larger still. Beyond the fortress, until it seemed to cover the entire planet.
[With a mere··· flood-control··· sword······!]

All those who had fallen to the ground, incarnation and small person alike, groaned and bled from all seven orifices of their heads. The terrifying difference in Status became an oppressive weight crushing my body. My knees were being forced toward the ground.

[A mere··· hu···man dares··· defy··· a great··· star······!]
I realize it instinctively.

The governing principle of the <Star Stream>: balance.
When someone destroys probability, someone else gains it.

Rrrrrumble!
A terrifying energy approaching at great speed from afar.

The Paradox Baekchung, Kyrgios Rodgraim.

Power no less formidable than that of a Narrative-grade constellation.

A face that looked happy, as though welcoming a long-awaited release.
To save one life, I kill another.

Scenario Destroyer

[The disasters have expressed their intention to abandon the scenario. The sixth scenario is therefore scheduled to end early.]

A banquet······

Ah, if that was the case······?

“Well······ it’s been hard to come by lately.”

[The eighth head of the ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads’]
[The seventh tail of the ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads’]

I threw the Totsuka-no-tsurugi he had given me into the alcohol.
This wasn’t how it was normally made, but it was a workaround of sorts.
Rrrrrumble!
Totsuka-no-tsurugi bubbled as it dissolved into the alcohol.
[Two Stories give meaning to your actions.]
[The Stories of the constellations ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads’ and ‘Snake Cutter’ combine.]

I’m telling you, Ways of Survival never got anything wrong.
Yoo Joonghyuk promptly reached out.
“This is mine.”

Normally, I would have stubbornly insisted, but this time even Yoo Joonghyuk’s gaze was serious.
This goddamn bastard······
Of course, the Star Relic itself hadn’t been my goal, but having one snatched away right before my eyes still stung.
Just as I reluctantly let go of the sword, unable to fight him here.

Another sword rose from the tub.
The contents of Ways of Survival raced through my mind.

「Names give birth to Stories, and Stories, in turn, reproduce reality. In the world of the <Star Stream>, [Ame-no-murakumo-no-tsurugi] had five names in all. In other words, [Ame-no-murakumo-no-tsurugi] was not ‘a single sword.’」

There were five names passed down for [Ame-no-murakumo-no-tsurugi].

Yoo Joonghyuk narrowed his eyes and glared at me for a moment before turning away.
“Do as you like.”
I barely managed to let out a sigh of relief.
The sword settled neatly into my hand. Its grip felt satisfying.
The second in the Ame-no-murakumo-no-tsurugi series, the Grass Cutting Sword.
With this sword’s power of dragon slaying (龍殺), I wouldn’t have to fear the dragons I would encounter from now on.

“Honestly, grown men being so petty over a single sword······”

“If you’re done, can I try some? It smells incredible.”

It wasn’t just Lee Jihye.

Well, just the smell was enough to make you drunk······
“Everyone, help yourselves.”

“Whoa! How can anything taste like this?”
“It’s heavenly!”

“You’re not drinking?”
Wandering nearby, I asked Yoo Joonghyuk. Looking more closely, I saw that, strangely enough, he was making a simple dish.
Grilled skewers of roughly cut meat and vegetables.

“I don’t eat things made by other people.”

“Because they taste bad.”
“And how good can your cooking possibly be······?”

Wait, what was this?
Lee Seolhwa, who was helping him nearby, smiled at me and asked:
“It’s good, isn’t it?”
It was fucking delicious.
Really, it was delicious.
No, it was the best food I had ever eaten.
How could a meat skewer taste like this?
One corner of Yoo Joonghyuk’s otherwise expressionless mouth had lifted in an infuriating smirk.
Damn it.
Even if he was a regressor, how the hell was this bastard good at cooking, too?
Grumbling to myself, I quietly slipped away. Then I heard what sounded like an instrument playing somewhere.
Very gentle music, with a rich, dignified beauty.
Turning toward the sound, I saw a figure atop the fortress.
The world’s smallest handsome man, whose looks rivaled Yoo Joonghyuk’s.
Kyrgios Rodgraim was there.

He sat on the railing, gazing into the distant sky as he played the viola. Softly, and at times mournfully. A distant, wistful longing. One by one, the people who had been talking boisterously fell silent and listened. The feverish excitement gradually cooled.
First, someone’s eyes reddened.
Then the person beside them burst into tears.
As though it were contagious, before long all the small people began to cry.
People who had missed their chance to cry, too busy running all this way, were finally shedding tears.
The inhabitants of [Peace Land], too, were beings who endured scenarios.
This music was offering comfort to his suffering homeland.

She hadn’t joined the Japanese group.

“How do you feel?”
“······Strange.”

“Perhaps this has become a world where that no longer matters.”

“······Um, well. I’m not sure, but I think the email address might have started with a t.”
t?
I went blank for an instant, then reflexively asked:
“Was that username······ ‘tls123,’ by any chance?”
tls123.
That was the username of the author of Ways of Survival.
Asuka Ren’s eyes widened as she repeated it.
I urgently pressed her.
“Do you remember?”
“I don’t really remember······ Huh?”
“······What’s wrong?”

Faint sparks flickered from her body.
Huh?
Startled, I asked:
“What did you just say?”

The viola’s melody ringing through the lonely night.

The moment a world is complete, its author must step down from the position of creator.

[You have come to know the planet ‘Peace Land.’]
[All beings belonging to ‘Peace Land’ faintly sense your gaze.]
[The small constellation of the small planet rejoices in your existence.]
[The beings of ‘Peace Land’ begin writing a legend about you.]

······So that was it.
Where a story would go after leaving its author had been decided from the very beginning.

“I’m sorry, I really don’t know. It does seem like a manga I’ve read······”
To think she felt she had read a story she herself had drawn.

Asuka Ren closed her eyes for a moment and pondered something, then continued:

Perhaps the author of Ways of Survival had been just as dissatisfied with the original ending as I was.
Perhaps that was why they had given me this ‘text file’ before this world’s end.

I stepped away from Asuka Ren, who was taking in the scenery, and took out the small ampoule I had tucked inside my clothes.

I felt bad, but I had a job for him today.

The job I entrusted to Lee Hyunsung was guarding me.
Because I planned to be unconscious for a while.

A ritual that could only be performed with Orochi’s snake liquor mixed with Star Blood.

This was a problem.

Should I have brought Yoo Sangah after all?
With a direct line to Olympus, I could send a signal right away······
‘O Father of the Rich Night.’
My surroundings went dark the moment I wrote Hades’s modifier.

Something important enough for both Hades and Persephone to leave at once.

The only means of forgetting the tragedies of those long years.

······Sure enough, it worked.

A woman who had lost her words and her memories.

There were still things she had to do in this world.

‘Yes.’

Shin Yoosung, who had come from the future of the 41st round.

Asuka Ren’s eyes reddened.
The Japanese groups disappeared into the portal one by one. Our group was last. The small people’s song continued.

The hero who saved Peace Land
His name
Neither Dokuja nor Dogeza, but Dokja
Oh, oh, his name is Dokja
······Damn it, why had they come up with lyrics like that?

The sight of Seoul, for the first time in a while.

We had entered the same portal, but apparently the exits were different.
Even so, why did I have to end up with this guy······.

KABOOOOOM!
Magic bullets flying in from every direction were tearing apart the spot where we had stood.

BOOM! BOOOOM!

Guys whose equipment and constellation sponsors were clearly of high caliber, even at a glance.
Were they incarnations belonging to the other ‘nebulae’ Persephone had mentioned?
I couldn’t tell yet.

······When had even that information leaked?
I hadn’t imagined they would know about the ‘King of No Killing’, too.

A force that could easily hold its own against the wanderers my mother had led.
Where on earth had these bastards come from?
The apparent leader was smiling at me as though it were all over.
