[Hey, you shouldn't throw a true name around like that. Though the tingles do feel good.]
“······Why do you look like that?”
[Probability, what else? A symbolic form like this is good for cutting costs. As you know, the great <Star Stream> is pretty strict.]
Actually, it was better for me if he wasn't in his true body, either.
Even with [Fourth Wall], I still wasn't sure I could look at a constellation's true body and remain sane.
The chariot set off as soon as I sat down.
I didn't know why Dionysus was driving the Sun Chariot of the Titan god Helios, but there seemed to be a reason.
[This is our first time meeting in person, right? Nice to meet you. I'm the ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’. In your country, I'm famous as the name of a fatigue remedy.]
“It's nice to meet you, too.”
After exchanging awkward greetings, we sat in separate corners of the chariot.
Unlike his usual playful manner, Dionysus wasn't very talkative.
Was he unexpectedly shy around strangers?
I hadn't expected that. Still, the Stories couldn't all be accurate.

More than that, the wine sloshing around in his glass whenever the chariot jolted was really bothering me. He wasn't going to suddenly spill it on me, was he? That liquid had to be a symbol of something, too. What part of Dionysus did it represent?
After I'd spent a little while on such pointless thoughts, Dionysus spoke.
[Oh, sorry. I was chatting with a goddess I know.]
“······You must be very busy?”
[Not really, but we've got a little something going on these days, so I have to keep her interested.]
I couldn't tell whether he was serious or joking.
[But you're calmer than I expected. I am a constellation, you know.]
“This isn't my first time seeing a constellation.”
[Oh, come to think of it, you're right. I sent you to the Underworld last time, didn't I?]
“Thank you for that.”
[No need to thank me. More to the point, what did you get up to in the Underworld?]
“Pardon?”
[I've never seen that haughty queen act so kindly. Taking on the nebulas to protect a single incarnation, no less······ Huh? Could it be? Is that it? You and that lady······.]
His voice sounded oddly envious. Dionysus didn't seem to know that I had carried out Persephone's task.
“Nothing happened.”
[Hey, hey, don't play dumb. She's fucking sexy, isn't she? If she didn't have a husband, I'd have tried something with her ages ago······.]
“······Is it all right for you to talk like that? Isn't the Queen of the Underworld your mother?”
[Hmm? Haha. There is that version, yes.]
“Was that version false, then?”
[I didn't say that.]
[What's that look for? Don't you know Olympus? A taboo like this is nothing.]
Come to think of it, Olympus was that sort of place.
A paradise for gods who thought with their crotches.
Even so, wasn't this going a bit far?

[Oh, right. Good thing you brought it up. You got my message earlier, didn't you? Come over to my side. I'll bestow the ‘Cult Leader of Bacchus’ Story on you as a special favor······ You don't look too pleased?]
“That's not it.”
I hurriedly shook my head.
As one of the twelve Olympian gods, Dionysus was a constellation of high Status.
But merely ‘Cult Leader of Bacchus’······.
[Aha, I get it. Look at you. You were comparing it with the Stories <Eden> and <Vedas> are offering, weren't you?]
“Not particularly, but······.”

[You idiot, that's because you don't know any better! Do you know what happens if you receive a Story like ‘Resurrected Messiah’? You have to live your entire life as a virgin! And after you die, too. Huh? You have to serve the creator god without ever getting to fuck!]
Dionysus shouted excitedly.
[Huh? Now, do you know how amazing ‘Cult Leader of Bacchus’ is by comparison? You know my female followers, right?]
“You mean the female followers who tore a homosexual person to pieces and killed them?”
Dionysus flinched.

[Uh······ Ahem. Y-yes! You can spend every night with them in a frenzy. And y-you get unlimited refills of the wine I bestow! Think that's all? Ever heard of an ‘Olympus Orgy Party’? You know Aphrodite, right? If you want, I could invite her, too······.]
[The constellation ‘Goddess of Love and Beauty’ glares at ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’.]
[······Forget what I said about her. Anyway, what do you think?]
“It doesn't really appeal to me.”
Dionysus's wine sloshed uneasily.
[······Come to think of it, a certain angel from <Eden> said you were a lover of men······ ]
“I think I know who spread that rumor, but I like women. More to the point, I'd like to hear the real reason you came to see me.”
[Hmm? What do you mean? Obviously, to bring you into our nebula······.]
“Is that really all?”
Dionysus was silent for a moment.
The wineglass, which had been sloshing for some time, spun once in the air.
[······You're sharp.]
“I get that a lot.”
[Want a drink? Have some of my wine.]
“I'm not very fond of alcohol.”
[Well······ All right. You're right. The truth is, I'm not here to bring you into ‘Olympus’.]
Just as I'd thought.

He had rattled on about goddesses and whatnot, but he hadn't meant any of it. No matter how many nebulas had their eyes on me, it had been strange from the start that one of the twelve major Olympian gods had come to pick up a mere incarnation.
But Dionysus's next words completely overturned my expectations.
[I'll get straight to the point. I don't want you to join ‘Olympus’.]
“······Pardon?”
[To be more precise······.]
That was when a terrible explosion rang out.
KABOOOOM!
The Sun Chariot lurched as though struck by artillery, and the horses at the front screamed. Looking back, I saw that wine had spilled from Dionysus's glass.
[Aaagh, fuck. I pissed myself from the shock!]
I was afraid to ask what, exactly, was piss.
I scrambled desperately to avoid touching the spilled wine.
[Damn it, looks like other nebulas are after you.]

Looking outside the curtain, I saw things radiating an overwhelming presence flying toward us from every direction. They were still too far away to tell which nebula they belonged to, but they clearly weren't friendly.

[Fuck. I paid that bastard Helios a fortune to rent this······ Hey, this won't work. I'll drop you off here, so run the rest of the way. Follow the Cloud Road straight ahead, and you'll be there in no time.]
Here? In midair?
[I'll hold them off, so hurry! Once you reach the banquet hall, no nebula can touch you!]
With those words, the curtain flew open.
I swallowed as I looked at the floor of clouds far below.
I was a soul. So even if I fell, I wouldn't die.
Dionysus's voice came from behind me.
[Remember. Trust no one.]
As I leaped from the chariot, Dionysus spoke with a grin.
[See you again, incarnation Kim Dokja.]
I jumped straight out of the chariot.
Tzzzzzt!
KABOOOOOM!

An enormous explosion resounded behind me, and an overwhelming presence pressed against my entire body. It was a tremendous power unlike anything I had felt before. At least part of a true body seemed to have descended.
Rrrrrrumble!
CRRRRASH!
Sparks struck like thunder.
I knew without looking back.
A battle between constellations had clearly begun.
I ran along the Cloud Road with all my might. Something like debris skimmed over my head, and it felt as though the ground was splitting beneath me. Still, I didn't look back.
How long had I been running?
At last, an enormous fortress came into view, and the noise behind me subsided.
I reached the entrance to the fortress.
“I've come to attend the banquet.”
The gatekeeper looked me up and down.
It appeared to be a low-ranking dokkaebi dispatched by the Bureau.
“What's this? I didn't hear anything about an incarnation coming.”
Damn it. Getting out of the Sun Chariot seemed to have been a mistake.
That had probably been my ticket straight in.
Just then, a door inside the fortress opened, and an unexpected savior appeared.
[Let that fellow in. He's with me.]
It wasn't Persephone.
A constellation I had long wanted to see was waiting for me there.
He stood at the entrance to the banquet hall.
If I was right, he was one of the few high-ranking constellations who had consistently supported me since the early scenarios.

「A face framed by brilliant white-gold fur, wearing a mischievous expression. A prisoner confined in the world's smallest prison as punishment for making a mockery of the most exalted throne. No one could help drawing a sharp breath upon meeting his noble Fiery Golden Eyes (火眼金睛).」

He really was exactly as ‘Ways of Survival’ had described him. I gazed at him as though spellbound. A being at the very pinnacle of the Narrative-grade constellations in ‘Ways of Survival’. Ignoring the gatekeeper, I rushed inside.
“Great Sage, Heaven's Equal!”
But with a mischievous smile, the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal, vanished before my eyes.
Like smoke.
As though to say I wasn't yet worthy of meeting him.
······Was that a clone?
Dejected, I lowered my outstretched hand, but that wasn't the end of it.
Having entered while repeatedly calling out the name of the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal, I had suddenly drawn the attention of the constellations on the first floor of the banquet hall.
[Who's that guy?]
An incarnation entering while calling out a particular constellation's nickname.
There was no way most constellations would take kindly to that.
Gazes poured toward me from all over the banquet hall.
[He's an incarnation?]
[What? Whose incarnation is he?]
As countless gazes converged on me, the air instantly began to boil, and my body went so rigid I couldn't move.
The gathering gazes made my mind go blank. I couldn't even tell who was looking at me.
I had thought I could now endure hearing the constellations' True Voices. But it became clear that this had been entirely due to [Fourth Wall].
To end up like this just from being looked at.
Only then did it truly sink in.
Right now, I was the only being in this banquet hall who wasn't a constellation.
At last, I stood before the constellations.
“Now, now, please calm down, constellation-nims. There's been a little mix-up, so I'll be taking this fellow away.”

I thought I heard a familiar voice, and then someone hoisted my rigid soul body up and began carrying me somewhere. Once we left the murmuring banquet hall and entered a corridor, that hell of staring eyes ended, and I could finally breathe.
“······Why the hell did you come alone?”
I raised my head at the voice, and sure enough, a familiar figure was bobbing in the air.
“Bihyung?”
“Yeah, it's me. The Queen of the Night said she'd send an envoy. Didn't you come with them? Why are you wandering around the wrong place by yourself? Trying to get yourself killed?”
“Something came up.”
“Hey, you can't just brush this off like that! This isn't a scenario area, you bastard! Get cocky here, and you're dead! This place······.”
“Is full of beings who can kill humans like bugs with a glance.”
I knew.
I knew very well.
That was why I'd come here.
Bihyung jutted out his lips in displeasure, then led me somewhere.
“I'll take you to the waiting room, so rest there for a while. There's a screen in there, so make sure you watch it. You have to watch, got it?”
Judging by the way he was swaggering, something good seemed to have happened to him. Before long, I reached the waiting room.
But the sign on the waiting room was, well, rather peculiar.
“······<Incarnation Waiting Room>? There's such a thing?”
“You think you're the only incarnation here? ······Of course, you're the only bastard who barged in alone.”
When I opened the door, someone I had never expected to see was there.
He reacted first.
“······Kim Dokja?”
I, too, stared at him blankly before awkwardly raising a hand.
“······Yoo Joonghyuk.”
<The Constellations' Banquet> was mentioned fairly often in the original ‘Ways of Survival’.

It was usually somewhere Yoo Joonghyuk came when he used ‘regression’ to milk the constellations for all they were worth, and sure enough, he was on the guest list this time, too. I didn't know who had invited him, but with someone like him, Narrative-grade constellations would be lining up to make connections······.
This <Constellations' Banquet> was an event jointly held by several countries.
<Seoul Dome>, <Washington Dome>, <Moscow Dome>, and even <New Delhi Dome>.

The Bureau seemed to have gathered domes with good recent results to hold a joint presentation of their achievements. Judging by the combination of participating countries······ the atmosphere seemed roughly similar to Yoo Joonghyuk's 24th round.
The incarnations in the waiting room sat apart from one another, grouped by country.
“Why are you here?”
“Probably for much the same reason as you.”
“When are you coming back to life?”
“Probably tomorrow.”
“The others are worried.”
“Sorry about that.”

Having a conversation like this with that Yoo Joonghyuk left me feeling oddly unsettled. His clenched fists suggested he was holding back his anger······ Honestly, watching this bastard lately, I was starting to wonder if he had an anger management problem.
I sat beside Yoo Joonghyuk and watched the proceedings on the large screen in front of us. The ‘Intermediate Dokkaebi Promotion Ceremony’ was in full swing.
―I would like to thank all the constellations and dokkaebis who have granted me the glory of stories once again······.
Bihyung was being interviewed as the representative of the low-ranking dokkaebis.
So this was why that bastard had told me to watch the broadcast.
―Half of this honor is actually thanks to an incarnation who has been working hard on my channel. You probably all know him. I dedicate half of this joy to that incarnation!
He had no trouble spouting such mortifying lines.

The incarnations around me seemed to be glancing my way, so I deliberately averted my eyes. In the middle of his speech, Bihyung took a golden egg from inside his clothes and held it high overhead. I recognized it immediately.
―And I dedicate the other half to this child who will soon be born!
It was the egg in which Shin Yoosung's soul lay sleeping.
Fortunately, it seemed to be well on its way to hatching.
“You bastard, don't tell me······?”
Apparently having used [Sage's Eye] in that brief moment, a horrified Yoo Joonghyuk looked back and forth between me and Bihyung's egg. I spoke as though making an excuse.
“It was the only way.”
“Do you know what you've done?”
“I do.”
“If you do something like that, Shin Yoosung will······!”

I knew what Yoo Joonghyuk was worried about. Someone who had suffered from ‘stories’ for so long would now become one of those who produced that tragedy. Yoo Joonghyuk knew very well how painful that would be. He could hardly say anything else.
“If she's born as a dokkaebi, at least she won't have to die in the future. The ‘Bureau’ is the safest place there is until the <Star Stream> falls.”
Of course, that wasn't my only reason, but I couldn't explain all my reasons for turning Shin Yoosung into a dokkaebi in a place like this.
Yoo Joonghyuk's gaze met mine in midair. If we'd been in the mortal world, he looked ready to draw his sword and cut me down on the spot.
“Excuse me······ Are you ‘Kim Dokja’?”
At the interrupting voice, that menacing air vanished without a trace.

Turning my head, I saw a beautiful woman who looked distinctly of mixed Eastern and Western heritage. She had gently wavy khaki-brown hair and large eyes with a soft brown hue. Her bright, healthy smile was especially lovely.
“I am. Do you know me?”
“Ah······ A little. I've heard about you.”
I was oddly glad. To think this woman would approach me first.
“It's nice to meet you, Selena Kim.”
“You know me?”
“You're the American representative, aren't you? I've heard about you, too.”
Of course, I hadn't heard about her.
But I knew her.

Character : Selena Kim
Exclusive attributes : Animal Lover (Rare), King’s Guardian (Hero)

‘Selena Kim’ of the Washington Dome.

She was a member of <Zarathustra>, founded by Anna Croft, and a woman who would become one of the hundred strongest people in Ways of Survival. ‘King of No Killing’, the attribute I had once possessed, was originally meant to be hers.
Unfortunately, since I had acquired the attribute first, she seemed to have unlocked a different one, but······.
“Didn't Anna Croft come with you?”
“······You know Anna?”
“We met through a dream some time ago.”
“She wanted to come, too. If she'd known you were coming, she certainly would have.”
Of course, her presence would only have complicated things.
Why? Because of this guy.
“Tell that woman to take good care of her neck.”
“······You're exactly as Anna described, Yoo Joonghyuk.”
It was obvious that Yoo Joonghyuk was the reason Anna hadn't come.
Anna Croft had betrayed Yoo Joonghyuk in the previous round, and Anna would have seen what she'd done to him through Past Sight. Naturally, she wouldn't come here.
“There's a really ugly guy on the Korean side, too. Are you Korea's representative?”
Wondering what this was about, I turned around. This time, it was Russia's representative.
“Iris, that's rude. Judging others by their appearance is a bad habit.”
“I just called an ugly guy ugly. Honesty is a virtue in Moscow.”
Snow-white platinum hair and snow-white skin.
A petite, pretty girl with twin ponytails stood there.

From that business about Moscow, I thought I knew who she was. But I didn't particularly want to let on. This girl was one of the characters I disliked in ‘Ways of Survival’. I deliberately dropped the politeness when I asked.
“Who are you?”
“······You don't know me? You don't know the great Iris Vladimirovna Rebezova?”
“Should I?”
Unable to watch any longer, Selena Kim intervened.
“Dokja-ssi, let me introduce her. This is Iris, Russia's representative. In Russia, she's called the ‘War God of the Red Square’.”
“Ahem. That's me, all right.”
I nodded.
I wanted to snap back with a comment about what a pretentious nickname it was, but I held my tongue because I thought it might cause unnecessary trouble.
Selena Kim continued.
“Iris, this is Kim Dokja-ssi. He's Korea's representative, and his nickname is······ Um, I'm sorry, but Dokja-ssi, your nickname······.”
Then Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“His nickname is······.”
I hastily covered his mouth and cut him off.
“I don't have a nickname yet.”
A sneer curled Iris's lips.
“A guy without even a nickname has graced us with his presence?”
I had one.
I did have one. I just didn't want to say it.
“I don't know what qualified you to be invited here, but you'd better watch how much you show off.”
As a menacing aura began pouring from the Russian side, Yoo Joonghyuk sprang up beside me and unleashed his own aura in response. Perhaps sensing its immense force, Iris retreated half a step.
“Stay out of this. This is between me and that ugly guy.”
Despite Iris's warning, Yoo Joonghyuk merely glared at her in silence.
Good job. While you're at it, slap her, too, Yoo Joonghyuk.
Finally, Iris bit her lip, retreated another step, and snapped.
“Well, looks like you're here to beg some insignificant Historical-grade for a Story······ Just you wait.”
······Beg a Historical-grade for a Story?
What a cute thing to say.
Come to think of it, the program for <The Constellations' Banquet> did include something about <Story Inheritance>.
That was probably what Iris meant.
Knock, knock, knock.
Just then, the waiting-room door opened, and a low-ranking dokkaebi poked its head inside.

“Incarnations, the <Story Inheritance Ceremony> will begin shortly. Please proceed to the hall. Temporary seats have been prepared for you in the banquet hall on the first floor. Please note that only Historical-grade constellations are on the first floor. Please keep that in mind.”
<Story Inheritance Ceremony>.

A <Sponsorship Contract> wasn't the only way constellations and incarnations could influence each other. Incarnations could increase their power by inheriting the <Stories> of constellations other than their sponsors and paying homage to those stories. Of course, spreading their own Stories also allowed constellations to expand their influence, so it benefited both incarnations and constellations.
We walked into the banquet hall one by one.
The first name they chanted was Selena Kim's.
[Selena Kim! King's Guardian!]
[I've been following your exploits!]
Unlike before, the constellations' response was friendly.
Probably because they were welcoming their favorite incarnations.
Their excited demeanor, as though they'd met their favorite celebrities.
Iris was next.
She walked toward the constellations with a haughty air and gave them a little wave, as though doing some fan service.
[Iris! The little brat of the Red Square!]
[Hahaha! How cute.]
[She's just like she is on screen, isn't she?]
She cast a haughty glance at me where I stood behind her.
She seemed to be saying something like this.
「See that?」
······So what?
At last, it was my turn.

As I stepped into the banquet hall, the pressure of the gazes I'd felt earlier poured over me again. Still, whether because I'd already experienced it once or because the gazes felt different, it was fairly bearable this time.
But the constellations' reaction was strange.
The atmosphere, so heated a moment ago, went quiet as though someone had doused it with cold water.
······Was I not very popular?
I could see Iris sneering at me as though she'd expected as much.
That was when someone spoke.
[······That's him. Kim Dokja of the Korean Peninsula.]
[Kim Dokja? That guy is the Kim Dokja?]
That set off a wave of murmurs. Their reaction was completely different from the ones they'd given the earlier incarnations.
[Kim Dokja! That guy is the Kim Dokja]
[Kim Dogeza! Kim Dogeza!]
[King of a Kingless World!]
With every step I took, the constellations' voices grew louder.
[One Who Opposes the Extraordinary!]
Like a wildfire carried by the wind, their voices spread throughout the hall.
[Say, do you remember me? I'm the ‘Bald General of Justice’!]
[Kim Dokja! I am ‘King Heungmu the Great’!]
I walked silently toward the center of the banquet hall.
[I really enjoyed Peace Land! You've got some moves, kid!]
[Hey! Wave this way! I donated a whole 3000 coins to you!]
[Everyone, come over here! Kim Dokja's here!]
[But he's much easier on the eyes than I'd heard, isn't he?]

With the constellations forgetting all decorum and going wild, the whole banquet hall felt like an enormous furnace. Its scorching heat seemed about to cook my soul through, so I had no choice but to raise a hand to them.
The constellations erupted in cheers.
[You're handsome, Kim Dokja!]
Iris was staring this way, her face aghast.
But I wasn't looking at her.
I hadn't come here for fun.
Scenario footage was playing across the ceiling and all over the walls.
Incarnations dying amid screams, and constellations snickering as they watched.
Watching them, I realize all over again what kind of place this is.
A place where every human tragedy becomes a feast.
I looked up at the banquet hall's second floor.

Unlike the rowdy Historical-grade constellations on the first floor, the Narrative-grade constellations on the second floor gazed down at me in ominous silence. Constellations, each shining with a terrifying presence.
They were the true enemies I had to fight.

Yoo Joonghyuk, who went next, was no less popular. When he appeared, there was even a little noise from the second floor. I had the impression that the <Eden> contingent was chanting my name along with his, but I wasn't sure whether I was imagining it.
[Yoo Joonghyuuuuuk―!]
[You're the best, Supreme King!]
[Join our nebula!]

There was still a little time before the <Story Inheritance Ceremony>, so I sat at a banquet table on the first floor and watched the situation for a while. All constellations, Historical-grade or Narrative-grade, warranted caution, but here I needed to judge carefully.
I wasn't exactly looking for someone trustworthy. Dionysus must have had a reason for telling me to “trust no one.”
So what I was looking for now was ‘someone to use’, rather than ‘someone to trust’.
Iris approached hesitantly and spoke to me.
I have a rough idea of what she's going to say.
Before she could speak, I warned her.
“Don't act rashly if you want to survive.”
“Wh-what?”
For a moment, Iris looked blank. Then she started and looked up into the air.
[A few constellations are surprised by your judgment.]
[A considerable number of constellations have donated 5000 coins for your satisfying comeback.]
A huge close-up of her face filled a panel at the edge of the ceiling. The constellations snickered at the sight of Iris blushing. Stunned, Iris muttered.
“Th-that was all being filmed?”
It was naïve to think the channels would be switched off just because we'd come to the constellations' world.
If anything, the constellations would have been watching our reactions with burning eagerness from the moment we arrived.
Especially those sinister bastards on the second floor.
If Iris and I had actually fought in the waiting room, the constellations' excitement would probably have been near its peak.
But I didn't want to give them that pleasure.
As I said, I didn't come here for fun.
So at least here, I don't want to be made a fool of.
“Do better next time, kid.”
I patted Iris's shoulder and stood up. As I moved, a whole host of constellations on the first floor responded.
[Kim Dokja! Come here!]

All the constellations on the first floor had taken the form of ‘symbols’, rather than humans or living creatures. Historical-grades, who struggled to bear a large probability burden alone, had to maintain simplified symbolic bodies to reduce their expenditure.
That made it impossible to tell who was who at a glance.
What approached: a jangling bamboo staff and an elaborate golden crown reminiscent of Silla.
“‘Bald General of Justice’-nim. And is the other person······ ‘Supreme Maegum’?”
[Oh! You remember me!]
[Indeed. It has been a long time.]
It was the constellations of the Korean Peninsula who had sought me out.
[I've been wanting to see you at least once. So this is how we meet.]
That floating ‘eyepatch’ seemed to be the ‘One-Eyed Maitreya’······.
There were also symbolic bodies I guessed belonged to ‘The Last Hero of Hwangsanbeol’ and ‘King Heungmu the Great’. I'd been meaning to ask Gyebaek something, anyway······.
[Kim Dokja, you of a later generation.]
I turned around to see a hundred-won coin floating there.
A hundred won? Why a hundred won?
[I'm very pleased to meet you.]
“Um, who might you be······?”
[How disappointing. Don't you recognize me?]
Wait. Which historical figure was on the hundred-won coin again?
“Admiral-nim?”
I asked, startled.
My patriotism might be close to zero, but even I couldn't meet this man in person without being moved.
The coin spun in the air, revealing the figure engraved on its face.
[You seem to be making good use of the stigma I gave you last time.]
“Thank you for your help back then.”
Yi Sunsin, Duke of Loyalty and Warfare.
He, too, had been invited to this banquet—the man who had passed [Song of the Sword] on to me.
“But why have you taken that form?”
[······This form is not of my choosing.]

Somehow, I thought I understood what he meant. Come to think of it, the Duke of Loyalty and Warfare wasn't the only one shaped like currency. I looked at the green piece of paper draped over a wall on the first floor, swaying limply, and asked.
“Then could that person be······?”
Yi Sunsin nodded.
[The ‘Creator of Hangul’. Like me, he has a statue in Gwanghwamun. Don't you know him?]
I knew who he was. I hadn't asked out of ignorance.
Yi Sunsin continued.
[Symbolic bodies are modeled on our best-known symbols. He's probably in much the same situation as I am.]
I gave the ‘Creator of Hangul’, who was looking at me with sad eyes, a small bow with my hands clasped.
King Sejong the Great was one thing, but Yi Sunsin, whose symbol should obviously have been a turtle ship, was a hundred-won coin.
Confining great historical figures to hundred-won coins and ten-thousand-won notes had left even their symbolic bodies like this.
Snickers came from the second floor.
Come to think of it, all the Narrative-grade constellations on the second floor were ‘humanoid’, or at least looked like living creatures.
Even the Korean Peninsula's most famous historical figures can't maintain human forms. I can't begin to imagine how powerful the true bodies of Narrative-grades must be.
Seen that way, I'd been incredibly lucky to hunt down Yamata no Orochi's shadow.
Just then, one constellation caught my eye.
“Who is that constellation?”
[Who? Oh, that man?]

I'd spotted a man sitting on the landing between the first and second floors, downing liquor. With a long sword and sturdy armor, he was maintaining a humanoid symbolic body, but he didn't look Narrative-grade to me. Every Narrative-grade constellation passing him was giving him a contemptuous look.
Samyeongdang chimed in.
[Among the Korean Peninsula's Historical-grades, none can surpass him.]

“I told you not to involve yourself with me again. Saving you then was merely repayment of my debt to Kim Dokja.”
“This concerns that very Kim Dokja-ssi.”
For a moment, Yoo Joonghyuk’s murderous intent eased.
“······What do you mean?”

“In this scenario, Dokja-ssi will die.”
Kim Dokja would die?
Yoo Joonghyuk gave a little scoff.
“Kim Dokja can resurrect. I believe I told you before. Apparently, you weren’t listening.”

By now, Yoo Joonghyuk had some idea of Kim Dokja’s abilities. Of course, he probably couldn’t resurrect indefinitely, but he would be able to come back at least a few more times. That meant Kim Dokja’s life would not be in danger for a while.
“He should have revived by now······ It seems you haven’t met him yet?”
This time, Yoo Sangah’s gaze wavered.
But she persisted and spoke again.
“That isn’t what I mean. If we leave things as they are, Dokja-ssi will ‘really’ die.”
“······How do you know that?”
“Because I saw it.”
“You saw it?”
The next moment, a massive skein of thread appeared behind Yoo Sangah.
It was not [Ariadne]’s skein.

On closer inspection, the threads of the skein were not made of fibers. Tiny strings of text. Cords woven from countless stories. Yoo Joonghyuk knew that shape, embroidering the air like an enormous fabric of fate.
And because he knew it, he couldn’t help being shocked.
Because it was the symbol of the three goddesses of fate, the Moerae.
Yoo Joonghyuk spoke through gritted teeth.
“Don’t tell me you stole a look at the constellations’ prophecy?”
Yoo Sangah nodded cautiously.
Enraged, Yoo Joonghyuk said,
“Do you understand what you’ve done? ‘Fate’ is······.”
“I know! That’s why I’m asking you for help, Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi.”
Yoo Joonghyuk’s mind became a tangle.
The Moerae’s ‘fate’ was not merely a power to see and foretell the future.
Rather, the prophecy was closer to a ‘conclusion’ drawn through ‘big data’.
The ‘most reasonable future’, predicted through a combination of countless stories.
Viewed this way, ‘fate’ might seem far from absolute, something that could be changed any number of ways. But that was by no means the case.
Because <Olympus>’s prophecies had never once been wrong.
Even Zeus, the chief god of <Olympus>, had been unable to escape that ‘fate’.
Because the moment a fate began, the probability of all of <Olympus> was used to make it come true.
“Please stop Kim Dokja-ssi. Otherwise······.”
Yoo Sangah’s desperate words could go no further.
Bzzzzzt.
The forbidden probability caused Yoo Sangah to collapse unconscious amid the sparks. But Yoo Joonghyuk could clearly read the text of the skein embroidered in the air behind her.
「Incarnation Kim Dokja will die at the hands of the person he loves most.」
“Whoa, these plains are huge!”
“Is this really the ‘Dark Castle’?”
Lee Hyunsung stared in apparent wonder at the endless horizon.
Vast plains, with stretches of jungle spread here and there.
An ominous, pitch-black river flowed majestically through the middle, dividing the plains in two.
That river was probably [Phoenix], a tributary from the Demon Realm.
At last, we had reached the Dark Castle’s second floor.
“Yes. This is the second floor. It’s completely different from the first.”
Unlike the first floor, where a new scenario was underway, the Dark Castle’s second floor held a scenario that had been running for a very long time.
In the distance, I could see incarnations gathered in groups, talking among themselves.
They seemed to be Seoul’s incarnations, who had newly entered along with us.
They showed no particular reaction when they saw us. Looking more closely, I saw that a dokkaebi was giving them guidance.
[······And so, congratulations to all you incarnations who have newly reached the second floor. These <Abyss Plains> will be a place of opportunity, where you can do anything.]
It was a dokkaebi I had never seen before.
The dokkaebi looked noticeably old, and seemed to have worked for the Bureau for a very long time.
Well, that made sense for someone in charge of the <Abyss Plains> scenario.
The scenario here was assigned to dokkaebis who had been demoted.
I turned on my smartphone and found the information about the Dark Castle’s second floor in ‘Ways of Survival’.
「The <Abyss Plains>. The dokkaebis call this place ‘the grave of scenarios’.」
······The grave of scenarios.
Seeing that expression stirred fresh feelings in me.
I’d already come this far.
Listening to the dokkaebi, Han Sooyoung spoke.
“More bullshit. Opportunity, my ass. They’ll fucking work us to death whenever they get the chance, spouting crap about adjusting the difficulty.”
She wasn’t the only one. The other incarnations, now accustomed to the dokkaebis’ sweet talk, simply glared at the dokkaebi with distrust.
Now that they’d already reached the ninth scenario, there was no way talk of opportunities or whatever else would work on them.
Whether the old dokkaebi had heard her or not, I didn’t know, but the dokkaebi smiled.
[Do not worry. The dokkaebis will not interfere in this scenario. Whether the scenario is entertaining or dull, we promise never to meddle with the story.]
The incarnations murmured.
No dokkaebi had ever said anything like that before.
Why were the dokkaebis, who always wanted more sensational stories, saying they would not interfere with the ‘story’ here?
“What the hell are you up to?”
“What’s that supposed to mean!”
[I know you are all weary from the scenarios thus far. But I speak the truth.]
[The updated main scenario has arrived!]
<Main Scenario # 9 ― ???>
Category: Main
Difficulty: ???
Clear Condition: ???
Time Limit: ―
Reward: None
Failure: ―
A scenario with all its conditions concealed, and neither a time limit nor a failure condition.
The incarnations, who had never received a scenario like this, were deeply bewildered.
“What? What are we supposed to do if you don’t reveal anything?”
“Fuck, you’re trying to screw us over with another shitty scenario, aren’t you?”
Even at the incarnations’ angry reactions, the dokkaebi simply smiled indulgently.

[What have you been striving for all this time? For family or friends? To become stronger? Or to reign over others? Each of you will have an answer. But I believe those answers are all lies. Because you have only come this far ‘to carry out the scenarios’.]
The incarnations’ gazes wavered at those words, which dismissed the lives they had been living lately.
The old dokkaebi continued.
[But it will be difficult to overcome the coming scenarios with that mindset alone. Such passive beings cannot survive in the <Star Stream>. Therefore, this scenario will demand nothing of you.]
A scenario that demanded nothing.
The incarnations shuddered.

[There is neither a time limit nor a failure condition. Because there is nothing to fail at. Find your own clear condition. Only those who find it will be able to move forward. Heh heh, though I wonder how many will make that choice... I do hope you will not fall asleep in this ‘grave’.]
With those final words, the dokkaebi vanished.
Suddenly deprived of a purpose, the incarnations filled the air with restless murmurs.
It was a strange sight.
Even though this scenario was more ‘peaceful’ than any they had experienced before, the incarnations seemed somehow anxious.
Like people who had been happier when they had an impossible goal.
Lee Hyunsung asked,
“Dokja-ssi? What on earth is this······?”
Lee Hyunsung also seemed deeply bewildered.

Until moments ago, he had been burning with determination to raise his ranking. Now a scenario ‘without a clear condition’ had suddenly appeared. He could only feel deflated. I had already been a little worried.
Because this might be the most dangerous scenario of all for our group.
Just as I was about to speak, I sensed someone stirring behind me.
“Ugh······ Where are we?”
Lee Jihye and Lee Gilyoung were regaining consciousness.
After checking her staggering rank of ‘98761st’, Lee Jihye sank into deep despair.
“I’ve never ranked this low, even on a mock exam······.”
Of course, that was a lie.
According to ‘Ways of Survival’, Lee Jihye wasn’t good at studying.
“······Dokja-hyung?”
Lee Gilyoung leaped like a grasshopper the moment he saw me. A little later, he curled up like a demure pill bug and pretended to be calm.
“I knew you’d be alive. I believed in you right to the end, hyung!”
Lee Jihye scoffed at that.
“What’s this little brat saying? You were crying with snot running down your face.”
“I wasn’t crying!”
Lee Gilyoung kept protesting that he hadn’t cried, insisting that of course he’d known I would come back to life.
But ten minutes later, his eyes brimming, Lee Gilyoung lost control of his emotions again and lunged at my thigh, shouting, “Hyuuuuung!”
“······A scenario without a scenario?”
A little later, after hearing our explanation, Lee Jihye looked at us as though asking what sort of bullshit that was.
“How do you clear something like that?”
After some thought, Lee Hyunsung said,
“Maybe there’s some hidden intention? If we find the hidden condition, I’m sure we’ll be able to clear the scenario.”
“Right? If we all work together and look······.”
Watching Lee Hyunsung and Lee Jihye join forces, I smiled wryly.
Sure enough, simplicity helped at times like this.
But not everyone possessed their straightforward drive.
“Um······ Do we really have to clear it?”
The speaker was Kim Yongpal of the Pink Kids.
Lee Jihye asked,
“Who’s that woman?”
“Just a woman······ a lady who happened to come along with us.”
I couldn’t be bothered to explain, so I glossed over it.
She wouldn’t believe me if I suddenly said he was a man in his forties.
Meanwhile, Kim Yongpal was still stammering, his eyes half glazed over.
“Wouldn’t it be all right to just stay as we are? Do we really have to clear it······?”
“What’s this bullshit all of a sudden?”
“······D-do any of you know what lies at the ‘end’ of these scenarios?”
It felt as though someone had pierced straight to the heart of the matter from an unexpected direction.
To think that man would have such a thought.
Taken aback, Lee Jihye asked,
“What?”

“W-we don’t know whether continuing to carry out the scenarios is good or bad for us······. In this endless succession of scenarios, we’re nothing but the constellations’ toys. Even if we clear this scenario, we don’t know what the next one will be like. We could die at a-any moment.”
Kim Yongpal’s words left my companions looking troubled.
Because, on reflection, he was right.
No one knew how these scenarios would end.
No one knew who would die, or where, or how.
Everyone had only come this far because ‘they would die if they didn’t clear them’.
But this scenario had neither a failure condition nor a time limit.
Biting her lip hard, Lee Jihye shouted,
“So what are you suggesting? That we stay here? Do you even know where we are? There are demon bastards roaming around. This place isn’t remotely safe······!”
But before Lee Jihye could finish, large demons began swarming toward us from across the plains. At a glance, they were grade 5 or stronger. Lee Jihye smiled as if to say she’d known it.
“See? They’re already coming.”
“Everyone, gather here!”

The nearby incarnations quickly gathered around our group. The approaching creatures were [Devil Bears], grade-4 demons. There were roughly twenty. If I used [Electrification] and joined forces with my companions, we could handle that number easily enough.
Of course, the other incarnations, who didn’t know my strength, looked despairing.
“Fuck······ More monsters like that······.”
That was when beams of light poured in from beyond the [Devil Bears].
Boom boom boom boom boom!
Pure white flames. A path of holy fire opened, and the [Devil Bears] at the rear let out piercing screams.
Power enough to slaughter even grade-4 demons.
That stigma was undoubtedly······.
“Unnie!”
Lee Jihye shouted.
Sure enough, those flames were Jung Heewon’s [Hell Flames Ignition].
Spotting us from afar, Jung Heewon looked startled.
In particular, the sight of me alive seemed to leave her almost aghast.
When I waved awkwardly, Jung Heewon hesitated, then nodded.
At that moment, a strange sense of something being off brushed past me.
······What was it?
Looking closely, I saw that Jung Heewon was riding a [Black Unicorn].
How had she tamed that beast?
Several others riding [Black Unicorns] alongside Jung Heewon drove back the [Devil Bears] and rapidly approached us. The incarnations who recognized Jung Heewon began chanting her name.
“Woooow! It’s the ‘Judge of Evil’!”
As Jung Heewon came close, Lee Jihye ran over.
“Unnie, I knew you’d be alive! Were you already here?”
“Jihye, I’m sorry, but let’s talk a little later.”

Leaving the chattering Lee Jihye behind, Jung Heewon immediately turned away. Looking crestfallen, Lee Jihye trudged back to my side. Jung Heewon was guiding the people with practiced ease, as though she was already accustomed to this.
“Everyone, follow me! I’ll take you somewhere safe!”
······Somewhere safe?
The unease I had felt earlier grew stronger.

Awed by Jung Heewon’s overwhelming strength, the incarnations followed her as though entranced. We had little choice but to follow, too. Had we crossed the plains for about an hour? A rampart hidden between stretches of jungle came into view.
A rampart so sturdy it seemed no demon could cross it.
As the incarnations stared in a daze, a voice sounded from somewhere.
[Welcome. It must have been difficult to come this far. You have endured so much. You are safe now.]
The people murmured.
Jung Heewon was looking at me, her eyes reflecting mixed emotions.
At that moment, I understood how this had happened.
Damn it. So that was it.
This was ‘that bastard’s’ fortress.
A man appeared atop the rampart.
A power that made you certain he was this place’s master merely by his presence there.
A demon harboring the most peaceful despair in the world looked down at us and smiled.
[You no longer need to carry out the scenarios.]
We no longer needed to carry out the scenarios.
At those words, everyone gathered at the fortress grew tense and alert.
“What the hell does that mean?”
Some people listened to him.
But most did not.
「He’s obviously a con artist.」
「······At least say something that makes sense. What? We don’t need to carry out the scenarios?」
「It must be a scheme to keep something all to himself.」
Whatever else they were, these were incarnations who had survived as far as the ninth scenario.

Even setting aside Cheon Inho of Geumho Station and Gong Pildu of Chungmuro, Seoul had been full of con artists. The incarnations here were either such swindlers themselves or people who had defeated them to make it this far.
So there was no way they would easily fall for sweet talk like that.
As though he had read their thoughts, the man on the rampart spoke.

[You will not believe me. I understand. Nine scenarios may hardly be called a long time, but neither can they be called a short one. I can well imagine what you have experienced, and what lives you have led to reach this place.]
A con artist’s basic technique was to pretend to understand the other person.
But these people were already sick of that ‘pretense’.
“You think we’ll fall for that again?”
“What the hell is your goal? What are you trying to say?”
Those who couldn’t hold back shouted first.
Then the man smiled faintly.
It was a smile so beautiful that you could hardly imagine him being a con artist.

[I mean exactly what I said. You no longer need to fight. I imagine the dokkaebis have explained it to you. The scenario here in the [Dark Castle] has neither a time limit nor a failure condition. Those of you who are clever will already have understood what that means.]
When I looked beside me, Kim Yongpal of the Pink Kids had a gleam in his eyes.

[You can continue living in this ‘scenario area’. You can eat as you once did, sleep in, and do whatever you wish. With your right to life respected, and free of the compulsion to clear scenarios······ you can live as you did before the ‘destruction’ began, and spend the rest of your lives here.]
“Right to life? Cut the bullshit!”
“How are we supposed to live somewhere with demons roaming around?”
“We have somewhere to go back to!”
The people shouted at the tops of their lungs.
Then the man asked,
[Go back? Where do you intend to go back to?]
“Obviously, to where we used to live······.”
[Surely you do not mean that ruined ‘planet’?]
“R-ruined? Not yet, it isn’t!”

[You must all know this already. From the moment the ‘scenarios’ began, your planet could move only toward ‘destruction’. Even if you return there, all you will see is ruins. You may clear scenario after scenario······ but in the end, all that awaits you is ruin.]
“Who are you to say that! What do you know―”
[I do know. Because the planet where I lived was destroyed by the ‘scenarios’ long ago.]
The agitated crowd fell silent all at once.
Someone who had lost his homeland to the ‘scenarios’ long ago.
A man who had remained in the [Dark Castle] longer than anyone here was now addressing them.
[That is why I can say with confidence that nowhere in the <Star Stream> is there a world safer than the one you now stand in.]
For the first time, the people’s defiance weakened.
Their eyes were still full of distrust, but an inclination to at least hear him out was emerging.
Someone asked in a loud voice,
“Who exactly are you?”
[My name is Reinheit von Djerba. I came to this land 800 years before you······ and I am the master of the fortress you see before you, <Paradise>.]
Then the fortress gates swung wide open.
The people’s expressions began to change as they saw the scene within.
Seeing their faces, Reinheit concluded with a smile.
[Once again, everyone, welcome. Welcome to <Paradise>.]
<Paradise>.
‘Ways of Survival’ also mentioned <Paradise> countless times.
The grave of scenarios. The incarnations’ nest. A flower blooming on the plains of despair······ Many beings had described this place with all sorts of flourishes.
In fact, most of those descriptions were true.
“To think a place like this existed······.”

Everyone in the group except me was spellbound by the vista of <Paradise> before us. Lee Jihye, Lee Gilyoung, Shin Yoosung, and even Lee Hyunsung. Lee Hyunsung in particular rubbed his eyes again and again, as though he couldn’t believe what he was seeing.
Residential and market districts laid out on either side of a broad central avenue.
The voices of the bustling people were filled with a vitality we had never heard before.
“Demon weevil legs for sale! Have a taste before you go! Great for relieving fatigue!”
“‘Prickly ash berries’ grown on the farm! Excellent for restoring stamina!”

The market vendors were kind, and customers paid contentedly after bargaining down the prices. People of different species and nationalities were gathered together, yet no one showed any sign of discriminating against or threatening anyone else.
All the incarnations entering the fortress looked bewildered by the bright atmosphere that had suddenly enveloped them.
“What on earth······.”
Until moments ago, words like ‘paradise’ and ‘peace’ had been nothing but bullshit to them. But that bullshit now existed before their eyes, with tangible substance.
“······Paradise?”
Some were so astonished that they sank to the ground.
Among the more impulsive incarnations, some had dropped their weapons and were gasping.
Kind hands reached out to them from all sides.
“Are you all right? Anyone who’s injured, please come this way! <Paradise>’s clinic treats all injured people free of charge!”
“We teach weapon techniques and internal cultivation methods! Want to know the difference between ether and magic power? Want to use sword aura like everyone else? All are welcome!”
The inhabitants of <Paradise> shared freely. They exchanged their knowledge and regarded helping others as a virtue.
There were even exchanges that crossed species boundaries.
A demon with horns on its head grinned broadly and waved at us.
“A-a demon!”
When several startled incarnations drew their weapons, the guards stationed in the fortress quickly approached.
“Put those away.”
“What are you talking about! That thing’s a demon bastard······!”
“Such hateful language is prohibited here. That person is a resident of <Paradise>, just like anyone else.”
“A r-resident?”
As the bewildered incarnations hesitated, the demon who had waved approached.
“I am indeed a demon. But I will not harm you. The stereotype that demons are bound to eat humans saddens me.”
The incarnations stared blankly at that sentimental tone.
Their eyes said they had no idea what on earth was going on.
Similar scenes followed one after another.
Demons, humans, and non-human species joining forces to build houses, walking to taverns with their arms around one another’s shoulders, or sitting side by side for meals on outdoor terraces······.
Now and then, some gestured toward us as if to welcome us.
The scene looked like a travel advertisement, and my companions were unable to gather their wits.
[The character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ is swayed by the surrounding scenery.]
[The character ‘Lee Jihye’ is swayed by the surrounding atmosphere.]
My companions’ feelings were conveyed to me in real time.
The first peace they had encountered since the scenarios began.
It was hardly strange that their hearts should waver.
People who had lived ordinary lives didn’t change their essential nature just because they picked up a sword.
Everything had merely been the result of forces beyond their control.
And now, for the first time, my companions were being tempted by the possibility of escaping those ‘forces beyond their control’.
We spotted Jung Heewon in the distance and went over. She was talking to someone. A woman I had seen before.
“Thank you so much for what you did back then. I didn’t even manage to thank you properly······.”
“Not at all! I’m glad you seem to be doing well.”
The young woman talking to Jung Heewon glanced my way, then widened her eyes.
Her emotions changed rapidly.
To surprise, to fear, and soon······ to gratitude.
“Could that man be······?”
“Ah, Dokja-ssi······.”
“It is you! I’ve never forgotten what you did to save us.”
At first, I wasn’t sure, but the sight of the young child holding her hand brought the memory back.
“Ah, were you at Geumho Station······?”
“You remember us? Dayoung, you should say hello, too.”
They were the mother and daughter who had fought with the Cheoldoo Group at Geumho Station.

I had been a little worried because they hadn’t joined our group, but apparently they had somehow survived this far. The mother and daughter pressed a heaping basket of fruit into our arms, saying they had gathered it from the farm here. No matter how insistently we declined and said it was all right, it was no use.
“Without your help, we wouldn’t have made it here. Thanks to you, we’ve been able to start over. Thank you so much.”
Having found a new home, the mother and daughter seemed to have reclaimed their lives.
Watching them walk away, chatting quietly together, brought back memories of Geumho Station.
The regret that I should have saved more people, and the cowardly consolation that I had done the best I could at the time.
As they walked away, the child suddenly turned to look at me.
A shy smile spreading across the child’s face.
A gentle guilt washed over me.
It was more of a reward than my hypocrisy deserved.
Perhaps Jung Heewon felt what I was feeling, too.
As Jung Heewon and I watched the mother and daughter recede, she spoke.
“Congratulations on coming back to life. It took a little longer this time.”
“Isn’t that a rather understated reaction? Jihye and Gilyoung were crying and making a huge fuss.”
“Would you like me to try that, too?”
“I don’t even want that.”
I turned to her with a small laugh, but worry clouded Jung Heewon’s face.
As I hesitated over what to say, she spoke first.
“······Dokja-ssi, could the two of us talk alone for a moment?”
Jung Heewon had arrived here four days ago.
Drawing on the power of [Hell Flames Ignition], she had cleared the first floor in the shortest possible time and reached the second floor before anyone else.
And she had arrived here, at <Paradise>.
A place where one could escape the shackles of the scenarios.
Naturally, Jung Heewon had not believed those words.
On the first day, she trusted nothing. On the second, she doubted everything.
She had begun to waver on the third day, and unfortunately, I had arrived on the fourth. Jung Heewon spoke.
“Suddenly, I started wondering what the point was in continuing the ‘scenarios.’”
Jung Heewon hadn't been brainwashed or anything of the sort.
Because the very existence of <Paradise> was a sweet drug to begin with.
I smiled bitterly and asked,
“Aren't you wavering a little too soon?”
“······Maybe I've felt this way all along.”
Jung Heewon smiled bitterly, too.
“Let go! I can pay in coins! I'll pay for what I stole! I said let go!”
As we walked through the streets, we occasionally saw prisoners being dragged away by the fortress guards. Some were people who had entered the fortress with me.
Apparently, they hadn't been able to give up their old thieving habits and had helped themselves to other people's belongings.
Watching a man being dragged away, Jung Heewon said,
“It's safer here than it was in Seoul.”
“So it seems.”
“The different species don't discriminate against one another, and they help each other through difficulties. Everyone has a home to live in and a place to work.”
She sounded almost as though she were making excuses.
“You don't have to worry about your companions betraying you, or about monsters appearing at night.”
I quietly watched Jung Heewon as she strung those words together.
Jung Heewon, the Judge of Evil.
The sword I had personally nurtured since entering this world.
Jung Heewon was probably the woman who had killed more people than anyone else in our group.
The person who had been forced to ‘kill them all’ to uphold my ‘no killing.’
“We don't have to live as though the scenarios are chasing us. We don't have to have nightmares because we killed someone. And we don't have to lose anyone······ anymore.”
The hardest sword is the sword most easily broken.
Because it is the hardest, it is wielded the most.
And so it suffers the most damage, and its edge is chipped the most.
That is why it falls apart sooner than any other sword.
“If you like it here, you can stay.”
Jung Heewon's gaze wavered at my words.
Meeting her eyes, I continued.
“I also think this is a safe place.”
That was no lie.
“There is nowhere in the [Dark Castle] safer than here. No, perhaps······ it would be difficult to find somewhere this safe anywhere in the ‘scenarios.’”
I hated to admit it, but a fact was a fact.
<Paradise> really was such a place.
“Then, Dokja-ssi, are you······?”
Knowing what she was about to say, I answered quickly.
“Yes, I won't be staying here.”
“Why?”
“Because this isn't the ‘end.’”
“······You said you knew the future, Dokja-ssi.”
Once, I had spoken with Jung Heewon in the <Theatre Dungeon>.
She had asked what would happen to her in the future, and I had told her that she hadn't existed in that future. Because she was a character who hadn't been in the ‘original.’
A ‘character’ whose future I didn't know······.
“I have to continue the scenarios.”
At my words, Jung Heewon seemed to consider something for a moment.
She looked at the people of <Paradise>. People laughing, chatting, and rejoicing in the lives they had reclaimed.
“Where is this ‘end’ you have in mind, Dokja-ssi?”
“I can't tell you that.”
“Then is that ‘end’······ a better place than this?”
Because it was Jung Heewon, of all people, asking, I couldn't answer readily.
“If we don't continue the scenarios······ will everyone be unhappy?”
Could I really say that the ending I wanted for all these stories would be a more beautiful place than this <Paradise> for everyone?
Could all the characters really become happy once they reached the ‘ending’?
For a while, we gazed silently up at the sky.
It felt as though something precious had surely been there, but I had forgotten what it was.
As though waking from a brief dream, Jung Heewon spoke.
“The lord of this fortress is looking for you, Dokja-ssi.”
I nodded.
Jung Heewon and I passed through the central shopping district of <Paradise> and headed toward a small hill.

Normally, a fortress lord would naturally reside in a splendid court within the inner fortress. That had been true of the fortress in [Peace Land], too. But the lord of <Paradise> was by no means an ‘ordinary’ being.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ opens her eyes wide.]
[The constellation ‘Guardian of Youths and Travel’ expresses displeasure.]
The closer we came to the hill, the more fiercely the constellations of <Eden> reacted.
Guardian of Youths and Travel.
It seemed another archangel had begun to take notice of me. Judging by the faint pressure of presence I could feel through the indirect message, this one seemed at least on Uriel's level.
Probably on the level of <Eden>'s Three Great Angels.
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ looks forward to you going on a rampage.]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ is curious about your stigma.]
And now the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal, and the Black Flame Dragon, too.
For the first time in a while, all three channel regulars had gathered.
I was happy to see the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal, especially since he had helped us establish our nebula last time.
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ picks his nose with the Ruyi Jingu Bang.]
······Looking only at his indirect messages, it was hard to believe this guy was the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal, who had radiated such an imposing presence.
Could he actually be having someone ghostwrite his indirect messages?

······<Paradise>?

They couldn't rely solely on Kim Dokja every time.
Surely, somewhere out of sight, Kim Dokja was carrying out another hellish scenario.
“Hey! This is fucking sweet, Kim Dokja. Why didn't you start living like this ages ago?”
A sports car raced across the vast <Abyss Plains>, its engine roaring with terrifying force.

“That one's weakness appears in the 34th round. So, if you press the three little spots on its lower back······.”

Traveling with Han Sooyoung also made things easier in some ways.

Vrooooom!

[A considerable number of constellations are pleased with the spirited declaration by incarnation ‘Han Sooyoung’.]
[A considerable number of constellations approve of your approach.]
[You have acquired 20000 coins.]
Ratatatatat!
Monsters approaching from the distance burst apart under the Ferrarghini's magic bullets.

A life of endless overtime.

So······ wasn't I allowed to enjoy myself a little?

[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ covers her eyes in embarrassment.]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ considers switching channels.]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ is intoxicated by your eighth-grade edginess.]
Fuck······ Can't I enjoy myself a little?
Anyway······ things should be starting to happen in <Paradise> around now.

I couldn't remember the last time things had gone this smoothly.
At this rate, we'd clear the scenario in no time······.
[A great fate desires your death.]

But the message didn't change.
[A great fate desires your death.]
What was this?
Bewildered, I slammed on the brakes.
Han Sooyoung let out a small scream as the sudden stop threw her forward.
“······What the hell? I was just getting into it!”
“Be quiet for a second.”
I listened again. This time, the message appeared on a screen as well as sounding aloud.
[A great fate desires your death.]

I swallowed without realizing it.
Damn it. Had a ‘fate message’ ever sounded three times in the original novel?
I thought back.
Probably······ Yoo Joonghyuk in the 71st round.
Back then, Yoo Joonghyuk's name had been entered in King Yama's death register.
Damn it, what was about to happen?
Han Sooyoung pressed me for an answer.
“Why? What's going on?”
“Someone has read my ‘fate.’”
Fate. In Ways of Survival, it was a word as frightening as ‘probability.’
Strictly speaking, this too was a power that used ‘probability’ in the broader sense. But there was a reason it was given a separate name.
‘Fate’ was a power constellations exercised by using their accumulated probability cost.
“Uh, hold on. I feel like I've heard about that too······.”

“Fate······ Isn't it something like ‘Future Sight’?”

In fact, it was very different.
Reading fate wasn't simply reading ‘information about the future.’
In some ways, it was far more dangerous.
“If ‘Future Sight’ merely lets you glimpse a predictable future, ‘fate’ is a ‘power’ that forces a predictable future to happen.”
Unable to tell whether Han Sooyoung understood, I added an explanation.
“Say I step on the accelerator five seconds from now. If you looked with ‘Future Sight,’ you'd see me driving, right?”
“······Well, sure.”

“I guess you could.”

When I nodded, Han Sooyoung spoke as though something didn't add up.
“But that's a little strange.”
“What is?”
“It doesn't square with probability. From what you're saying, ‘fate’ is powerful enough to interfere with a scenario. Who the hell can force something like that to happen?”
“······Who do you think?”
In principle, this scenario had no dokkaebi interference.
That left only one group of bastards who could interfere.
Understanding immediately, Han Sooyoung replied.
“Even a constellation couldn't do that alone······.”
“The problem is, they're not alone.”
“What?”
“Only great nebulae can read ‘fate.’”

Rrrrrrumble!
Something was approaching at a terrifying speed.
A being on an entirely different level from the pathetic monsters we'd faced so far.
Han Sooyoung's face went pale.
“······Kim Dokja, what exactly did that fate message you got say?”

Just as Han Sooyoung began spewing curses and tried to get out of the car.

Instinctively, I felt he wasn't an enemy.
The moment I caught the fragrant scent of wine and the air of excessive excitement, I had an inkling of whose incarnation he was.
“······Did you come to tell me I'm going to die?”
Reeking of drunkenness, Dionysus's incarnation smiled at me with the whites of his eyes showing.
“Oh, you knew?”

I still had a favorable impression of Dionysus. On my way to the banquet hall, he'd once descended in his true body and fought for me. But in a situation like this, things were different. I spoke warily.
“Were you the ones who read my fate?”

“What does that mean?”
Dionysus's incarnation merely smiled.

“Could <Olympus> have split?”

······Already?

“But aren't I just a fledgling constellation?”

“Normally, yes. But this scenario that began on Earth is very special. Some constellations believe it's the very scenario we've been waiting for all this time. Ah, don't make that face. I didn't say that expecting you to understand.”

“Anyway, all you need to know is that this scenario is incredibly important to us. And you just had to turn up in that particular scenario.”
“I don't know what this is about, but you're saying I'm in the way.”

“Yes. You can't help being in the way. Probability affects you far less than it does other constellations. You even have overwhelming strength and growth potential compared with other incarnations. That's why some nebulae believe they must bring you into their fold, or eliminate you if they can't.”
I looked at Dionysus for a moment.
“······Why are you telling me this?”
That was what I most wanted to know.
Why was Dionysus showing me such kindness?
“Because I like your story, of course.”
Dionysus gave a hearty laugh and added,
“A few other constellations and I believe you are someone who can reach ■■.”

Jung Heewon and her companions spent the entire day investigating Paradise's ‘underground prison.’ Since there was no way for a large group to enter all at once, they decided to split up and each find a way in. The method Jung Heewon chose was, in its own way, a direct approach.

Just as the question arose, the guards all stopped in their tracks.
Strangely, tension showed on every one of their faces.

The guards were frightened, as though they'd set foot somewhere they shouldn't. Even the intimidating guard captain was afraid. Soon, a thick iron door appeared. “U-uaaagh!”

Having slipped inside among the prisoners, Jung Heewon gave a low groan as she watched them struggle frantically.

No, she couldn't see any prisoners already confined here at all.
‘How do they distribute food? What is this place?’
The utterly incomprehensible workings of this ‘underground prison.’
The prisoners who'd come in with her seemed equally bewildered.
“What are we supposed to do here by ourselves?”

Grrrrrr.

“A-aaaaaagh!”

A terror that chilled every one of her senses.

Grrrr······.
Gwaaaaaah!

She must have already been eaten by these creatures, or······.
Gaaaaaah!
Become one of them.

Reinheit's voice.

On this scale, at least around a third of its true body would be summoned.
A god's true body (眞體).
Its Status was incomparable to a mere shadow's.
“Yoo Joonghyuk! If we don't stop it now―”
“It's already too late. It's beyond anything you or I can stop.”
Simply looking up at the sky made my whole body tremble.
That was how badly it affected even me, with a constellation's Status.
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ activates strongly!]
Thanks to the ‘Fourth Wall,’ the trembling gradually subsided, but the fear remained.
The being beyond that [Great Hole] was something the current Yoo Joonghyuk and I couldn't defeat even if we joined forces.
In that helplessness, I realized.
The battle from this point onward was not one for incarnations.
Tzzzzzt!
Crrrrrrrack!
“Aaaaaaagh!”

Even incarnations with Historical-grade sponsors died the moment they saw part of the being, bleeding from all seven orifices. Yoo Joonghyuk and I retreated, protecting our huddled companions. Even his eyes were darkening. I spoke as if in defiance.

The Great Sage, Heaven's Equal, or Uriel, or even that somewhat unreliable Black Flame Dragon······.
Rrrrumble!
But even as a substantial portion of its true body crossed over, the constellations showed no response. Yoo Joonghyuk spoke through clenched teeth.
“······Perhaps this is where this life ends.”
I was baffled, too.
An Outer God had descended here, and no one was coming to help us?
[Some constellations are horrified by the Outer God's descent!]
[A considerable number of constellations express dissatisfaction with the tyranny of certain nebulae!]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ expresses hostility toward the nebula <Papyrus>.]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ bares its fangs at the nebula <Vedas>.]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is outraged by the atrocities of the nebula <Olympus>!]
Only then did I realize.
So that was it. This damned situation.
[All the constellations of the Korean Peninsula wonder which nebula you will choose.]
It had all happened because of me.
Then messages appeared, one after another.
[Many nebulae want you to inherit their Stories.]
[If you inherit one of these Stories, your existence will be forcibly bound to the corresponding nebula.]
[The nebula <Olympus> wants you to inherit ‘Carnival of Lightning.’]
[The nebula <Vedas> wants you to inherit ‘Guide of Thunder and Lightning.’]
[The nebula <Papyrus> wants you to inherit ‘Master of the Typhoon Wolf.’]
[The nebulae offer you a final choice.]
[All the constellations of the Korean Peninsula watch your choice.]
I gave a hollow laugh.
This was why I couldn't like constellations.
Carnival of Lightning.
Guide of Thunder and Lightning.
Master of the Typhoon Wolf.
They were all Stories of constellations with histories of killing their own relatives.
At the same time, Stories among the most powerful in their respective nebulae.
If I inherited one, I could probably borrow the nebulae's probability to repel the Outer God.
And Mother would die here.
Yoo Joonghyuk was looking at me.
His gaze seemed to ask what I would do, and I answered.
“······Yoo Joonghyuk. You remember the nebula we made, right? Kim Dokja’s Company.”
It wasn't simply to save Mother.
If I belonged to a nebula, everything would be over.
With my current Status, I had no way to overcome an unfair contract with them, and then I would never reach the ending of the story.
“······You still want to use that ridiculous name.”
Frowning, Yoo Joonghyuk strode to my side and drew his sword.
“I'll decide the nebula's name.”

I chuckled at the thought that perhaps this was Yoo Joonghyuk's own way of making a joke. The energy of a transcendent beside me. Although a being far beyond anything I could measure was manifesting before me, I felt strangely reassured.
Perhaps it was because, for the first time since the scenarios began, I felt we were standing on the same horizon.
I declared to the stars in the night sky.
“I won't bow to a fate handed down by bastards like you.”
I pointed my sword toward those gazes watching in breathless silence.
“I decide my own story.”
Then something like laughter sounded from somewhere.
A whisper from the universe, as if mocking the declaration of an insignificant insect.
―Unfortunate constellation.
―You will kill your father with your own hands.
―You will destroy your mother.
―And you will watch the downfall of things you hold dear.
I looked at the Outer God, still descending.
Once it finished descending, the second floor of this [Dark Castle] would be erased entirely.
This was different from what had happened in [Peace Land].
There was no prickly master here who would come running because his disciple was in danger.
Right now, there was a constellation inside me who was as sick of the word [Fate] as I was.
[Hundreds of years, and they haven't changed a bit. Fucking bastards.]
Whoooooom!
Cheok Jungyeong, possessing me, began to unleash his presence. Even I didn't know whether Cheok Jungyeong, the strongest of the Historical-grade constellations, could stand against an Outer God.
But for now, I had no choice but to trust him.

[Since when has <Hongik> become so cheap?]

[The ones I made a deal with······were not······the ‘Outer Gods.’]

[Don't tell me you made a deal with other <nebulae>?]
Cheok Jungyeong shouted in fury.
[Still obsessed with that little patch of land, and now you're betraying even your descendants?]
[You do not know. You······.]
[What is this disgraceful behavior? Where have all the creation gods gone! Why haven't they shown their faces, even with things reaching this point?]
[The creation gods······.]
But the ‘Mother of the Founder’ couldn't finish.
The next moment, I felt Cheok Jungyeong within me glare defiantly at the sky.
[Don't tell me······?]
Instead of answering, the night sky sent the following message.
[Certain nebulae declare that any constellation who helps ‘Goryeo’s First Sword’ will henceforth be considered their enemy.]
Then, as if by magic, the indirect messages in the night sky fell silent.
I occasionally heard Uriel and the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal, but they, too, seemed unable to intervene because of conflicting interests or particular circumstances.
Through my eyes, Cheok Jungyeong silently stared at that night sky.
I could feel every bit of the explosive emotion within that silence.
Cheok Jungyeong's rage and sorrow. His resentment and grief. And······even his resolve.
[You may take pride in yourself.]
Cheok Jungyeong spoke to me.
[Those who stand at the very top of this damned world are afraid of just one person: you.]
“······What use is pride when I'm about to die?”
[You will not die.]
They were only words, but to a constellation, those ‘words’ were existence itself.
As if anchoring a buoy against fate, I felt all the Stories Cheok Jungyeong had built take root in my existence.
[I will not let you die.]
As Cheok Jungyeong's Stories began to surge through my whole body, I began to hear the stories of Cheok Jungyeong scattered throughout the <Star Stream>.
A good Story could raise a being's Status merely by being read.
[You have learned of the Story ‘Dragon’s Blood.’]
[You have learned of the Story ‘Wiping Out an Army With One Sword.’]
[You have learned of the Story ‘Battlefield Slaughterer.’]
「He was born a strongman. Born with a dragon's blood in his veins.」
「“It's Cheok Jungyeong! Cheok Jungyeong is here!”」
「“He has slain 36 enemy commanders single-handedly.”」
From around the time of Cheok Jungyeong's birth to the present.
I heard histories that had not been known to the world as ‘scenarios,’ but had in fact been parts of ‘scenarios.’
[You have learned of the Story ‘Exiled from the Scenario.’]
「“He's too strong. Exile him from this scenario. Use every means at your disposal and send him to another world.”」

Watching the history flow past, I grew angry as Cheok Jungyeong had, felt sorrow as he had, and shared his joy and despair. This story was Cheok Jungyeong himself.
“Why are you going this far to help me?”

No constellation revealed the foundation of their Stories to an incarnation.
And Cheok Jungyeong wasn't even my sponsor.
[I was like you, too.]
One of Cheok Jungyeong's Stories flowed into my mind.
[You have learned of the Story ‘One Who Fights Against Fate.’]
「“Impose [Fate] on him. He must die here.”」
The drifting voices of the constellations left me stunned.
I had known that Cheok Jungyeong had been wronged.

I saw a system message appear.
[The Story ‘One Who Fights Against Fate’ begins!]
The same Story as Cheok Jungyeong's.
Cheok Jungyeong laughed.
[It was not as great as the fate you now bear. Only one nebula did that damned thing to me.]
Cheok Jungyeong spoke as he looked at the world through my eyes.
[Back then, I survived with <Hongik>'s help. But even now, I often think that I should not have accepted help from any nebula.]
Cheok Jungyeong's mighty spirit burst forth from within me.
[That is why I am helping you.]
He gripped the sword with my hand and took an opening stance with my feet.
Grrrrraaaaaah······.
The Outer God, which had almost swallowed the ‘Mother of the Founder,’ let out a roar.
Cheok Jungyeong unleashed his energy in answer.
[Unbreakable Faith] in my hand gave a fierce cry.
[A fine sword.]
The blade trembling as if responding to those words.
My magic power drained away like the contents of a jar missing its bottom, and particles of pure ether began to gather at the sword's tip.
Whiiiiine!
An Ether Blade more than ten meters long.
Even as I shuddered at that terrifying power, I struggled to stay alert.
[I will borrow it for a moment.]
Having fully possessed my body, Cheok Jungyeong began to run, gripping [Unbreakable Faith] in both hands.
An overload that even stats of 100 across the board couldn't withstand. Every joint in my body creaked, and the ground I stepped on exploded, forming a huge crater.
I brimmed with the confidence that, with power like this, I could cut through anything.
But the moment I leaped into the air and saw the enemy, a faint despair washed over me.
It was an emotion I felt because I had lived in the world of ‘humans.’
Could something that huge be killed?

The ‘Outer God’ emerging beyond the [Great Hole] exceeded imagination in sheer size alone. Its torso looked easily a kilometer in diameter. Each of the twelve legs attached to that torso was dozens of meters across.
It was that large with not even a fifth of it across yet.
If all of it crossed over, who in the world could kill it?
Perhaps reading my despair, Cheok Jungyeong laughed.
[I am Cheok Jungyeong.]
As if he meant the world to hear.
Or as if he were making a declaration to the entire <Star Stream>.
[The strongest military commander (武將) on the Korean Peninsula.]
And the sword moved.
There are moments when, even though I am doing something, I cannot tell what I am doing.
Cheok Jungyeong's swordsmanship was like that for me.
Second Form, Two Swords Cleave a Mountain (二劍斬山)
Cheok Jungyeong's second sword moved. It was not a sword for cutting down humans. Nor was it a sword for cutting down monsters.
It was, one might say, a sword for cutting through nature (自然).
The blade, more than ten meters long, slashed downward twice in succession.
There was a sound like enormous entrails bursting.
Krrrrrunch!
What poured out looked more like darkness than blood, and more like tiny printed characters (活字) than darkness. I recognized it as the story the Outer God possessed.
In the end, Outer Gods existed in the same way as constellations.
Gaaaaaaaah!
With a scream, the god's tentacle separated from its torso and fell toward the ground. It was like watching a gigantic building fall.
Shocked incarnations fled in every direction, while I was shocked in a different way.
So a human could cut through something like that.
Awe at a being born human who had surpassed humanity by an unfathomable margin.
But what followed the shock was terrible pain.
Bzzzzzzzt!
“Hah, haaah······ Gnnnnngh.”
Pain so terrible I couldn't hold back my groans.
A torrent of backlash sweeping through my entire body.
I trembled and drooled like someone being electrocuted by hundreds of thousands of volts.

The bones in the hand that had swung the sword were shattered, and my mind was shriveling like an insect crushed in a press. With great power came great responsibility, and in this world, that responsibility was called probability. But I wasn't ready to bear it yet.
[The constellation, ‘Goryeo’s First Sword’, is looking at you.]
Cheok Jungyeong was sharing the burden of probability, but my existence was still too frail to withstand his power. Cheok Jungyeong sighed.
[You are more of a weakling than I thought! Since you had become a constellation, I thought you could withstand at least this much······.]
I wanted to tell him he was just absurdly strong, but I couldn't get the words out.
“Gah! Haaah! Haaah! Haaah!”
Instead of food, I violently vomited streams of electricity.
Only after sitting on the ground and gasping for several minutes did I barely manage to escape the probability storm.
When I lifted my head, I saw the scene Cheok Jungyeong had created.
A sword that cut mountains.
With that attack, Cheok Jungyeong had shredded two of the twelve legs. In other words, he had cut down two mountains.
But more than ten mountains still remained, and the creature's torso remained as well. Cheok Jungyeong's voice was grim.
[······Not enough. For the first time, I may have to use the third sword or go beyond it.]
“There's something beyond the third sword?”
[I have not used it before······ But judging by your current condition, I doubt I can even use the third sword.]
I gritted my teeth.
The Outer God was being summoned faster.
The scales of probability should already have been nearly balanced, yet it kept summoning its true body into this world. That last blow seemed to have made it furious.
“Couldn't we negotiate with it?”

“They're gods too, so······.”
Realizing what I really meant, Cheok Jungyeong cut me off.
[If you are trying to save your mother, give up. Even the ‘Mother of the Founder’ has had her shadow devoured. Your mother's soul will have scattered long ago.]
