Why did it feel as though people who didn't even know my face knew me better?
“Kim Dokja. What are you doing?”
A foot nudged me, and I groaned as I got up.
Yoo Joonghyuk stood there shirtless, drenched in sweat.
It looked as though he'd just come back from the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's grueling training.
“······I was just thinking for a minute.”
“You're slacking off.”
“I need to slack off right now. I'm a patient.”
It sounded like an excuse, but it was true.
I still hadn't fully recovered from the injuries caused by the ‘Exile Penalty’. Needlessly challenging the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had also done a lot to delay my recovery.
At least my proficiency in ‘Lamarck’s Giraffe’ was improving, and I was steadily consuming Story fragments, so my recovery shouldn't take too long.
I looked at the man and woman diligently practicing martial arts in the courtyard in front of the manor and asked,
“How are those two doing?”

There, an equally sweat-drenched Jang Hayoung was sparring with a miserable-looking Han Myungoh. The Breaking the Sky Sword Master, acting as their supervisor, barked away as it pointed out flaws in their moves.
“That girl has considerable talent. She's using a peculiar attribute to learn martial arts remarkably quickly.”
“Not a girl. He's a guy.”
“Sometimes I wonder where the hell your eyes are.”
What was this idiot talking about? He really was a guy, you know?
It said so in the original novel, too.
Just as I was about to snap back, Yoo Joonghyuk continued.
“More importantly, what happened with the constellations?”
“······I'm thinking it over.”
Before I knew it, a whole week had passed since I'd received Persephone's message.
[The constellation, ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’, has invited you to the ‘Gourmet Association (美食協)’.]
[In one week, the Gourmet Association's festival will be held at Oro Castle (五輅城) in the Dark Dimension.]
[By tonight, please decide whether you will depart.]
An invitation to the Gourmet Association.
I'd expected something like this might happen someday, but it had come far sooner than I'd anticipated.
The Gourmet Association (美食協).
Just as the name suggested, a gathering of constellations with discerning palates who loved fine food.
At first glance, it might seem similar to the ‘Constellation Banquet’, but the reality was entirely different.
While the ‘Constellation Banquet’ was an official gathering, the ‘Gourmet Association’ was unofficial, and the intensity of the events held there was on another level altogether.
[The constellation, ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’, is worried about you.]
Above all, Uriel wasn't in the Gourmet Association.
[The constellation, ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’, is curious about your choice.]
The Great Sage, Heaven's Equal wouldn't be there either, nor would the Secretive Plotter.
The Abyssal Black Flame Dragon······ had that one been there? I couldn't quite remember.

In any case, the atmosphere there wouldn't be entirely friendly toward me, the way it had been at the ‘Constellation Banquet’. And in the <Star Stream>, nothing was more dangerous than going somewhere full of unfriendly constellations.
Perhaps reading my expression, Yoo Joonghyuk asked,
“Are you scared?”
“Of course not.”

If something as trivial as that could keep me from attending the ‘Gourmet Association’, I could never have made it this far in the first place. I silently watched Jang Hayoung and Han Myungoh spar. Han Myungoh, taking blow after blow to the head, screamed as though adding a rhythm to the silence. Watching the same scene, Yoo Joonghyuk continued.
“It's because of this place.”
According to Persephone's message, the Gourmet Association's festival was exactly one week away.
And as luck would have it, that date coincided exactly with the ‘Martial Arts Tournament’.
In other words, I wouldn't be in the <First Murim> on the day the Martial Arts Tournament scenario began.
If something unexpected were to happen······.
“Go and come back, Kim Dokja.”
At Yoo Joonghyuk's firm words, I reflexively raised my head.
“······Will you be all right?”
“The scenario we're facing right now is the ‘Demon King Selection’, not the ‘Martial Arts Tournament’.”
I'd been thinking that all along, but hearing Yoo Joonghyuk say it filled me with a strange mixture of relief and pride.
“You······ really have become a decent human being. At least you won't die for a while.”
Yoo Joonghyuk ignored me and continued.
“The most we can get from the Martial Arts Tournament is the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword]. But getting the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] doesn't mean we can win the ‘Demon King Selection’.”
Yoo Joonghyuk was right.
Winning the ‘Murim Tournament’ certainly wouldn't mean we could win the ‘Demon King Selection’.
“That's why you have to go to the ‘Gourmet Association’. Our nebula needs companions. If you go to the Gourmet Association, you might be able to find allies.”
I understood what he meant.
Go to the Gourmet Association and sweet-talk some useful constellations into coming along.
But one word caught my attention.
“······Our nebula?”
“Didn't you say last time that you were going to make one?”
“Kim Dokja’s Company?”
“If it really has a name that lousy, I'll quit immediately.”
Yoo Joonghyuk, turning his head away with a fierce scowl.
A chuckle escaped me.
[The constellation, ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’, wipes away tears of emotion with a handkerchief.]
I could never have imagined this when he first grabbed me by the collar.
To think that ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ and I had truly become companions.
In any case, now that Yoo Joonghyuk had gone so far as to say all that, it would be ridiculous for me to hesitate.
I got to my feet and said,
“I'll be back.”
That night, I welcomed the Gourmet Association's guide, who came flying through a portal.
Dressed like a cowboy straight out of a Western, the guide arrived driving a small carriage drawn by a black horse.
The guide seemed to be one of the retainers bound to the master of Oro Castle.
Stepping down from the carriage, the guide bowed politely to me before speaking.
[Are you the constellation ‘Demon King of Salvation’-nim?]
“I am.”
[Please board the carriage. The journey will be rather long, so you are welcome to get some sleep.]
The guide showed no particular surprise or other notable reaction upon seeing me.
So someone who served as a guide for the Gourmet Association wouldn't be surprised by the likes of the ‘Demon King of Salvation’?
On the way to the driver's seat, the guide turned to ask,
[Other passengers will be joining us along the way. Would that be all right?]
“Oh, that's fine.”
Other passengers······ who could they be?
I wanted to ask, but the guide immediately set the carriage in motion, and I missed my chance.
Whatever it was made of, the carriage was quite spacious and comfortable inside. There wasn't the slightest jolting; I couldn't even feel the inertia that would tell me we were moving.
Perfect.
I could read some ‘Ways of Survival’ on the way.
For the next several hours, I read ‘Ways of Survival’ without stopping.
Perhaps it had been days rather than hours. Since I couldn't tell exactly how fast the carriage was moving, it was difficult for me to gauge the time.
「······And so, as the Yoo Joonghyuk of the 15th round lay dying, he thought, ‘Bad luck.’」
「······Ending his 19th round like that, Yoo Joonghyuk thought, ‘Next time.’」
「······As his 25th life came to an end, Yoo Joonghyuk muttered, “Next time, I'm really going.”」
······I took back what I'd said about him becoming a decent human being.
This bastard was still a sunfish, even in the First Revised Version.
Was he going to die all the same, whether I helped him or not?
As I skimmed past Yoo Joonghyuk's deaths, I didn't forget to look for the information I needed.
There wasn't much about the Gourmet Association.

Yoo Joonghyuk had visited the ‘Gourmet Association’ in one of his very late rounds, but he'd gone there to beat those bastards to death, not to make peace. That section was mostly riddled with “Aaaaargh!”
「Flying Fox said, “Constellations are all the worst. But the lunatics in the Gourmet Association are the worst of the worst.”」
Besides, there was hardly anything favorable to be found.
The more I read, the less certain I was that going to the Gourmet Association was the right thing to do.
In any case, I kept reading ‘Ways of Survival’.
「Yoo Joonghyuk thought, ‘I wish that guy had come with me.’」
If there was a difference in how the original and the revised version felt to read, it was when passages like this appeared.
Traces of the moments when I'd intervened in the original novel.
Whenever such passages appeared, I paid especially close attention.
They were among the few scenes that mentioned the story of the ‘3rd round’, which was absent from the revised version.
「‘But I have to do it this way. After all, that guy, too, said this was the right path.’」
······The right path? What was he talking about?
[It is mealtime. It is nothing special, but I have prepared a modest meal.]
“Thank you.”
Whenever the carriage stopped at intervals along the way, the guide brought me a meal.
It seemed to be a sort of in-flight meal.
It looked like jamón, a fine cured ham, and gave off a wonderfully fragrant aroma.
Of course, it wasn't real ham.
[The Last Gladiator of Planet Selegedon]
As expected of something provided by the Gourmet Association, even the in-flight meal was a Story.
Judging by the concentration of the Story I could sense, it seemed quite powerful······.
I sank the fork the guide had provided deep into the smooth flesh of the ham.
But at that moment, part of the Story's contents flowed into my mind.
―S-spare me. Please, spare me······!

A city being hideously torn apart amid the constellations' rampage. Incarnations crushed beneath immense pressure, their bodies bursting. A gladiator opposing them, stripped of all dignity and dying······.

The torn bodies of incarnations poured whole into the mouths of constellations laughing like demons. The final scene of a world that had already vanished. The incarnations' screams and despair gathered together, lingering at the tip of my nose.
I stared down at the ham for a moment, then quietly set down my fork.
[······Is the food not to your liking?]
“I'm not very hungry right now.”
I said it with a nonchalant smile.
[My apologies. It seems I failed to consider your preferences, constellation-nim. Some different food······.]
“No, I'll eat what I brought.”
Looking apologetic, the guide took the plate away and withdrew to the driver's seat.
Only when the guide was completely out of sight did I finally manage to let my expression relax.
I felt as though I was about to retch.
Suddenly, a passage from ‘Ways of Survival’ that I'd just read flashed through my mind.
「“It's a nightmare of a place for incarnations.”」
Once again, I realized just where I was going.
And who the beings I was dealing with were.
Like an idiot, I'd been acting as though I were going on a picnic.
I fiddled with a few Story fragments in my pocket.

Compared with the Stories those bastards ate, the Stories abandoned on the ‘Story Horizon’ were almost colorless and odorless. Unremarkable scraps of Stories about ordinary second- and third-rate incarnations who had lived ordinary lives and died.
There was a reason the Gourmet Association had discarded every one of them.
Absorbing those Story fragments through my hand with [Lamarck’s Giraffe], I quietly closed my eyes.
For some reason, I felt as though I would have a nightmare.
The journey continued for several days, and I used the spare time to tend to a few things I'd been unable to put in order.
[Coins held : 1,252,353 C]
First, I checked my coins, something I'd been too preoccupied to do for a while. When I looked, I found I'd accumulated a truly enormous sum.
1.25 million coins. That was enough to buy the [Great Demon's Eyes].
But Anna Croft had already bought that. I had a better skill, so I didn't particularly need it anyway······.
I considered how to use the remaining coins.

Raising my overall stats wouldn't be a bad idea, but once overall stats exceeded an average of 100, the returns actually began to drop sharply. From that point on, investing in skills was much better value for money than investing in overall stats.
Of course, overall stats could still prove useful when built up to overwhelming levels.
First, I'd have to persuade the ‘Fourth Wall’ to let me check my Attributes Window sometime soon.
[It seems the other passengers will be boarding now. Would that be all right?]
I'd been so deep in thought that I hadn't even noticed the carriage had stopped.
“Yes, that's fine.”
As I answered, the door on the left side of the carriage opened.
A little tense, I peered through the opening at the people about to join me.
After all, there was a good chance a constellation would be boarding.
“Ah! We've been waiting forever. Why are you so late?”
[My apologies. The road was somewhat rougher than expected······.]
The voice sounded strangely familiar.
A girl's high, thin voice with a Russian accent.
I could see three people in total through the opening.
[There is already a passenger aboard. I hope you all enjoy the journey.]
Whether that was fortunate or unfortunate, I couldn't sense the Status of a constellation.
In other words, they were all incarnations.
A woman approached with a gentle smile and boarded the carriage first.
“Please excuse me.”
The woman's khaki-brown hair fluttered in the breeze as she greeted me politely.
The moment she raised her head, I reflexively spoke.
“Selena Kim?”
Selena Kim.
She'd once attended the ‘Constellation Banquet’ as the representative of the United States.
Perhaps because my face had changed, the woman tilted her head for a moment before exclaiming.
“Do you remember who I am?”
“Of course! Kim Dokja! It's been a while! Were you invited, too?”
“That's how things worked out.”
As I shook hands with a delighted Selena Kim, I looked over the rest of her group.
Next to enter was a small girl with twin ponytails.
“Who are you······ huh?”
Sure enough, I'd seen this one before, too.
The Russian kid I'd met at the ‘Constellation Banquet’.
Her name······ what was it again? I remembered she'd had a nickname like Little Red Kid or something.
Ignoring the girl opening and closing her mouth at me, I turned to inspect the last person.
But at that moment, goosebumps broke out all down my spine.
“This is our first time meeting in person.”
That calm, unhurried voice held a depth that made the speaker's intentions impossible to fathom.
I knew this person well.
Someone counted alongside the Supreme King Yoo Joonghyuk as one of the strongest incarnations in ‘Ways of Survival’.
In fact, I'd even met this person before.
“I once saw you in a dream. It was so long ago that I wonder if you remember. I believe you told me then that we should meet again······.”
I remembered clearly.
During the ‘Green Zone’ scenario, I'd eaten a Specter's Stone and seen her.
“I remember.”
“Let me introduce myself properly. A pleasure to meet you, Kim Dokja. No······ ‘Demon King of Salvation’.”
Between strands of fluttering blond hair, a swirling yellow demon eye (魔眼) smiled quietly.
It was an exceptionally beautiful smile, but I couldn't take it at face value. I knew better than anyone the sinister ideology concealed behind it.
“I'm Anna Croft.”
The Prophet of Asgard.
Anna Croft, the leader of ‘Zarathustra’, was there.
Gourmet Association
Anna Croft remained silent throughout the journey to Oro Castle.
She occasionally gave a strange smile when our eyes met, but she never initiated a conversation.
It would have been nice to at least read her thoughts, but my understanding of Anna Croft was too low to activate stage 2 of [Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint].
Well, I hadn't particularly liked Anna Croft in the original novel either.
I wouldn't have enough fingers on both hands just to count the times Yoo Joonghyuk had been killed or betrayed by her.
With both Anna Croft and me keeping quiet, the atmosphere in the carriage rapidly grew awkward, leaving poor Selena Kim sweating buckets.
“······That's how we ended up coming together. Asgard's incarnations were invited too.”
Too kind by nature to endure this atmosphere, Selena Kim kept explaining things no one had asked about. Still, it was good for me, since I was getting all sorts of information.
“I see. Do all three of you belong to Asgard?”
“Yes. Anna arranged it.”
“You chose a good nebula.”
“Ahaha, we just happened to get lucky. Thanks to that, we get to enjoy a privilege like this. The other incarnations weren't even invited······.”

Selena Kim seemed a little excited. An invitation from the Gourmet Association did mean something different from an invitation to the Constellation Banquet. If the Constellation Banquet was a gathering of all the nobility, the Gourmet Association was more like a salon for the upper aristocracy.
But a privilege (好事), huh.
Even once Selena Kim arrived there, I doubted she would still be able to think that.
“Iris, why are you so quiet? You said you wanted to see Dokja-ssi again.”
“Blin (влин)! When did I ever!”
“Honestly······ Ever since the last banquet, it's been Dokja-nim this, Dokja-nim that, hasn't it? You finally get to see him again, so try talking to him.”
Iris's face turned bright red at Selena Kim's words, which sounded like teasing.
After stealing glances at me to gauge my reaction, Iris cautiously spoke.
“Um, you are the Demon King of Salvation······ -nim, right?”
For a moment, I wondered whether this really was the same cheeky brat from back then, but I decided to be polite too.
“I am.”
“······D-does being here with us make you uncomfortable?”
“Why would you think that?”
“We're just ordinary incarnations. And you, Demon King of Salvation-nim, are······.”
Beside her, Selena Kim's expression was changing too.
She seemed to have remembered that I was a ‘constellation’, different from them—a fact she'd briefly forgotten in her delight at seeing me.
The gap between a ‘Narrative-grade constellation’ and an ordinary ‘incarnation’ was as vast as the distance between heaven and earth.
Another constellation would probably have spouted some line like, “You insignificant insects have finally realized your place.” Of course, I wouldn't.
“It's fine. I was an incarnation once too.”
At my words, I saw Selena Kim let out a sigh of relief.
Encouraged, Iris spoke again.
“Um, then······ may I ask you a question?”
“Go ahead.”
“Do you have an incarnation under a sponsorship contract?”
“Why do you ask?”
Selena gave the hesitant Iris a pointed look.
“Iris. You already have a constellation sponsor chosen for you, don't you?”
“I-I was just asking! I'm curious!”
Watching Iris twist her twin tails around her fingers and turn her head sharply away reminded me of Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung back on Earth.
I wondered if those two were doing all right······.
I spoke, doing my best to hide how much I missed them.
“My incarnation is on the Korean Peninsula.”
Iris's expression changed at my words.
“Oh, is it that little girl······?”
I nodded.
It seemed rumors about Shin Yoosung had spread elsewhere too.
Since the constellations loved gossip, they'd probably already told their own incarnations.
That was when Anna Croft spoke.
“Have you considered changing incarnations?”
Startled, Selena Kim and Iris glanced at Anna Croft.
Anna Croft continued.
“There are many excellent incarnations under the nebula <Asgard>. Many talented ones too. Iris here is one of them.”
It was an unexpected proposal.
Why was Anna Croft suddenly making an offer like this?
Perhaps they were talking about me in Asgard too.
I hadn't formally founded a ‘nebula’ yet, after all.
“Are you asking me to join <Asgard>?”

“Not necessarily. There are many excellent incarnations under Asgard, so I'm merely suggesting that choosing one of them wouldn't be a bad idea. A sponsor can withdraw a sponsorship contract at any time anyway, can't they?”
Iris, who had briefly looked dejected, gazed at me with sparkling eyes.
I answered with an expressionless face.
“I have no intention of canceling my sponsorship contract.”
“You must be quite fond of that girl. ‘Shin Yoosung’, was it?”
When I didn't answer, I saw deep disappointment spread across Iris's face.
The change in her emotions was strong enough for my skill to detect despite my very low understanding of her.
Then Anna Croft said something strange.
“Suppose that incarnation were to die suddenly······.”
An inscrutable smile rested on Anna Croft's lips.

“Don't look so surprised. I'm only giving an example. It could happen, couldn't it? An unforeseen accident, or an incarnation dying in a sudden disaster······. Such things happen all the time. Would you still have no intention of changing incarnations even if that happened?”
“An unforeseen accident, you say?”
“Yes, an unforeseen accident. An unforeseen accident that simply happened by chance.”
I stared quietly at Anna Croft.
Shin Yoosung dying······.
I'd never considered it.
“That won't happen as long as I'm alive.”
“You never know. No one knows when or how [Fate] might take effect.”
The air suddenly trembled.
The air around us took on an ominous hue, and the entire carriage shuddered.
Iris's and Selena Kim's faces were stiffening.
Goosebumps rose along the two incarnations' forearms as they looked at me in terror.
Woooooo.
I hadn't wanted to do this.
I hadn't wanted to frighten innocent incarnations as well.
But just now, Anna Croft had crossed a line she should never have crossed.
[If that happens.]
Tzzzzzzzt!
Sparks of probability began to fly as I used my True Voice.
[The constellations of the nebula <Asgard> express their concern to you.]
[The constellations of the nebula <Asgard> issue warnings to you!]
The Asgard constellations' indirect messages reached my ears. But I didn't stop using my True Voice.
[If that happens, I will destroy every world that brought about that [Fate].]
Booooom!

The shock of my erupting Status blew out all the carriage windows at once. The startled coachman was looking back at us. Even the composed Anna Croft looked faintly shocked. It seemed she hadn't known exactly how much ‘Status’ I possessed.
Before long, the carriage stopped, and we heard the guide's voice.
[We have arrived at Oro Castle.]
I grinned at the three of them, still frozen in place, and said,
“Let's get out.”
Once we stepped out of the carriage, we were led straight to Oro Castle.
Oro Castle (五輅城).
One of the Gourmet Association's principal bases scattered across all dimensions, this fortress was personally owned by one of the association's executives.
If I remembered correctly, its owner was······ probably one of the Demon Realm's 72 demon kings. Was it ‘Immeasurable Austerity’?
[These guests have been granted permission to enter.]
[Confirmed. Please come in.]
Once we entered the castle, the interior looked more modern than medieval. It reminded me of the lobby of a luxury hotel. Here and there, I spotted constellations in the form of symbolic bodies.
[Several constellations take notice of your presence.]
Our guide led us to a waiting room in a corner of the first-floor lobby.
Apparently no one else had arrived yet, since the waiting room held only me and the Asgard trio.
[Please wait here for a moment. There are still more incarnations due to arrive······ Ah, since the ‘Demon King of Salvation’-nim is a constellation, we will prepare a separate waiting room for you.]
“No, that's all right. I'll stay here.”
The guide gave me a puzzled look, but soon disappeared, apparently satisfied.
Honestly, I still felt more comfortable here.
I needed some time to prepare myself too.
As expected, panels hung on the waiting room walls for our viewing pleasure. Scenes from lower-level scenarios taking place across the dimensions even now······.
“Um, about earlier······.”
It was Selena Kim who spoke to me.
She could easily have been wary of me after what had happened in the carriage, but sure enough, the character descriptions in Ways of Survival never got anything wrong. I answered with a faint smile.
“It's all right. I went a little too far.”
Only then did Selena Kim's expression soften a little.
“No, we were terribly rude. I apologize, Demon King of Salvation.”
Her words were much more formal than before.
I hadn't meant to elicit that kind of apology, and it left me feeling uneasy.

Selena Kim hadn't done anything wrong. She was one of the few characters in all of Ways of Survival I thought well of. The one I disliked was that shameless woman standing in the corner, watching how things unfolded.
Just then, the waiting room door opened, and another guide appeared.
[Would the incarnations of Asgard please follow me.]
It seemed Asgard's constellations wanted to see them.
Selena Kim and Iris gave slight bows and left first.
Anna Croft, however, didn't immediately leave the room. She was looking at me.
“You have too many constellations as enemies.”
“That isn't your concern.”
Anna Croft's brow creased slightly at my firm answer.

Despite what had happened earlier, Anna Croft didn't seem particularly intimidated. She was merely an incarnation, but she had a contract with an entire nebula. <Asgard>'s highest-ranking incarnations were probably protecting her from my Status.
“I'm giving you sincere advice as a comrade working toward the same goal. Whether you like it or not, now is the time to cooperate with other constellations.”
The same goal······.
“Well, I don't know what your goal is, so I can't answer that.”
“Protecting this world. Isn't that what you're fighting for too?”

Instead of answering, I quietly studied the panels on the waiting room walls. Videos of incarnations being brutally torn apart by the appearance of disasters or constellations. When I didn't respond, Anna Croft walked past me.
At that moment, I spoke.
“We'll have to wait and see whether this world is worth protecting.”
Anna Croft's expression stiffened at my casually dropped remark.
She glanced anxiously between me and the guide walking ahead, then spoke with a short sigh.
“······I hope we have another opportunity to talk later.”
After she hurried away, I was alone in the waiting room.
Left by myself, I quietly gathered my thoughts.
I recalled the Gourmet Association constellations mentioned in Ways of Survival and made a mental list of those I might be able to persuade.
I didn't forget to consider their traits, likes, and dislikes either.
I'd been lucky at the Constellation Banquet, but there was no guarantee I would be again.
In terms of high society, this Gourmet Association gathering was my proper debut.
The impression I made here and the things I said would change the course of the scenarios I would shape from now on.
Then the waiting room door burst open.
I thought it might be another guide, but this time an unexpected figure was waiting for me.
Just as I was about to say something in alarm, the visitor spoke first.
[It's been a while, Kim Dokja. I've been waiting a long time.]
The moment I heard the bright tone of that True Voice, I realized who it was.
Honestly, the Queen of the Underworld was far too mischievous.
I asked with a sigh.
“······Why on earth do you look like that?”
Persephone smiled faintly.
[Why? Don't you like it? The archangel from next door has been telling everyone that this is your type.]
“That is a complete misunderstanding.”
Persephone let out a seemingly disappointed sound.
For the record, Persephone had taken on Yoo Joonghyuk's appearance.
At least she wasn't wearing a cheongsam. Thank goodness for that.
[Then how about this?]
Before I could finish trying to stop her, Persephone changed her appearance again.
As her clothing transformed into a cheongsam, I thought she was turning into Yoo Sangah again. But this time, to my surprise, it was someone I'd never expected.
“What on earth······.”
At that radiant little smile, I felt my face growing hot even though I knew it was Persephone. She had taken on the appearance of ‘the Punisher’, whom I'd seen in the Demon Realm not long ago.
[You seemed unable to take your eyes off her back then. Is this your type after all?]
At the sight of the snow-white bare skin exposed through the dress's side slit, I reflexively closed my eyes and shouted.
“······Please stop teasing me!”
[Hehe, you're so entertaining.]
Laughing like a child, Persephone transformed once more.
This time, she looked like Yoo Sangah.
A neat office outfit instead of a cheongsam or garter belt.
Seeing her like that reminded me of my days at Mino Soft, stirring complicated feelings. Yoo Sangah had always dressed that way when she came over to talk to me.
I wondered if Yoo Sangah-ssi was doing well.
I was a little worried to hear she was traveling with Han Sooyoung······ but she was ‘Yoo Sangah-ssi’, after all. I believed she'd be all right.
Persephone spoke with a bright smile.
[Come with me. I'm here to fetch you.]
I nodded and followed Persephone.
The moment I left the waiting room, several constellations' gazes bore down on me, making me a little tense. I also saw constellations whispering as they watched me with Persephone.
Somehow, I felt like a noblewoman's young attendant.
Before long, Persephone and I reached the enormous elevator in the center of the lobby.
The Gourmet Association's festival would probably take place on the fortress's top floor.
The doors of the elevator, which resembled a giant crystal ball, opened, and Persephone and I stepped inside.
With a tilting sensation, my body grew a little heavier, and the scenery of a dark dimension unfolded beyond the transparent crystal walls.
Beyond the dimension's horizon, the vast world of the <Star Stream> was revealing itself.
[You look very excited.]
“I'm more nervous than excited.”
Persephone smiled as though she understood how I felt.
[I'm glad you're alive. You were an incarnation the last time I saw you, and now you've become a constellation in your own right.]
“I'm still only a novice. I'm not sure I really belong here.”
I'd meant it as a modest remark, but whatever Persephone had heard in it, her expression had stiffened slightly.
[Do you think I lack even that much standing in the ‘Gourmet Association’? That I'd struggle to bring along a single new member?]
“That isn't what I meant······.”
[I'm joking.]
“Please stop teasing me.”
[Who knows how promising a constellation you might become? Think of this as an early investment. It's something you'll have to experience someday too.]
I'd wondered about it before, but I had no idea why this queen treated me so well.
All she'd asked in return for taking the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint to Tartarus in the Underworld was that I attend this ‘Gourmet Association’ gathering.
She probably knew too.
That even this condition of ‘attending the Gourmet Association’ would ultimately benefit me, rather than her. She had, in effect, arranged a proper debut for me now that I'd become a constellation.
Persephone's obsidian eyes sparkled.
[What level is your Status at now? Surely not Narrative-grade.]
Apparently, the other constellations hadn't learned that I was ‘Narrative-grade’. I thought for a moment before answering.
“We might see each other on the second floor at the next ‘Constellation Banquet’.”
Persephone's eyes widened.
She must have assumed my Status was Historical-grade at best.
It was rather satisfying to see the Queen of the Underworld flustered.
But deep concern soon entered her gaze.
[There will be constellations who envy you.]
[Some constellations will try to draw you over to their side.]
“I'm expecting that.”
I was prepared for it.
None of the constellations I would meet from now on would be easy to deal with.
Whether they envied me or wanted me on their side.
Either way, they would be equally dangerous.
[But most constellations won't take much interest in you.]
“······Pardon?”

[Until now, you've probably only visited places where the ‘Korean Peninsula scenarios’ have considerable influence, so you may not have noticed······ But don't forget that this is the ‘Gourmet Association’.]
The Gourmet Association.
A grand banquet where the high-ranking constellations of the <Star Stream> gathered.
Suddenly, Persephone's smile felt frightening.
[I won't play your nanny as I did at the ‘Constellation Banquet’. This time, I want to see you rise through your own strength.]
The elevator doors opened with a chime, and as though putting her words into practice, Persephone disappeared into the banquet hall. Left alone, I hesitantly stepped out of the elevator.
[Several constellations show curiosity about you.]
Several constellations turned their eyes on me the moment I stepped out, but their interest soon vanished.
That was a relief, if anything. Too much attention would have made it harder to move around.
There were no constellations in ‘symbolic bodies’ like those in the first-floor lobby.
All of them humanoid, or mimicking the forms of creatures from other worlds.
Not a single constellation here bothered with petty concerns about [probability].

Several constellations occupying the center of the noisy banquet hall looked just as I'd read about them in Ways of Survival. The first to catch my eye was a man in Viking attire at the center of the hall. It would have been stranger not to recognize him after seeing the enormous hammer strapped to his back.
[The best first-generation Story is obviously ‘Dragon Eating the Hammer’!]
‘Thursday's Thunder’, a constellation of the nebula <Asgard>, was raising his booming voice. A woman across from him answered.
[What are you talking about? The best is obviously ‘Children of Dawn’. It has the highest rating too.]
A goddess in a snow-white dress that looked embroidered with starlight.
If I remembered correctly, that woman was probably the ‘Morning Star Goddess’, a constellation of the nebula <Guardian Tree>.
Apparently, another argument had broken out over which Story was the best.

I'd heard that they were forever arguing over which Story was best, and the scene was exactly as described in Ways of Survival. Watching high-ranking constellations rarely seen on the Korean Peninsula stroll about so casually really brought home what kind of place this was.
Even the powerful ‘Persephone’ was merely an ordinary constellation in the ‘Gourmet Association’.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ cheers you on.]
My only consolation was that, thankfully, the ‘channel’ worked here.
Right. I couldn't let a place like this intimidate me.
I edged toward the groups at the center of the ‘Gourmet Association’ gathering and tried speaking to one of the constellations lingering nearby.
“Excuse me······.”
But no one turned to look at me.
Constellations acting as though I didn't exist here.
I gathered my courage and tapped the shoulder of the constellation beside me.
“Excuse me.”
This time, there was a response.
But after glancing back at me, the constellation shoved my shoulder as though picking a fight, then walked back to the center of the banquet hall.
「Kim Dokja knew this feeling very well.」
The feeling that I alone was isolated from the entire world.
Suddenly, all those constellations' voices felt distant.
We were clearly in the same place, yet they were somewhere else.
Only then did I understand the ‘indifference’ Persephone had spoken of.
The ‘Gourmet Association’ had built a sturdy wall of its own, keeping newcomers like me from casually setting foot inside.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ looks at you with pity.]
······But I couldn't give up like this.
I had to find a way to create an opening.
I looked farther afield, examining the edges of the Gourmet Association gathering.

Apart from the constellations chatting in the center of the banquet hall, I could see others wandering about alone. They were also members of the ‘Gourmet Association’, so they must have been powerful constellations too.
At the edge of the banquet hall, countless panels covered the walls, incomparably larger than those in the waiting room.
Videos of ‘scenarios’ taking place all over the world.
Looking closely, I found a small display in one corner showing the moment I'd become the ‘Demon King of Salvation’.
But no constellation was watching it.
Even the ‘Korean Peninsula scenarios’ I'd experienced were merely one passing story here.
The panel beside it showed a live feed of the Korean Peninsula.
It seemed to be Bihyung's channel.
On the screen, a self-proclaimed beautiful girl with bobbed hair was spouting nonsense.
―That bastard Kim Dokja is definitely having the time of his life right now.
The familiar voice made me chuckle.
Han Sooyoung, you wouldn't be saying that crap if you knew where I was right now.
―Hey, you're collecting those Abyssal Stones, right? Make sure you gather plenty. If things go wrong later, we'll at least have to use those.
―······Did Dokja-ssi really ask you to do this?
―I told you he did!
Watching Han Sooyoung and Yoo Sangah bicker on the screen filled me with longing. I felt that watching any longer would only make me miserable, so I turned to the next panel.
That panel showed a typical ‘mass-produced Story’.
The Story was titled 「Legend of the Legendary Return from Another World」.

The title alone reeked of third-rate fiction, and the plot was just as predictable: a returnee from another world saved the world, and everyone became happy. Still, it was watchable. There was something about it that resembled Ways of Survival······ Somehow, even the protagonist spoke like Yoo Joonghyuk. After I'd given the Story a quick look, a message appeared.
[Would you like to submit a star rating?]
Oh, so this was a system for rating each Story.
I cautiously placed my hand on the ‘star rating’ field beside the work.
Just then, I heard someone's voice.
[This is my favorite Story.]
I turned around to find an old man standing there.
I gave a slight bow and answered.
“It was an interesting story.”
[Hoho, wasn't it? You're a fellow with a discerning eye.]
In truth, the Story didn't particularly suit the ‘Gourmet Association’ as I knew it.
The association's constellations didn't like mass-produced Stories like this.
The constellations of the ‘Gourmet Association’ were refined sorts who recoiled and started retching whenever concepts like the ‘Ninth Circle’ or ‘sword masters’ appeared.
Yet 「Legend of the Legendary Return from Another World」 featured both.
“Are you the one who submitted this Story?”
[I am. Hahaha. I submit it every year. I want even one more person to know about it. It's so good, such an entertaining Story, but I just don't know how to put it into words.]
“I understand how you feel.”
Somehow, I was even glad to meet him.

Back when I was avidly reading Ways of Survival, I'd posted recommendations for it on every community site I visited. Mostly, I'd just gotten shitloads of abuse······ Anyway, this old man seemed to be in a similar situation.
The old man added with a sigh.
[No matter how much I recommend it, the fellows here only scoff. Young things, and already so fussy······ All they ever do is go on about first-generation Stories.]
The more he said, the more surprising his remarks became.
The ‘Gourmet Association’ did have its stodgy side.
In the <Star Stream>, that tendency grew stronger the higher one's position.
Then I heard some passing constellations mutter.
[That Steady Person is back again.]
[Tsk, tsk. They say he's gone senile and can't even recognize a good Story anymore······.]
······Steady Person?
Judging by the old man's fury beside me, it seemed to be his nickname.
Steady Person. I thought there'd been a constellation with a similar nickname in Ways of Survival······.
[Piss off, you bastards! I didn't put this Story out for you lot to stuff your faces with!]
Just then, with a beep, I saw the star rating beside 「Legend of the Legendary Return from Another World」 change.
The already low rating had fallen further.
It was obvious who had done it.
[Th-those bastards!]
It was what people called ‘rating bombing’.
The old man shouted at the top of his lungs at the constellations as they walked away, sneering.
Somehow, I felt I understood how he felt. I placed my hand on the rating field and said,
“I don't think this Story is bad enough to deserve a score like that.”
A beep, and the star rating rising.
The shouting old man turned to look at me.

“Honestly, I don't really understand why Stories need scores in the first place. Every Story has value in its own way. A story that's merely entertainment to one person can be salvation to someone else.”
The old man looked startled at my words.
His lips moved a few times before he murmured with what seemed to be sincere admiration.
[You're unlike the young constellations these days······ To have such fine principles······.]
“It's nothing.”
Anyone who'd endured their childhood through a story like Ways of Survival would come to think as I did. His mood apparently much improved, the old man gave an easy chuckle.
[Well, well. It seems I've found a good fellow to talk to. What's your modifier? With everything going on, I haven't even asked.]
This seemed to be going rather well, didn't it?
I grinned and said,
[I am the Demon King of Salvation.]
At my words, a variety of expressions crossed the old man's face.
[······Demon King of Salvation······?]
It was difficult to read his precise emotions from the strange folds of his wrinkles.

At first, the old man looked unimpressed. Then he seemed faintly surprised, wore a curiously angry expression, and finally appeared admiring. More precisely, all those emotions were contained in a single expression.
[I see. So you're the one······ Hoho, I see.]
He spoke as though he knew me.
Persephone had said the Gourmet Association's constellations wouldn't know much about someone like me, so I hadn't expected anything······ Was I better known than I'd thought?
“May I ask your modifier?”
Instead of answering my question, the old man gave an inscrutable smile.
[Do you like the coat I made?]
“······Pardon?”
[The coat you're wearing.]
Without thinking, I looked down at my white coat.
[Infinite Dimension Space Coat].
It was the coat I'd received as a reward after defeating Myung Ilsang some time ago.
And the name of the constellation who had made this coat was······.
“······Mass Production Maker?”
The old man grinned at the shock in my voice.
[That's what they call me, yes.]
Watching him point proudly at himself with his thumb left me a little overwhelmed.
Mass Production Maker.
Whenever people listed the constellations capable of exerting the greatest influence over the <Star Stream>'s scenarios, he was always mentioned.
A formidable presence thanks to his close connections with countless nebulas and the Bureau alone, even if his personal combat strength could hardly be called top-tier.
To make matters worse, while clearing the fifth scenario, I'd killed the returnee Myung Ilsang, the ‘Mass Production Maker’'s incarnation.
[Hoho, no need to look like that. I'm not going to eat you.]
The ‘Mass Production Maker’ seemed to have already guessed what I was about to say.
[I know what you're thinking. Don't worry about it. It's a common occurrence in the <Star Stream>. I wasn't particularly interested in the fellow to begin with.]
[He had no grit, a weak will, and always chose the easy path. I never much liked him.]
I felt a complicated mixture of emotions.
Relief that the ‘Mass Production Maker’ wasn't particularly bothered by it, and disillusionment that, in the end, even a constellation like him regarded incarnations as nothing more than tools······.
I spoke, trying to sound composed.
“Thank you.”
[Don't thank me for that. However worthless he was, he was my incarnation. ······Anyway, I enjoyed the story you made.]
“The story I made?”
[Yes. You have a remarkable knack for taking scenarios in unexpected directions and turning them into utter chaos. Thanks to you, I had plenty to watch for a while. I gave it five stars too.]
I couldn't tell whether it was praise or sophisticated mockery, but I thanked him for now.
[This must be your first time here. Who introduced you?]
“The Queen of the Underworld.”
A curious gleam crossed the Mass Production Maker's eyes.
[That old hag······ Hehe, she's finally gone and done it. Bringing a newcomer like you here at a time like this······.]
I thought I had some idea what he meant, but deliberately played dumb.
“Is something happening in the Gourmet Association?”

[Something's always happening. More importantly, did that old hag abandon a first-time newcomer and go off to attend to her own business? Tsk, tsk······ Those Olympus bastards, honestly. Come along. I'll make a few introductions.]
Things were going better than I'd expected.
I trailed closely behind the ‘Mass Production Maker’ as he walked ahead, looking all around me.
I couldn't let all the fascinating sights make me forget why I'd come.
Ultimately, I was here to recruit constellations who would help with the ‘Demon King Selection’.
Let's see.
The best constellation to approach first would be······.
[You can tell who that drunkard over there is just by looking at him, can't you? That's ‘Thor’. That uptight-looking girl over there is ‘Vakarine’······.]

Every time the ‘Mass Production Maker’ carelessly called out a constellation's true name, a chill ran through my chest. A constellation's true name had the power to draw their attention. The problem was that you never knew whether that attention would be friendly or furious. I'd occasionally called constellations such as Persephone by their true names too, but never so recklessly······.
[I'm not particularly close to them, so don't expect much of an introduction. They recoil whenever I so much as approach.]
Indeed, ‘Thursday's Thunder’ and the ‘Morning Star Goddess’ seemed to be edging away simply because the ‘Mass Production Maker’ had appeared.
I could more or less guess why.
[Tsk, tsk. Those bastards can't even recognize a good Story······.]

Anyway, I could feel a marked difference in the constellations' reactions simply from accompanying the ‘Mass Production Maker’. The ease with which we'd entered the center of the banquet hall, where I'd struggled even to set foot earlier, was proof enough.
But at this rate, everyone would run away before I could even speak to them······.
Oh, come to think of it, ‘Asmodeus’ was also a member of the Gourmet Association······ Where was he?
[Looks like the main event is about to begin.]
The ‘Mass Production Maker’, who'd been doing all the talking, beamed and pulled me along by my sleeve. The moment we sat at a nearby table, an attendant brought us food.
[Eyes of the Ninth Circle Great Sage Merbatos]

After prodding the food a little, I cautiously put down my fork. Several constellations around me snickered in my direction. They seemed to be mocking me for not being able to eat even that, or perhaps despising me for touching such lowly food at all.
Of course, regardless of those looks, the ‘Mass Production Maker’ was busy spearing the eyeballs and munching away.
[The flavor's passable. Look, that one over there is today's host.]
Lights came on over the prepared stage, and the host appeared.
Her face looked familiar. She was the constellation who'd shoved past me in the hall earlier.
A young woman with a cute face, wearing a voluminous Gothic lace dress.
[Hello, members of the Gourmet Association~ I'm ‘Euphrosyne’, your host for today!]
Hearing her name, I thought I knew who she was too.
Euphrosyne, the ‘Goddess of Joy and Celebration’.
She was a constellation of the nebula <Olympus>.
Amid the thunderous applause, several constellations forgot their dignity and shouted.
[Ooooh, Miss Euph! Over here, over here!]
Specifically, the ‘Mass Production Maker’ beside me did.
A memory of Ways of Survival suddenly came to me.
There had definitely been a regression round in the original novel where ‘Euphrosyne’ hosted the ‘Gourmet Association’ gathering.
And back then, Yoo Joonghyuk······.
[Thank you all for taking time out of your busy schedules to attend! And my heartfelt thanks to ‘Immeasurable Austerity’-nim, the owner of Oro Castle, for lending us this venue!]
Had probably killed her.

[We have two main events prepared for today. But first, I'd like to introduce a special guest. Some of you constellations may have heard of our guest! Today's guest comes from a planet that's recently become one of the hottest places around!]
With a sense of foreboding, I watched fireworks go off in a corner of the stage.
[Please give a round of applause for the Prophet from Earth, ‘Anna Croft’!]
The noisy constellations all fell silent at once.
I saw Anna Croft stride up the steps to the main stage.
I thought I was beginning to understand why Anna Croft had come to the Gourmet Association at this time.
Sure enough, she was a woman I couldn't like even if I tried.
Surveying the audience with her characteristically composed gaze, Anna Croft greeted them with a radiant smile.
“It is a pleasure to meet you, constellations of the ‘Gourmet Association’. I am Anna Croft, an incarnation of the nebula <Asgard>.”
She maintained her dignity, but the moment she spoke, the constellations were already frowning.
[The ‘Gourmet Association’ has really gone downhill. Prey speaking onstage.]
[The <Star Stream> really has fallen on dark times lately.]
This was the ‘Gourmet Association’.
A banquet of constellations who savored carefully selected ‘Stories’.
It went without saying that the main ingredient of a ‘Story’ was a ‘fresh incarnation’.
Anna Croft must have come here knowing that.
“Despite my shortcomings, I have been entrusted with hosting the first ‘event’.”
That made her all the more frightening.
[I don't know what prey could possibly prepare.]
[Drag her down at once!]
As the atmosphere grew heated, it was Euphrosyne who quickly tried to intervene.
[Now, now, everyone. Don't get so worked up······ Wouldn't it be worth at least hearing what this delectable prey has to say? Surely we gourmets have that much patience?]
When Euphrosyne smiled and turned on her charms, the agitated constellations briefly faltered. The shrewd Anna Croft didn't miss that opening.
“Recently, the <Star Stream> has been flooded with predictable Stories.”
At that provocative opening, the grumbling constellations' attention instantly focused on her.
Anna Croft continued.
“Returnees, reincarnators, sword masters, Ninth Circle archmages······ Even ‘Prophets’ like myself. All formulaic Stories in which one ‘starts out with greater power than others’······.”
With a faint smile, Anna Croft went on.
“A flood of Stories made solely for cheap thrills and satisfying payback—that is the reality of today's <Star Stream>.”
A curious gleam entered the constellations' eyes.
As though they found it remarkable that prey would say such things.
But Anna Croft was only getting started.
“It was not always like this. At least, things were different when ‘first-generation Stories’ were popular.”
As though spellbound, the constellations waited for her next words.

“In those days, constellations loved Stories. Because they were stories worthy of that love. Dokkaebis gave Stories themes, and constellations explored form and aesthetics within them. Back then, ‘Stories’ firmly belonged to the realm of ‘art’.”
She really was a frightening woman. To say such things so readily as an incarnation.
At Anna Croft's words, each constellation seemed lost in a different memory.
I could see Persephone among them.
They were all constellations who had lived through and endured that era.
[Interesting. So you're saying the Story you have can satisfy our palates?]
The speaker was a demon king leaning against a wall in a corner of the hall.
Despite the decidedly provocative remark, Anna Croft smiled without losing her composure.
“Yes. Today, I intend to give you back the ‘first generation’ you have lost.”
The constellations' expressions changed completely.
They all looked as though they couldn't believe their ears.

“A Story without the sword masters or Ninth Circle archmages you so dislike. A Story with a theme that comes to fruition through blood and sweat, tears and effort alone. I have come here today to present you with such a Story.”
The constellations' reactions to Anna Croft's shocking declaration varied wildly.

Some constellations shouted at the top of their lungs, demanding how a mere incarnation dared spout such nonsense. Others were interested and wanted to hear what she meant. Some were skeptical. The ‘Mass Production Maker’ beside me was one of them.
[······What foolish talk. Even the ‘Gourmet Association’ couldn't possibly find Stories like that entertaining anymore. Don't you agree?]
“I agree.”
There were certainly excellent first-generation Stories.
But times had changed.
Constellations already accustomed to sensational narratives wouldn't now be moved by a Story imitating the first generation.
But······ there was no way ‘Anna Croft’ didn't know that as well.
She was the most capable incarnation in all of Ways of Survival.
I recalled the passages of Ways of Survival that described her actions.
In the original novel, Anna Croft had never held an event like this at the ‘Gourmet Association’.
But she must have done something similar somewhere.
That was when someone grabbed my shoulder.
“Demon King of Salvation-nim!”
I turned to find a woman with a familiar face.
“Selena Kim?”
“Please, please save Iris!”
A tremor transmitted through the hand on my shoulder.
That kind, composed Selena Kim was wearing an expression like this?
“If this goes on, Iris will······!”
A certain scene from Ways of Survival flashed through my mind.
「“Anna, why would you go this far······? There was no need for this!”
“It was necessary.”
“This is wrong. This is······ Those incarnations don't know anything! How could you do this!”
“This too is for the sake of saving humanity. Don't forget, Selena. We've been thrown into a pack of wild beasts that could devour us at any moment.”」
That hadn't happened in this regression round.
But the original novel had already undergone its first revision.
In other words, it wouldn't be strange for something from another round to happen in this one.
Especially since the story of the third round had been deleted from the First Revised Version······.
“Selena Kim. Please be specific. What's going on?”
Before Selena Kim could even continue, I heard the furious voices of the surrounding constellations.
[How dare a mere incarnation······!]
Terrifying gazes were pouring down on Selena Kim and me.
Rrrrrrumble.
Frozen like a statue, Selena Kim was turning deathly pale.
Perhaps to protect me, the ‘Mass Production Maker’ raised his Status in response, and dazzling sparks of probability flew around Selena Kim.
This ‘central hall’, a place for ‘constellations’ alone.
For a moment, I'd forgotten that this was the ‘Gourmet Association’.

Her mouth opening and closing like a frightened goldfish's, Selena Kim was dragged away by the attendants who appeared next. Unable to resist even once, she could only look toward the stage with resentment in her eyes.
I still didn't know exactly what Selena Kim had tried to tell me, or whether it was the same thing I'd read in Ways of Survival.
But one thing was certain. That her reason for coming to me was connected to what Anna Croft was doing onstage right now.
I looked back at the stage with a troubled gaze. Anna Croft looked down at us with expressionless eyes and continued speaking.
“The Story I will give you is the ‘Bracelet Expedition’.”
The constellations murmured.
[······The Bracelet Expedition?]
“Yes.”
[Is it perhaps a parody of the first-generation Story ‘Demon Emperor of the Bracelet’?]
Demon Emperor of the Bracelet.

That Story, also mentioned in the original Ways of Survival, was considered an older classic than ‘Dragon Eating the Hammer’ or ‘Children of the Morning Star’. A traditional adventure Story older than the first generation—closer to the zeroth generation, really.
A typical expedition narrative in which a fifteen-member ‘Bracelet Expedition’ set out to burn the ‘bracelet’ that was the source of the calamity.
Listening, the ‘Mass Production Maker’ muttered in disbelief.
[Hah······ She's going to tell that tedious Story?]
But Anna Croft continued, paying no heed to the constellations' reactions.
“Allow me to introduce the ‘Bracelet Expedition’ that will lead this Story.”
When Anna Croft clapped her hands, a large panel appeared behind her.
An immense panel covering an entire wall of the hall.
On it, a vast forest stretched out, and fifteen incarnations were huddled together, talking.
―······Where the hell are we?
―What Anna-nim told us must be true, right?
―Everyone, keep your heads on straight. As long as we prove ourselves here, we can get top-class constellation sponsors too.
I thought I could more or less guess what she'd said to entice them.
Looking closely, I saw Iris among them, looking frightened.
I see.
So that was why Selena Kim······.
It seemed she'd even obtained a dokkaebi's authorization already, since a system message soon appeared.
[Sub-scenario ― ‘Bracelet Expedition’ is beginning.]
[A new Story can be acquired upon success or failure in this scenario.]
●A total of 15 incarnations will participate in this scenario.
●All incarnations must cooperate to reach the [Volcano] at the center of the [Hunting Grounds].
●The expedition possesses the [Absolute Bracelet]. The scenario will be completed only when this bracelet is thrown into the [Volcano]'s lava and destroyed.
●An incarnation who completes the scenario may ask the ‘Gourmet Association’ to grant one wish.
Judging by the contents alone, it sounded exactly like a certain novel I knew.
The Story ‘Demon Emperor of the Bracelet’ itself seemed to be an homage to that novel in the first place······.
The scenario messages continued.
●Numerous [evil spirits] of the Demon Emperor inhabit the hunting grounds. If the expedition is wiped out by [evil spirits], the scenario will fail.
●If the [Absolute Bracelet] is not destroyed within the time limit, the scenario will fail.
[Oh······ so this is the scenario you've prepared. Interesting.]
Several constellations reacted favorably.
To me, it was a shoddily assembled scenario, but there was certainly a flavor within it that the constellations could appreciate.
A revisiting of an old Story.
Anna Croft was peddling nostalgia to the constellations of the ‘Gourmet Association’.
But there was no way the fastidious constellations of the ‘Gourmet Association’ would be satisfied with so little.
[······But something is missing. So what are we supposed to do? Surely you don't mean for us to just sit here watching that boring game.]
“As you can see on the panel, there are ‘incarnations’ awaiting your choice.”
[Are you asking us to become their ‘constellation sponsors’?]
“Of course, you may choose to do so. Though it would not be very entertaining.”
[You mean······?]
“Honored constellations, you may participate directly in this ‘scenario’ and taste those fresh incarnations.”
As Anna Croft spoke, additional scenario messages appeared.
●A total of 15 [evil spirits] will appear in this scenario.
●All constellations of the ‘Gourmet Association’ may apply for [evil spirit] roles on a first-come, first-served basis.
The moment I read the scenario messages, a chill ran through me.
This was what ‘Anna Croft’ had been aiming for from the start.
A scenario that would satisfy the constellations' desires while bringing them the flavor of the first generation.
I could feel a quiet fervor among the constellations. An exhilaration mingled with excitement, completely different from their earlier murmuring.
Even the ‘Mass Production Maker’ looked intrigued.
One of the constellations asked.
[What do you gain from this scenario?]
“Nothing. I merely hope that the honored constellations can enjoy themselves without a care.”
That shameless smile made me grit my teeth.
There was no way she really wanted nothing.
She was probably just saying that to strengthen her own position.
[The constellations of the Gourmet Association feel favorably toward ‘Anna Croft’.]
Anna Croft's scheming surpassed even the constellations' cruelty.
Someone who would sacrifice anything to achieve her ends.
Yoo Joonghyuk hadn't been stabbed in the back more than ten times for nothing.
“Then we will begin the scenario in 1 minute. Any constellations who wish to apply, please sign the selection window.”
As Anna Croft spoke, a selection window appeared before my eyes as well.
[Would you like to participate in this scenario?]
[Current applicants: 2/15]
An opportunity to devour the subjects of a Story at the very place where that Story was being created.
The number of applicants was rising rapidly.
[Current applicants: 5/15]
I reminded myself once again why I had come here.
Here, I had to secure allies for the ‘Demon King Selection’.
To do that, participating in this scenario would be a good idea.
Sharing a Story with the other constellations would allow me to grow closer to them.
[Hahaha, we'll be eating a ‘work of art’ for a change.]
[Aren't you looking forward to it?]
Damn it, perhaps it was time to admit it.
That I had become the same kind of being as the ‘constellations’ I hated so much.
[Current applicants: 9/15]
Just then, I heard a “Baat” beside my ear.
Then, a small panel coming into view.
It was a screen Biyoo had brought up herself, one only I could see.
―The 857th Martial Arts Tournament will now begin!
There was Yoo Joonghyuk, participating in the ‘Martial Arts Tournament Scenario’.

He seemed to have grown considerably stronger in the meantime. With minimal movements, Yoo Joonghyuk was defeating his opponents one after another. Quietly watching those composed movements, I thought what I always did.
What would Yoo Joonghyuk have done?
At that moment, Yoo Joonghyuk looked this way, and our eyes met.

This dark, dingy medicine had a horrific history (前史): the Blood Demon School was said to have made it long ago by refining the souls of as many as 1000 martial masters.

A cursed pill that could open the Ren and Du meridians (任督兩脈) and grant supreme internal power with a single dose, but would turn whoever took it into a madman steeped in demonic qi because of the souls' curse.
Setting aside Yoo Joonghyuk, who had been out of his mind to begin with, Jang Hayoung would certainly die if they took this.

Grinding three [Great Return Pills] together with the [Demon Spirit Bead] and taking them would let you avoid the curse.
Easy to say.

“Biyoo.”
I called Biyoo and opened the [Dokkaebi Bag].

[Recommended Products List]
●Great Return Pill ― 200,000 C / Stock: 5
200,000 coins, huh.

Tzzzzzzt!

A constellation I had once quarreled with at the ‘Gourmet Association’.
The one I had left buried in debt, who had consequently been dragged away by the enforcement division.
Grrrrrooooar!
A lizard standing well over thirty meters tall.

Tzzzzzzt!

Graaaaaah!
